output: Prescription Drug Monitoring Act of 2016 This bill requires each state-licensed prescription drug monitoring program (PDMP) to provide each patient receiving controlled substances a proactive notification when the treatment is over and a quarterly de-identified data set is provided. The bill also requires the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to share data on PDMP use and misuse. The bill sets forth requirements for the sharing of PDMP data among states. DOJ may withhold grant funds from a state that fails to comply.

Promoting Financial Literacy and Economic Opportunity Act of 2015 Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business-related tax credit for 50% of the amount paid to a nonprofit organization for programs that promote economic and financial literacy. Limits the amount of such credit to 20 for profit organizations.

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require that accrediting agencies and accrediting associations apply procedures through the accrediting process, including evaluation, interim sanction, and withdrawal or termination of accrediting proceedings, that comply with due process, including the right to:  (1) adequate specification of accrediting requirements; (2) written notice of deficiencies at the institution of higher education or program being examined and a reasonable time period, expressly set forth in the notice, to correct the deficiencies; (3) advance notice of and an opportunity for a hearing by any such institution before its decision making body prior to the agency's final consideration of imposition of an adverse action; (4) appeal any adverse action by the agency against any such institution to an independent and impartial arbitration panel appointed jointly by the agency and the institution and conducted at the institution's location; (5) appeal, at a minimum, the adequacy of the evidence supporting the adverse action decision, the adequacy of the agency's compliance with its own policies and procedures, and the extent to which the decision of the agency was tainted by bias or prejudice of any agent or official of the agency; (6) representation by counsel for any such institution; (7) an arbitration panel decision that may

Contributions Legally Interdicted from Noncitizens To Our Nonprofits Act of 2016 or the CLINTON Act of 2016 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to prohibit a federal official organization from treating a tax-exempt organization as knowingly or willingly accepting a contribution from a person connected to a foreign government.  The bill defines "person connected to a foreign government" as: (1) any department, agency, or instrumentality of a foreign government, (2) any public international organization, (3) any officer or employee of such organization, (4) any individual who was serving or has served as President or Vice-President, or (5) any person belonging to a ruling or royal family by virtue of sanguinity or marriage.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to deny any tax benefits to a political organization that receives excess campaign contributions during a taxable year. 
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to reduce the third-class mailage rates for a candidate for election as a Member of, or Delegate or Resident Commissioner to, the United States House of Representatives.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that the determination of whether any pre-effective date electric output facility bond is a private activity bond (or an industrial development bond under the Internal Revenue Code) shall be made without regard to any permissible competitive actions taken by the issuer. Defines "pre-effective date electric output facility bond" as any bond issued as part of an issue if: (1) such bond was issued before the enactment of this Act; (2) any portion of the proceeds of such issuance was used for an electric output facility; and (3) such bond was not, as of such date of enactment, a private activity bond (or an industrial development bond under the Internal Revenue Code).

Amends the Code to revise the definition of "private activity bond" to include any bond issued as part of an issue any of the proceeds of which are to be used for electric output facilities other than small distribution property. Defines "small distribution property" as any output facility, including functionally related and subordinate property, that operates at 69 kilovolts or less.

Amends the Code to revise the definition of "qualified refunding bond" to mean any bond (or a bond which is part of a series of refundings) issued to refund a pre-

United States-Afghanistan Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) Act of 2011 - Directs the President to seek to enter into a bilateral status of forces agreement with Afghanistan to: (1) prohibit the permanent basing or military presence of U.S. Armed Forces in Afghanistan; (2) provide a date, no later than one year after the date on which the agreement is entered into with Afghanistan, for the safe and orderly redeployment of all members of the U.S. Armed Forces, Department of Defense civilian employees, and contractors working for the Department of Defense; and (3) establish that the temporary presence of U.S. Armed Forces in Afghanistan is at the request and invitation of the sovereign government of Afghanistan.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the President should submit the status of forces agreement to the Senate for its advice and consent to ratification as a treaty or alternatively the President should request statutory authorization for the status of forces agreement by Congress.

Requires the President to submit to the House Select Committee on Intelligence and the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence a copy of the status of forces agreement.

Return of Talent Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish the Return of Talent Program to permit eligible aliens to temporarily return to their country of citizenship in order to make a material contribution to that country if the country is engaged in post-conflict reconstruction activities, for a period not exceeding 24 months, unless an exception is granted under specified circumstances.

Allows the Secretary to extend the period for such temporary return by requiring that circumstances warrant such extension.

Authorizes the Secretary to provide for the permanent resident (PR) and continuous resident (CR) status of certain immigrant participants in the Program.

Directs the Secretary to submit a report describing: (1) the countries of citizenship of the participants in the Program; (2) the post-conflict reconstruction efforts that benefitted, or were made possible, through Program participation; and (3) any other information the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

Authorizes appropriations.

Strategic Withdrawal of Agencies for Meaningful Placement Act of 2018 or SWAMP Act This bill repeals the requirement that the head of a federal agency's headquarters be located in the Washington metropolitan area.  No new construction or major renovations may be undertaken, or lease agreements entered into or renewed, for the headquarters of the Department of Defense (DOD) or the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) after such date of enactment, except as otherwise expressly provided by law.  The General Services Administration (GSA) must establish a process for the solicitation of the relocation of the headquarters of an agency.  GSA may use the proceeds from the sale of any federal building or land to offset the cost of relocating the headquarters of an agency.  No additional funds are authorized to carry out this bill.

Minority Business Development Improvements Act of 2010 - Directs the Director of the Minority Business Development Agency to establish the Minority Business Development Program to assist qualified minority businesses.

Authorizes the Director to certify a qualified minority business as a qualified minority business for the Program term of five years and to authorize appropriations.

Authorizes the Director to enter into agreements with the U.S. Government and any department, agency, or officer having procurement powers for purposes of providing for the fulfillment of procurement contracts and providing opportunities for qualified minority businesses with regard to such contracts.

Authorizes appropriations.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to make a grant to an eligible university to establish the Center for the Study of Women and Workplace Policy. Requires the Center to compile and analyze data and data sets on the difference between the earnings of men and women, including the Panel Study of Income Dynamic housed at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, and to identify factors which affect differences in earnings. Requires the Center to disseminate its findings annually to the public and maintain a website to serve as a clearinghouse for the data and findings of relevant recent studies. Requires the Center to publish one best practices guide, as follows: (1) for businesses; and (2) for families. Requires the Center to publish a best practices guide for families, containing information about: (1) the policies of various employers relating to workplace equity, retaining women in the workplace, and promoting a family-friendly workplace; (2) strategies for addressing inequity in the workplace; and (3) recent findings on inequity in the workplace. Directs the Center to update, revise, and publish a subsequent edition of each of its best practices guides once every two years after its initial publication.

Small Business Access to Capital Act of 2009 - Amends the Small Business Act to: (1) increase the maximum amount of business loans eligible for under the Small Business Administration (SBA) Business Development Program (BDP) to 90% of the collateral of a small business; (2) allow a small business to refinance existing indebtedness if the amount of the financing is not more than 80% of the value of the collateral; (3) allow a small business to include the refinancing of existing indebtedness in its low-cost financing program; (4) allow a small business to enter into a marketing, management, and technical assistance grant program; (5) allow a small business to enter into a microloan program; (6) allow a small business to enter into a maximum loan amount of 50,450% of the collateral of a new markets venture capital company; and (7) limit the amount of leverage that a new markets venture capital company may engage in.

Amends the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 to require the Secretary of the Treasury to provide FY2010 appropriations for the National Institutes of Health (NIH) programs that are part of the Business Financing Program.

Census Improvement Act - Prohibits participation in the Planning Partnership Program for the 2010 census of population from being allowed in the case of: (1) an organization indicted for a violation under federal or state law relating to an election for federal or state office; or (2) an organization employing applicable individuals.

Requires the following two-thirds vote in either chamber of Congress to repeal or otherwise limit confidentiality of certain information concerning an individual.

Requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to report to Congress on the questions proposed to be included in the upcoming American Community Survey and the 2010 census of population.

Prohibits the officer, employee, or other person referred to in this Act from seeking answers to any questions relating to any household or any member of such household from any person who is not a member of such household.

Electronic Campaign Disclosure Act of 1998 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to establish a public Internet site with the following features:  (1) any person filing a report required by this Act to be posted directly on the site; (2) any member of the public to obtain the reports posted on the site (together with any other information the Commission may make available through the site) at any time; (3) the report to be submitted in a manner that permits the posting of the report on the site immediately upon receipt; and (4) the Commission to permit each person to file a report electronically. 
Requires the Commission to:  (1) require each person to file a report electronically during an election cycle if the aggregate amount of contributions or expenditures reported by the person during the cycle exceeds $25,000; and (2) provide for one or more methods (other than a signature on the report being filed) for verification of reports filed. 
Requires the Commission to:  (1) provide for one or more methods (other than a signature on the report being filed) for verification of reports filed; and (2) provide for the

Directs the Secretary of the Air Force, in its capacity as a federal corporation and a volunteer civilian auxiliary of the Air Force, to administer the Civil Air Patrol (CAF) as a federally chartered corporation and a volunteer civilian auxiliary of the Air Force.  Requires the Secretary to appoint a National Board of Directors for the CAF.  Requires the Chairman of the National Board to be the senior active duty Air Force officer.  Permits the Board to appoint officers and employees on active duty and civilian Department of the Air Force staff to serve on the National Board.  Prohibits the Board from exceeding a minority of the Board.  Authorizes the Chief of Staff of the Air Force to assign officers and enlisted members of the Air Force to serve on the staff of the National Board.  Prohibits the Chief of Staff from receiving any compensation, other than the regular military compensation to which the officer or member is otherwise entitled, as a result of the appointment or assignment.  Authorizes the Executive Director and National Board of Directors to use such CAF employees and volunteer Civil Air Patrol members as their Executive and National Board of Directors.  Prohibits a member of the CAF or an employee of the CAF from receiving any Federal compensation or Federal benefits as a result

Children's Bicycle Helmet Safety Act of 1993 - Authorizes the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to make grants to States, State political subdivisions, and nonprofit organizations for programs that require or encourage individuals under age 16 to wear approved bicycle helmets. 
Requires the Administrator to allow grantees to use wide discretion in designing programs that effectively promote increased bicycle helmet use. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) grant purposes; (2) standards; (3) the interim and final standards; (4) the Consumer Product Safety Act's application to the proceeding under this Act; and (5) failure to meet standards. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Electronic Employment Verification Reauthorization Act of 2008 - Amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to extend through 11 years the employment eligibility verification program for certain federal employees.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to terminate a pilot program at the end of the 11-year period beginning on the first day the pilot program is in effect.

Revises the program to require: (1) a federal contractor to participate in the E-Verify Program; and (2) the Secretary to verify the employment eligibility of all federal employees not later than 10 days after notifying the Secretary of Homeland Security of such election.

Requires the Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to establish a rural demonstration program for small businesses to verify the employment eligibility of their newly hired employees.

Selected Reserve Home Loan Equity Act - Amends Federal housing law to permanently increase the authorized amount of the housing loan guarantee furnished to a member of the Selected Reserve.

Revises the loan fee table to specify that the initial loan fee shall be the loan amount (not the loan fee) minus the interest rate reduction.

Revises the loan assumption to require the member's loan to be made on the basis of the member's first $100,000 of loan equity, with an average of $100,000 of equity remaining after the member's first $100,000 of loan equity is repaid.

Revises the loan interest rate reduction to: (1) reduce the rate of the loan interest rate reduction to 0.5% for refinancing purposes, and (2) reduce the rate of the loan interest rate reduction to 0.5% for purposes of the loan assumption.

New Aid for Trustworthy, Affordable Drugs Act (NAFTA Drugs Act) - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to enter into agreements with other countries to harmonize regulatory requirements for drugs that may be imported or exported from any such country into any such country. Directs the USTR to carry out such requirements in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS). Authorizes the USTR to enter into a harmonization agreement only if such Representative determines that: (1) the proposed agreement provides for regulatory standards for drugs that are consistent with the requirements of this Act; (2) the proposed agreement provides for the display of a seal on the labeling of the drugs involved, which is to indicate that the drugs meet the standards of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States, and approval of such a seal by the appropriate health authority in any such country before the display of such seal in that country, to ensure that the seal complies with the uniform standards of the agreement; and (3) the proposed agreement provides that a drug may not be imported into a country from another country unless the labeling of the drug bears a seal described in this Act. Directs the USTR to implement such requirements in consultation

Older and Disabled Americans Criminal Protection Act of 1998 - Authorizes a shared housing referral service to request the Attorney General to conduct a search and exchange of records regarding any applicant for participation in a shared housing arrangement as a service provider resident by:  (1) submitting fingerprints and a written statement authorizing the service to request such search and exchange; and (2) making the submission of such information not more than seven days after completing acquiring the information.  Requires the Attorney General to provide any such information identified by the search and exchange to the appropriate State or local governmental agency authorized to receive such information.  Authorizes the use of such information only for determining the suitability of the applicant for shared housing arrangement as a service provider resident.  Sets forth criminal penalties for the unauthorized use of such information.

Fish and Wildlife Officer Retirement System - Amends Federal law to provide for the civil service retirement system (CSRS) for law enforcement officers of the United States Fish and Wildlife Service of the Department of the Interior.

Assault Weapons Prohibition Act of 1993 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit the possession or transfer of an assault weapon or an assault weapon after the 90-day effective date of this Act. 
Defines an "assault weapon" as a rifle, shotgun, or handgun which:  (1) is neither intended to be used in a manner similar to a semiautomatic rifle nor intended to be used with a silencer; (2) is not intended to be used with a bayonet, grenade launcher, flash suppressor, or folding stock; (3) has a detachable magazine capacity of 10 or more rounds of ammunition; and (4) from which a firearm or device could be assembled if such parts were possessed or controlled by one person. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to recommend modifications to the definition of an "assault weapon." 
Directs the Attorney General to investigate and study the effect of this Act and the amendments made by this Act on violent and drug-related crime. 
Directs the Attorney General to evaluate the recreational and other noncriminal uses of an assault weapon.

Open Our Democracy Act of 2014 - Requires a candidate for Member of the House of Representatives to be elected to such office pursuant to: (1) a single open primary election; (2) a single general election; or (3) a combination of the two. Requires each state to hold a single open primary election for each office of Member of the House in which the candidate, regardless of the candidate's political party preference, shall appear on a single ballot. Requires each voter in the state who is eligible to vote in elections for federal office in the congressional district involved to cast a ballot in the election, regardless of the voter's political party preference.  Provides that, at the time a candidate for the office of Member of the House files to run for such office, the candidate shall have the option of declaring a political party preference, and the preference chosen shall accompany the candidate's name on the ballot for the election for such office.  Provides that, if a candidate does not declare such a preference, the designation "No Party Preference" shall accompany the candidate's name on the ballot for the election for such office. Natural Gas Reserve Act of 2001 - Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to authorize the Secretary of Energy to establish a Natural Gas Reserve. Defines "natural gas" as specified in the Act.Authorizes the Secretary to: (1) purchase, contract for, lease, or otherwise acquire, in whole or in part, storage and related facilities and storage services; (2) use, lease, maintain, sell, or otherwise dispose of such storage and related facilities; (3) acquire by purchase, exchange (including exchange of petroleum products from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve or received as royalty from Federal lands), lease, or otherwise, natural gas for storage in the Reserve; (4) store natural gas in facilities not owned by the United States; and (5) sell, exchange, or otherwise dispose of natural gas from the Reserve, including to maintain the quality or quantity of the natural gas in the Reserve or to maintain the operational capability of the Reserve.Requires the Secretary to determine procedures governing the release of natural gas from the Reserve.Requires the Secretary to transmit to Congress a plan describing: (1) the acquisition of storage and related facilities or services for the Reserve; (2) the acquisition of natural gas for storage in the Reserve; (3) the

Hospital Price Disclosure Act of 2005 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a hospital to report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services, for each procedure or drug selected, and an ambulatory surgical center, the frequency with which the hospital performed the procedure or administered the drug in an inpatient setting, or the average and median of the hospital's and ambulatory surgical center's price charged for such procedure or drug during such quarter.

Directs the Secretary to post such data on the public Internet site of the Department of Health and Human Services.

Requires the Secretary to promptly post, on the Department's official public Internet site, the data reported.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) promptly post, on the Department's official public Internet site, the data reported; and (2) periodically update the data.

Authorizes the Secretary to impose a civil monetary penalty for each knowing violation of the provisions of this Act.

Radio Broadcasting Preservation Act of 2000 - Modifies the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) rules authorizing the operation of low-power FM radio stations to require minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels to: (1) prescribe minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels; and (2) prohibit any applicant from obtaining a low-power FM license if the applicant has engaged in any manner in the unlicensed operation of any station in violation of the Communications Act of 1934. Authorizes the FCC to: (1) eliminate or reduce the minimum distance separations required by this Act; or (2) extend the eligibility for low-power FM stations beyond the organizations and entities as proposed in the Act. Requires the FCC to conduct an experimental program to test whether low-power FM radio stations will result in harmful interference to existing FM stations if such stations are not subject to the minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels. Requires the FCC to select an independent testing entity to conduct field tests in the stations under the program. Requires the FCC to report to specified congressional committees on the program and field tests and to the Committee on Commerce of the House and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate not later than February 1, 2001

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) permit the use of qualified zone academy bonds for construction of qualified zone schools; (2) allow a tax credit for the use of such bonds; (3) allow a credit to the holder of such a bond and to the entity holding it; and (4) allow a credit to the entity holding the bond and to the entity holding it's holder.

Turkish Human Rights Act - Prohibits assistance under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (Fao 1996) from being provided for the Government of Turkey unless the Secretary of State determines that there has been significant progress in: (1) the Government permits domestic and international human rights monitoring organizations to monitor and report on the human rights situation within its territory without fear of reprisal or prosecution; (2) Turkey has ceased efforts to deny the recognition of the civil, cultural, and human rights of its Kurdish citizens; (3) Turkey has ceased military operations against Kurdish civilians; and (4) Turkey has taken steps toward a peaceful resolution of the Kurdish issue.

Environmental Finance Act of 1995 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to establish an Environmental Financial Advisory Board to provide expert advice and recommendations on issues affecting the costs and financing of environmental activities at the Federal, State, and local levels. 
Directs the Board to report to the Administrator and make services and expertise available to Congress. 
Requires the Board to:  (1) work with the Science Advisory Board to develop methods to integrate risk and finance considerations into environmental decision making; (2) identify and examine strategies to enhance environmental protection in urban areas, reduce disproportionate risks facing urban communities, and promote economic revitalization and environmentally sustainable development; (3) develop and recommend initiatives to expand opportunities for the export of U.S. financial services and environmental technologies; (4) develop alternative financing mechanisms to assist State and local governments in paying for environmental programs; (5) develop alternative financing mechanisms and strategies to meet the unique needs of small and economically disadvantaged communities; and (6) undertake other activities as the Board determines will further the purpose of this Act. 
Directs the Board to hold open meetings and seek input from the public and other interested parties. 
Authorizes appropriations.

High School Sports Information Collection Act of 2009 - Amends the Education Sciences Reform Act of 2002 to direct the Statistics Commissioner to collect, annually, for the immediately preceding academic year, from each coeducational secondary school that receives federal financial assistance that has an athletic program, the following information: (1) the number of male and female students that attended the school and for each student an identification of such student's race and ethnicity; (2) a listing of the teams that competed in athletic competition and for each such team the following data: (1) the season in which the team competed, and the total number of participants as of the day of the first scheduled contest and for each participant an identification of such participant's gender, race, and ethnicity; (3) the total expenditures for the team, including the travel expenditures, the equipment expenditures, the uniform expenditures, the expenditures for facilities, and the total number of trainers and medical personnel and their gender, race, and ethnicity; and (4) the total number of coaches and an identification of such coach's gender, race, and ethnicity.

Requires such schools to make such information available to students and to the public.

Generating American Income and Infrastructure Now Act - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to sell, under terms established by the Secretary of the Treasury, distressed notes and other obligations held by the Department of Agriculture.

Requires the proceeds from such sales to be deposited in an account designated for purposes of carrying out infrastructure projects in low-income communities.

Requires the Secretary to consult with the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a fair market valuation for such sales.

Requires the Secretary to notify the borrower of the intention to sell the note or other obligation.

Requires the Secretary to obtain the highest possible return from such sales and to sell such notes or other obligations on a competitive bidding or negotiated process, in amounts sufficient to assure market interest.

Authorizes the Secretary to employ public finance advisors from micro-, woman-, and minority-owned businesses.

Requires the Secretary to require persons offering to purchase the note or other obligation to demonstrate: (1) an ability or resources to provide such servicing; and (2) the ability to generate capital to provide such additional servicing.

National Youth Summer Jobs Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to eligible entities to provide summer employment and job readiness activities for out-of-school youths.

Requires the Secretary to give preference to an entity in a community where: (1) at least one of the following rates was higher than the national average of: (2) high school dropout rate; (3) poverty rate; (4) juvenile offender rate; (5) unemployment rate; or (6) industry-depletion rate.

Requires the Secretary to give additional preference to an entity that operates in a community where: (1) each rate of such rate was higher than the national average; and (2) the rate of such rate was higher than the national average for each of the following specified years.

Requires the Secretary to give additional preference to an entity that operates in a community where: (1) each rate of such rate was higher than the national average for each of the following specified years; and (2) the rate of such rate was higher than the national average for each of the following specified years.

Medicare Pharmacist Services Coverage Act of 2001 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000, to provide for coverage of pharmacy services under Medicare.

Reducing Barriers to Veterans' Benefits Act - Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA), in determining whether to provide veterans with benefits under the veterans' health care maintenance organization (HMO) program, to consider whether the veteran: (1) was assigned to a military occupational specialty or equivalent; or (2) served in combat against a hostile force during a period of hostilities.

Requires the Secretary to issue proposed regulations setting forth the Secretary's determination within 60 days after the Secretary determines that a presumption of service connection is warranted for a military occupational specialty or equivalent.

Requires the Secretary to ensure that a member of the armed forces under the jurisdiction of the Secretary is receiving an audiometric test at the 8000 Hz (Hz) frequency to evaluate the hearing of the member during the 90-day period before the date on which the member is discharged, separated, or retired.

Coal Cleanup Taxpayer Protection Act - Amends the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to issue a state reclamation bond authorizing reclamation of surface coal mining operations.

Prohibits the Secretary from accepting a self-bonded applicant for a coal mining reclamation bond until the applicant has been renewed for such bond.

Requires the Secretary to notify all state regulatory authorities that allow applicants to self-bond that the approved regulatory programs of the state regulatory authority must be amended to remove authority for self-bond and require coal mining operations covered by a self-bond by the earlier of: (1) the date of renewal of the permit; and (2) the date of any major permit modification.

Requires the Secretary to issue rules establishing limitations on surety bonds to minimize the risk of financial liability to the federal government or a state government, including rules regarding: (1) the maximum quantity of corporate surety bonds issued by any one corporate surety as a percentage of the total quantity of coal mine reclamation bonds in any one state; (2) the minimum percentage of surety bonds unrelated to activities regulated pursuant to this Act required to reinsure corporate surety bonds; (3) the minimum collateralization required for corporate surety bonds; and (4) the

United Nations Oil-for-Food Accountability Act of 2004 - Requires the President to withhold 10% of the amount of the United Nations (UN) regular budget for FY 2005 from amounts appropriated for contributions to international organizations as follows: (1) 10% of the funds appropriated for contributions to international organizations in an Act making appropriations for FY 2005; and (2) 20% of such funds in FY 2006.

Requires the certification of the President to Congress that: (1) the United Nations has procedures that provide the Comptroller General access to all documents relating to the oil-for-food program so that the Comptroller General may perform nationally mandated reviews of UN operations; (2) the United Nations Secretary General has formally confirmed that the United Nations will not assert the sovereignty of United Nations (UN) papers and internal records that concern the oil-for-food program or a sanction imposed on Iraq related to the program; (3) the United Nations Secretary General has authorized the release of any member state authentic copies of any document in the possession of the requesting authority that concerns the program; (4) the United Nations has waived any U.S. judicial immunity for any civil or

TANF Recipients' Lifeline Act - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to repeal the five-year limitation on benefits for certain qualified aliens. 
Excludes from the five-year limitation on TANF benefits for certain qualified aliens: (1) the temporary assistance for needy children program; (2) the block grant to States for assistance in the latter two fiscal years; and (3) the inflation adjustment to TANF block grant amounts.

Stop Assistance to Counterfeiters Act - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to prohibit assistance to a person seeking U.S. assistance for a fiscal year until the person certifies to the President that such assistance will not be used to: (1) intentionally traffic in goods or services that contain counterfeit marks; (2) be used by any person that has had an administrative or judicial determination issued against it for infringement, counterfeiting, or piracy of intellectual property in the United States or a foreign country; (3) be imported into the United States in violation of certain laws; or (4) be used in violation of certain conditions for a contract, grant, cooperative agreement, or other agreement that includes use of any intellectual property.

Requires the President to suspend or terminate assistance or other assistance to a person seeking U.S. assistance if the President determines that such person has used such assistance to: (1) carry out an activity in violation of such certification; or (2) be used in violation of certain conditions for a contract, grant, cooperative agreement, or other agreement that includes use of any intellectual property.

Developing Resources Immediately and Long-Term through Leases on Our Nation's Offshore Waters Act of 2008 or the DRILL NOW Act of 2008 - Terminates all existing federal offshore leasing activities for any area of the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) in order to eliminate the authority of the President to withdraw federal submerged lands of the OCS in leasing activities.

Revises the revocation of presidential authority for federal submerged lands of the OCS to: (1) provide for the availability of certain areas for leasing; and (2) provide for the disposition of revenues from such leasing.

Requires deposit of 25% of qualified revenues in the Treasury, 25% of qualified revenues in the general fund, and 37.5% of qualified revenues in a special account from which the Secretary of the Treasury disposes of the remainder to a state in order to implement a plan for expenditure of such funds.

Requires the Secretary to deposit 6.25% of qualified revenues in the Treasury, 6.25% of qualified revenues in the general fund, and 6.25% in a special account from which the Secretary disposes of the remainder to a state in order to implement a plan for expenditure

Energy-Efficient Cool Roof Jobs Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a 20-year property tax deduction for the costs of replacing an energy-efficient cool roof with a new one. Defines "qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property" as any roof system which: (1) is placed in service above conditioned or semi-heated space on an eligible commercial building and during the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on December 31, 2013, which has a slope equal to or less than: (2) 2:12, (3) less than 2:12, (4) less than 1:12, or (5) 3:1. Defines "qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property" as any roof system which: (1) has a cool roof surface, and (2) has a 3-year-aged solar reflectance index of at least 64.

Federal Propaganda Prohibition Act of 2005 - Requires an executive agency to notify Congress regarding certain contracts it may enter into with certain agencies for public relations, media relations, advertising, or public opinion research services.

Prohibits an officer or employee of the United States Government from making or authorizing an expenditure or obligation of funds for publicity or propaganda purposes unless authorized by law. Subjects violators to administrative discipline and criminal penalties.

Requires each advertisement or other communication paid for by an executive agency, either directly or through a contract awarded by the agency, to include a prominent notice informing the target audience that the advertisement or other communication is paid for by that agency. Includes among such notice: (1) an advertisement disseminated in any form, including print or by any electronic means; and (2) a communication by an individual in any form, including speech, print, or by any electronic means.

Confederate Commemorative Works Inventory and Joint Resource Study Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior, using inventories received pursuant to this Act, to conduct a special inventory of Confederate commemorative works, including those commemorating and interpreting the Civil War, the commemoration, the soldiers, people on the home front and battle lines, and the related locations in the United States from 1861 through 1865.  Requires the Director of the National Park Service to conduct a special resource study of such works, identifying: (1) a historical assessment of each inventoried work; (2) an evaluation of the suitability and feasibility of retaining the work; (3) the identification of properties that could meet criteria for listing in the National Register of Historic Places or criteria for designation as National Historic Landmarks or if the work is already on the or part of, another designation or district; (4) an evaluation of relevant historical research on, education about, and public awareness of the work; and (5) any other matters that the Director determines to be appropriate for this study.

Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard Deadline Harmonization Act of 2015 This bill directs the governor of each state to designate in accordance with the Clean Air Act all areas (or portions thereof) of the state's state as attainment, nonattainment, or unclassifiable with respect to the 2015 ozone standards. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) must promulgate final designations for all areas in all states with respect to the standards, including any modifications to the designations submitted. The standards shall not apply to the review and disposition of a preconstruction permit application if: (1) the EPA or the state, local, or tribal permitting authority determines that the application is complete on or before the promulgation of the final designations, or (2) the EPA or the state, local, or tribal permitting authority publishes a preliminary determination or draft permit for the application 60 days after the promulgation of the designations.  The bill amends the Clean Air Act to extend the 10-year period for the review and disposition of preconstruction permits for the implementation of the standards.

Endangered Species Community Advisory Board Act of 1995 - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish an Endangered Species Community Advisory Board in connection with the designation of an area as critical habitat or as a National Wildlife Refuge. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) the membership of the Board; (2) Board responsibilities; (3) Board funding; (4) Board personnel; and (5) Board monitoring and reporting.

Freedom to Mourn in Peace Act of 2011 - Amends the federal criminal code to prohibit persons from carrying out any demonstration where a funeral, memorial service, or other bereavement ceremony for a veteran is held unless the demonstration has been approved by the cemetery superintendent or the owner of the property on which the funeral is held.

Defines a "demonstration" to include: (1) any picketing or similar conduct; (2) any oration, speech, use of amplification equipment or device, or similar conduct that is not part of a funeral; (3) the display of any placard, banner, flag, or similar device, unless such display is part of a funeral; (4) the distribution of any handbill, pamphlet, leaflet, or other written or printed matter other than a program distributed as part of a funeral; and (5) any other written or printed matter that is not part of a funeral.

Helping to Encourage Real Opportunities (HERO) for At-Risk Youth Act This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2019 the work opportunity tax credit for summer youth and at-risk youth who are certified by the local agency as having attained age 16 but not age 25 on the hiring date, as not regularly attending secondary or technical or post-secondary school during the six-month period preceding the hiring date, as not regularly employed during such six-month period, and as not readily employable by reason of lacking a sufficient number of basic skills or as having attained age 16 but not age 21 on the hiring date and an eligible foster child who was in foster care during the 12-month period ending on the hiring date.

Save America's Utility Infrastructure and Secure America Now Act of 2008 - Amends the Federal Power Act to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to issue a rule to prohibit disturbances (other than planned maintenance) lasting greater than five days at certain substations subject to its reliability standards.

Directs the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, acting through the Assistant Secretary of the Office of the Infrastructure Protection, to study and report to Congress on gaps in emergency planning preparedness and management related to vulnerable populations, including: (1) individuals with disabilities, visual impairments, hearing impairments, limited English proficiency, and literacy barriers; (2) socially and economically disadvantaged households and communities; (3) individuals over age 65; (4) minor children; and (5) individuals with pets or service animals.

Small Company Capital Formation Act of 2011 - Amends the Securities Act of 1933 to exempt from its requirements for securities that are not publicly traded and that are not subject to the Federal securities laws and regulations, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) (currently, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)), and State law, any securities that are offered and sold in a manner that may substantially reduces the public offering and sale price of such securities.

Requires the SEC to add a class of securities to the securities exempted under this Act.

Directs the Comptroller General to study the impact of State laws regulating securities offerings, or Blue Sky laws, on offerings made under Regulation A (17 CFR 230.251 et seq.).

Directs the Comptroller General to report to the congressional financial services committees on the findings of the study.

Federal Election Integrity Act of 2004 - Amends the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 to require the appropriate State or local election official to provide proof of citizenship, in accordance with guidelines established by the Election Administration Commission (EAC), to accompany an application for, or a mail-in ballot for, a Federal election.

Prohibits the appropriate State or local election official from permitting any individual to register to vote in an election for Federal office (including a provisional ballot under the same circumstances) unless the individual provides the official with a photographic copy of any document that provides proof that the individual is a U.S. citizen, in accordance with guidelines established by the EAC.

Prohibits the appropriate State or local election official from accepting any ballot for an election for Federal office provided by an individual who votes by mail, unless the individual submits a copy of a current and valid photo identification to the official.

Prohibits the appropriate State or local election official from: (1) allowing any individual to register to vote in an election for Federal office (including a provisional ballot under the same circumstances) unless the individual presents to the official a current and valid photo identification, or (2) accepting any ballot provided by an individual who votes by

Child Care Lending Pilot Act of 2003 - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to authorize the Small Business Administration (SBA) to provide loans to child care businesses (i.e., small, non-profit child care businesses) to assist, in addition to other eligible small business concerns, small, nonprofit child care businesses, provided that: (1) the loan will be used for a sound business purpose that has been approved by the SBA; and (2) each receiving financial assistance meets all of the same eligibility requirements applicable to for-profit businesses.

Requires the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to report to the congressional small business and small business committees on the implementation of the program to specified congressional committees.

Flexible Refinancing for American Families Act of 2012 - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to each refinance qualified mortgages owned or guaranteed by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac into a five- or 30-year term that are first mortgages purchased or refinanced on or before the date of enactment of this Act.

Requires such refinancing mortgages to have a five- or 30-year term that are fully amortized over, with a single mortgage loan principal repayment of 30 years and a fixed interest rate of 5.5%.

Prohibits prepayment penalties for refinancing of the mortgage.

Prohibits the servicer of a mortgage refinancing through a refinancing mortgage from charging a fee for the refinancing of the mortgage.

Prohibits the borrower fees of the mortgage refinancing from exceeding $1,000.

This bill amends the federal budget law to provide for a two-fiscal year budget authority for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) specified in the Veterans Health Administration Act of 1990.  Beginning with FY2010, the bill provides for a new discretionary budget authority for the VA for the FY2010-FY2010 appropriations cycle.  The VA shall study the adequacy and accuracy of the budget projections made by the Enrollee Health Care Projection Model, or its equivalent, as utilized for the purpose of estimating and projecting VA health care expenditures for the FY2010-FY2010 four fiscal years.

(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on January 10, 2018.  (Sec. 1) This bill directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to study and report to Congress on the filing requirements under the universal service program for telecommunications carriers or service providers participating in the program for the provision of service under the Communications Act of 1934. The FCC must report to Congress on: (1) the financial impact of such filing requirements on covered carriers participating in the program; and (2) recommendations on how to consolidate redundant filing requirements for covered carriers participating in the program.

Hunt Unrestricted on National Treasures Act or the HUNT Act - Requires each head of a federal public land management agency to make available to the public on the agency's website a report that includes a list of the location and acreage of land more than 640 acres in size under the agency's jurisdiction on which the public is allowed, under federal or state law, to hunt, fish, or use the land for other recreational purposes.

Requires the head of a federal public land management agency to: (1) make such a list available to the public on the agency's website and to revise it as the head of the agency determines appropriate, a list of roads or trails that provide the primary public access and egress to contiguous parcels of land equal to more than 640 acres in size under the agency's jurisdiction on which the public is allowed to hunt, fish, or use the land for other recreational purposes; and (2) in considering public access and egress under this Act, consider public access and egress to the legal boundaries of the land, including access and egress by motorized or non-motorized vehicles and on foot or horseback.

Amends the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965 to provide that in an amount not

Clean Alternatives for Energy Independence Act of 2005 - Repeals the Energy Policy Act of 2005 (the Act) to repeal the tax subsidies for: (1) oil and gas production; (2) the excise tax on small refiners cooperatives; (3) natural gas distribution lines treated as 15-year property; (4) the deduction for the cost of capital for small refiners cooperatives; (5) the tax credit for new qualified fuel cell motor vehicles; (6) the tax credit for alternative fuel vehicles; (7) the tax credit for refueling hydrogen-related property; and (8) the tax credit for alternative fuel vehicle refueling property.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the fuel cell tax incentive for residential and business use.

Increases the credit for alternative fuel vehicle refueling property.

Fixed Asset Relief Act of 2015  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the 100% depreciation deduction for qualified property to an additional $100,000.  The bill also allows a 10% bonus depreciation for computer software and water utility property.

Amends the Siletz Tribe Indian Restoration Act to permit the Secretary of the Interior to accept title to additional real property located within the boundaries of the original 1855 Siletz Coast Reservation (comprised of land within the political boundaries of Benton, Douglas, Lane, Lincoln, Tillamook, and Yamhill Counties in the State of Oregon) if that real property is conveyed or otherwise transferred to the United States by or on behalf of the tribe. Considers such real property to be an on-reservation acquisition under the Federal reservation law provisions of the Federal charter law concerning the reservation of the Sioux Tribe of the Great Sioux Reservation in Dakota, Oregon.

Measuring the Economic Impact of Broadband Act of 2018 This bill requires the Department of Commerce to conduct an assessment and analysis regarding the effect of broadband deployment and adoption on the U.S. economy.

Increasing Medical Oversight in the Department of Veterans Affairs Act of 2014 - Establishes in the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) within the Office of the Under Secretary for Health the Office of the Medical Inspector, whose functions shall include: (1) reviewing the quality of health care provided to veterans by the VA and by the non-VA health care providers that the VA provides, (2) reviewing VA offices and facilities to ensure that policies and procedures of the VA and the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) are applied consistently at all such offices and facilities, (3) investigating any systemic issues that arise within the VHA, and (4) establishing temporary investigative teams to carry out reviews or investigations in response to specific incidents or inquiries. Directs the Medical Inspector to submit to the Secretary, the Under Secretary for Health, and Congress reports on any problems or deficiencies encountered in programs and operations of the VHA, including any recommendations for corrective actions. Requires the Medical Inspector to be the head of the VHA.

Rehab and Ahmed Amer Foster Care Improvement Act of 2012 - Amends part E (Foster Care and Adoption Assistance) of title IV of the Social Security Act to require states to: (1) exercise due diligence to identify and provide notice to all adult grandparents and other adult relatives of the child (including any other adult relatives suggested by the parents) that the child has been or is being removed from the custody of the parent or parents of the child; (2) provide notice of the decision and the reasons to each parent of the child, each relative who has expressed an interest in caring for the child, the guardian, and the guardian ad litem for the child, the attorney for the child, the attorney for each parent of the child, the child (if the child is able to express an opinion regarding placement), and the prosecutor involved; and (3) establish procedures to allow a person who receives a notice pursuant to such requirement to request, in writing, documentation of the reasons for the decision, the attorney for the child, and the court to review the decision.

National Strategic Gasoline Reserve for Purposes of National Security Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Energy (Secretary) to establish a Strategic Gasoline Reserve system with a total capacity of 10 million barrels of regular unleaded gasoline.

Requires the Secretary to determine strategic locations for no less than three and no more than five Gasoline Reserve sites, each located in a different geographical region of the United States.

Requires the Secretary to transmit to Congress, the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS), and the governor of each state in which a Gasoline Reserve will be sited a plan for the transportation of the contents of the Gasoline Reserve to wholesale or retail markets in the event of an emergency sale under this Act.

Requires the Secretary to complete the process of filling the Gasoline Reserve to a minimum of 90% within two years of submitting a transportation plan to Congress.

Requires the Secretary to conduct an annual review of the gasoline supply to ensure the reserves in the Gasoline Reserve do not exceed their shelf life.

Requires the Secretary to have in place within two years of enactment of this Act a plan for assuring that the inventory is sold and replaced in a manner that assures the integrity of the product at all times.

Directs the Secretary to sell gasoline from the Gasoline Reserve

Skill Game Protection Act - Amends the Wire Act to require the Secretary of the Treasury to prescribe regulations requiring each person who operates a game of skill on the Internet to maintain specified safeguards to ensure that the individual participant depositing funds is 18 years of age or older.

Requires the Secretary to prescribe regulations requiring each person who operates a game of skill on the Internet to maintain specified safeguards to ensure that the individual participant is physically located in a jurisdiction that does not bar participation in the particular Internet games of skill in which the individual participates at the time in the individual participates.

Requires the Secretary to prescribe regulations to combat fraud and money laundering as may be prescribed by the Secretary or a designee of the Secretary.

Requires the rules of construction of the Act to be nonapplicable to non-sports wagering.

Spearfish Canyon and Bismarck Lake Land Exchange Act - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to convey to South Dakota certain land in the Black Hills National Forest and certain land in the Bismarck Lake Area of South Dakota to the Secretary of the Interior if the state of South Dakota conveys to the Secretary all right, title, and interest of the state in and to the non-federal land.

Requires the Secretary and the state of South Dakota to select an appraiser to conduct appraisals of the federal and non-federal land.

Requires the value of the federal and non-federal land to be determined based on the agricultural value of the federal and non-federal land to be exchanged.

Requires the value of the federal and non-federal land to be equal or to be equalized.

Requires the state of South Dakota to convey additional non-federal land to the Secretary in order to exchange it for the federal land.

Requires the federal land acquired by the state to be managed for public recreation uses and the conservation of natural resources.

Requires the state of South Dakota to allow the grazing of domestic livestock in effect on the date of acquisition of the non-federal land to continue subject to the related user agreements, including permitted stocking rates, grazing fee levels, access rights

Troubled Asset Relief Program Enhancement Act - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to require the Comptroller General (GAO) to have access to any information, data, schedules, books, accounts, financial records, reports, files, electronic communications, or other papers, things, or property belonging to or in use by the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and to its officers, employees, directors, independent public accountants, financial advisors and any and all other agents and representatives, at such time as the Comptroller General may request.

Requires the Comptroller General to be afforded full facility for verifying transactions with the balances or securities held by, among others, depositories, fiscal agents, and custodians.

Authorizes the Comptroller General to make and retain copies of such books, accounts, and other records as the Comptroller General deems appropriate.

Prohibits the Comptroller General from publicly disclosing proprietary or trade secret information obtained under this Act.

Authorizes appropriations for FY2010 and FY2011.

American Livestock Protection and Ranching Opportunity Act of 2014 - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) the overwhelming majority of consumers want to know where animals used to produce the meat they ate is born, raised, and slaughtered; (2) country-of-origin labeling provides information consumers have a right to know; and (3) country-of-origin labeling facilitates supply chain information critical for food safety.  Amends the Animal Health Protection Act to prohibit the importation of fresh meat and meat products from countries that have foot-and-mouth disease without vaccination until the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) certifies that a country is free of foot-and-mouth disease without vaccination.  Establishes in the Department of Agriculture (USDA) a livestock disease initiative under which the Secretary shall provide to eligible entities competitive grants for research and development to conduct surveillance methods, vaccines, vaccination delivery systems, or diagnostic tests for diseases in domestic livestock that present a potential concern to public health and safety.  Authorizes the Secretary to give priority to research and development relating to bovine brucellosis, bovine tuberculosis, and other zoonotic diseases in livestock that are covered by a high-priority research and extension initiative.  Authorizes appropriations for FY2015-

Provides for the following additional educational assistance for full-time pursuit: (1) for amounts paid during FY 2003; (2) for amounts paid during a subsequent fiscal year; and (3) for amounts paid during a subsequent fiscal year.
Provides for the following educational assistance for half-time pursuit: (1) for amounts paid during FY 2003; (2) for amounts paid during a subsequent fiscal year; and (3) for amounts paid during a subsequent fiscal year.
Increases the aggregate amount of educational assistance available for administrative expenses.

Strengthening Entrepreneurs' Economic Development Act of 2013 - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to establish a loan program and a process under which an eligible small business concern may submit an application to the Administrator for loan assistance.  Requires each loan made to an eligible small business concern to be in an amount not to exceed $150,000.  Requires the SBA to: (1) establish a loan process under which lenders originating, underwriting, closing, and servicing the loan applicant will receive loan application participation fees; and (2) offer to sell loans made by the SBA under the program.  Requires the SBA to assess, collect, and retain a fee of not to exceed a certain percentage of the outstanding balance of the loan, as necessary to reduce to zero the cost to the SBA of making loans under this Act.

Affordable Housing Preservation and Revitalization Act of 2009 - Amends the United States Housing Act of 1937 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to ensure that funds in the residual receipts account of an eligible multifamily housing property are transferred, at the time of a qualified sale or exchange, to a preservation entity that is committed to maintaining the affordability and preservation of such projects by allowing expanded access to existing residual receipts to assist with the acquisition and rehabilitation of the project.

Defines "affordability and use restrictions" as the affordability and use restrictions in connection with project-based housing assistance payments under this Act.

Defines "preservation entity" as an entity: (1) that is a nonprofit corporation under State law that is exempt from Federal income taxation; or (2) that is approved by the housing agency that has the capacity to acquire and preserve an eligible multifamily housing property.

Requires the restrictions under this Act to be: (1) binding on all successors and assigns of the preservation entity; and (2) recorded as a restrictive covenant on the property pursuant to State law.

District of Columbia Government Improvement and Efficiency Act of 1996 - Amends the first section of the Proclamation from the President to:  (1) reduce the minimum number of members of the Board of Trustees of the American University to twenty-five; (2) repeal the Service Contract Act of 1965; (3) authorize agreements between the District of Columbia and the Bureau of Prisons to establish amounts for the housing District prisoners; (4) exempt certain contracts from the Council's review; (5) waive the residency requirement for certain employees of the District's Inspector General; and (6) authorize the Director of the Bureau of Prisons to waive the requirement that certain District employees serve without compensation for their services on the Board. 
Amends the District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act to repeal the requirement that the Mayor of the District of Columbia and the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, respectively, be nominated by the President to serve on the Board.

Children's Express Lane to Health Coverage Act of 2003 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to permit a State to provide for the financial eligibility requirements of a Medicaid or Child Health Assistance under the Medicaid program with respect to medical assistance for an individual under the State plan approved under title XXI.

State Prescription Drug Discount Act of 2002 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require manufacturers of outpatient drug programs under the Medicaid program to enter into agreements with the State for rebates for covered outpatient drugs. Defines "covered outpatient drug" as any drug that is sold at a low price in the State and is intended for use in the outpatient department of a patient.

Minuteman Missile National Historic Site Establishment Act of 1998 - Establishes the Minuteman Missile National Historic Site in South Dakota as a unit of the National Park System.  Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to make minor adjustments to the boundary of the Site. 
Authorizes the Secretary to acquire lands and interests therein by donation, purchase with donated or appropriated funds, exchange or transfer from another Federal agency:  Provides that lands or interests therein owned by the State of South Dakota may only be acquired by donation or exchange.  Prohibits the Secretary from acquiring any lands pursuant to this Act if such lands, or any portion thereof, are contaminated with hazardous substances unless all remedial action necessary to protect human health and the environment has been taken pursuant to such Act. 
Directs the Secretary to prepare a general management plan for the Site.  Authorizes appropriations.

Directs the Congress to establish a limit on total outlays to be made under the Medicare program for the fiscal year. 
Amends the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 to require that congressional sequestration of Medicare program outlays be eliminated if, with respect to a fiscal year, the Congress has not enacted a joint resolution to save Medicare Act of 1995 before the first day of the fiscal year. 
Requires the President to reduce payments under the Medicare program by a uniform percentage sufficient to reduce 50 percent of such amount. 
Requires OMB and CBO to issue preview, update, and final reports on Medicare sequestration.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) ensure that the mission and purposes of the System are carried out, except that if a conflict exists between the primary purpose of a Refuge and any purpose of the System, the conflict shall be resolved in a manner that first fulfills the primary purpose of the Refuge and, to the extent practicable, also achieves the purposes of the System; (2) ensure that opportunities for the uses of the Refuge receive priority attention in the planning and management of the System; (3) plan, propose, and direct expansion of the System to accomplish the mission and purposes of the System and contribute to the conservation of the ecosystems of the United States; and (4) inventory and monitor the status and trends of fish, wildlife, and plants in each Refuge.
Requires the Secretary to: (1) not initiate or permit a new use of a Refuge or expand, renew, or extend an existing allowed use unless the Secretary determines that the use is compatible with the primary purposes of the Refuge and the System specified in this Act; and (2) identify, prior to acquisition, existing compatible public uses of the Refuge that shall be permitted to continue on an interim basis pending completion of comprehensive planning and revise such plans not less frequently than every 15 years thereafter.
Government Shutdown Prevention Act - Amends Federal law to provide for continuing appropriations in the absence of regular appropriations for a fiscal year.

Investment Tax Incentive Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a special depreciation deduction for tangible depreciable property placed in service in a taxable year beginning after December 31, 1992.  Repeals the special depreciation rules applicable to the adjusted current earnings provisions of the alternative minimum tax.

Deter Revolving-door Appointments in our Nation; Stop Washington Appointees from becoming Manipulative Petitioners Act or the DRAIN the SWAMP Act This bill amends the federal criminal code to prohibit former political appointees from serving as registered lobbyists, agents of foreign principals, or representatives of a foreign government.

Requires a dealer to disclose to each new automobile purchaser certain information regarding any event data recorder installed on such automobile, including: (1) the presence and location of such recorder; (2) the type of information recorded by such recorder and how such information is recorded; and (3) that such information also may be used in a law enforcement proceeding.  Requires the manufacturer to include in the owner's manual of any new automobile containing such recorder clear and conspicuous disclosures.  Requires any event data recorder in the vehicle and any recorded data on such recorder to be considered property of the vehicle. Prohibits the downloading or otherwise retrieving of such data by a person other than the owner, except under specified circumstances.  Prohibits the manufacture of a new automobile after 2008 from having an event data recorder unless the recorder includes a function whereby the consumer has the option to enable or disable the recording function.  Sets forth enforcement provisions.

Stabilize Medicaid and CHIP Coverage Act - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) and CHIP to require a State Medicaid or Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) plan to provide that an individual who is determined to be eligible for benefits under such plan (or waiver) shall remain eligible and enrolled for such benefits through the end of the month in which the 12-month period (beginning on the date of determination of eligibility) ends.

Requires a State child health plan that provides child health assistance under title XXI (State Children's Health Insurance Program) (SCHIP) to provide that an individual who is determined to be eligible for benefits under such plan shall remain eligible and enrolled for such benefits through the end of the month in which the 12-month period (beginning on the date of determination of eligibility) ends.

Makes such requirements applicable to determinations (and redeterminations) made on or after 18 months after the enactment of this Act.

Prohibits a State from applying such requirements, or a State plan under title XIX or XXI, on any date before the 18-month enactment date.

National Milestones to Measure Progress in Ending the Opioid Epidemic Act of 2018 This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop national indicators to measure success in curtailing the opioid epidemic, with the goal of significantly reversing the toll of opioid misuse and opioid-related morbidity and mortality in the United States within five years of enactment of this bill. The national milestones shall include: (1) the establishment of at least 10 indicators or metrics to measure progress in meeting the goal, which shall include a reduction in opioid overdose, a reduction in emergency room visits related to opioid misuse and abuse, an increase in public and provider education, an increase in the number of individuals in sustained recovery from opioid use disorder, a reduction in the number of co-infections associated with injection drug use, and an increase in the number of providers prescribing medically assisted treatment for opioid use disorder in different settings. HHS may extend the timeline for meeting such goal by one year if the goal will not be achieved within five years of this bill's enactment. HHS must include with any such extension a rationale for why additional time is needed and a description of changes the HHS will make in order to achieve such goal within such extended period.

Amends Federal law to deem the full equalization of allotments within the meaning of such Act to have been completed.  Excludes allotments in the Mineral Springs area from such equalization. 
Amends the Act to provide for the equalization of allotments on the Agua Caliente (Palm Springs) Reservation in California. 
Removes the restriction on the distribution of net revenues derived from parcel B under the Act to members of the Band and their heirs entitled to equalization of the value of allotments of those members.

Special Needs Trust Fairness and Medicaid Improvement Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to report to Congress on the use of tobacco cessation services for mothers of newborn children. HHS must assess the use of tobacco cessation services under the Medicaid program. (Sec. 3) The bill also amends title XIX (Medicaid) to require the Medicaid Improvement Fund to provide additional funding for FY2021.

Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to provide for the relief of a member of a reserve component who is ordered to report for military service for a period of more than 90 days and who is a lessee of real property occupied by the member or dependents of the member.  Provides for the refundable tax credit for lessors for the rent of such a member or dependents.

Patent and Trademark Office Authorization Act of 2002 - Authorizes appropriations to the United States Patent and Trademark Office for salaries and necessary expenses for each of FY 2003 through 2008 for the Office's activities related to the registration and protection of trademarks used in commerce.

Directs the Director of the Office to submit to specified congressional committees an electronic filing and processing system for patent and trademark applications.

Requires the Office to develop an electronic system for the filing and processing of patent and trademark applications, including the necessary infrastructure to allow examiners and applicants to send all communications electronically and to allow the Office to process, maintain, and search electronically the contents and history of each application.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce to report to specified congressional committees on: (1) the progress made in implementing the 21st Century Strategic Plan; and (2) any amendments made to the plan.

Amends Federal patent law to grant the Office's third-party appeal rights in patent and copyright infringement and related patent appeals.

Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 2011, the duty on certain three-ring binders, standard letter-sized paper measuring approximately 51 mm by 280 mm, and certain other covered polyester fabrics.

Wholesale Motor Fuel Fairness and Competition Restoration Act - Makes it a violation of this Act for an owner or operator of a terminal facility to sell motor fuel from the terminal facility to a distributor or retailer at a price in excess of the price it charges any other distributor or retailer, including a distributor or retailer which it owns or with which it is affiliated.

Authorizes the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to assess a civil penalty for each violation.

Requires the FTC to issue regulations requiring full disclosure by refiners and distributors of their wholesale motor fuel pricing policies, including rebates, incentives, and market enhancement allowances.

Directs the FTC to: (1) ensure that all information acquired pursuant to such regulations is made available to the public, except trade secrets and commercial or financial information protected from disclosure; and (2) transmit a report to Congress on whether ownership or operation by a refiner of a facility for the retail sale of motor fuel has anticompetitive effects on the price of motor fuel.

Foreign Medical School Accountability Fairness Act of 2013 - Amends title I (General Provisions) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 to repeal provisions that require a foreign graduate medical school to meet certain criteria for participation in the Department of Education (ED) part D (Student Assistance) loan program before it may qualify a student for loan assistance under such program.  Excludes from such requirement that a foreign graduate medical school meet certain criteria for participation in ED part D before it may qualify a student for loan assistance under ED part D.  Excludes from such requirement that a foreign graduate medical school meet certain criteria for participation in ED part D before it may qualify a student for loan assistance under ED part A (Aid to Families with Dependent Children).  Excludes from such requirement that a foreign graduate medical school meet certain criteria for participation in ED part A before it may qualify a student for loan assistance under ED part C (Child and Education Assistance) (currently, ED part A).  Excludes from such requirement that a foreign graduate medical school meet certain criteria for participation in ED part A before it may qualify a student for loan assistance under ED part C (Child and Education Assistance) (currently, ED part B (Child and Education Assistance) (formerly known

Disclosure; and Encouragement of Verification, Innovation, Cleaning, and Efficiency Act of 2017 or the DEVICE Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require manufacturers of devices marketed in interstate commerce to give the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) premarket notification of any change to the design, reprocessing instructions, or recommendations for reprocessing of a device.  The FDA must publish a list of types of rapid assessment tests for which premarket notification must include:  instructions for use that have been validated in a manner specified by the FDA; and validation data of the types specified by the FDA.  The bill also requires the FDA to periodically update the list.

Biased IRS Audit Systems Prevention Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to: (1) provide to the taxpayer a tax return selected for auditing by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) that includes a description of any data used in the selection process, including whether such data was filed electronically or transcribed from a return printed and filed on paper, and (2) preserve such information in a manner that it is available for review by an applicable oversight entity.

Requires the Undersecretary to choose at least 10 military installations on which to implement the pilot program.

Requires the Undersecretary to contract for an independent evaluation of the pilot program.
