Authorizes a cash market to operate only in accordance with rules approved by the Commission.

Amends Federal law to provide for continuing appropriations in the absence of regular appropriations.

Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to require the Director of the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management to establish an emergency preparedness demonstration program to research and promote the capacity of disadvantaged communities to carry out programs to provide data, information, and awareness education by providing grants to or executing contracts or cooperative agreements with nonprofit organizations to establish and conduct such programs.

Authorizes an organization to use a grant, contract, or cooperative agreement to: (1) acquire expert professional services necessary to conduct research in disadvantaged communities; (2) develop and prepare informational materials to promote awareness about emergency preparedness and how to protect their households and communities in advance of disasters; (3) establish consortia with national organizations serving disadvantaged individuals, institutions of higher education serving disadvantaged individuals, and faith-based institutions to disseminate information about emergency preparedness to such communities; and (4) implement a joint project with an institution serving disadvantaged individuals, including a part B institution, an institution of higher education, or a Hispanic-serving institution.

Requires the Director to establish a procedure by which to accept such applications.

Territorial Economic Growth and Recovery Act of 2016 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the tax on the excise tax on distilled spirits.  The bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for the payment of lost revenue to the Virgin Islands from the tax on distilled spirits.

Veterans Traumatic Brain Injury Treatment Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to establish a screening program for veterans who are eligible for hospital care, medical services, and nursing home care for symptoms of traumatic brain injury.

Requires the Secretary to develop and carry out a comprehensive program of long-term care for post-acute traumatic brain injury rehabilitation that includes residential, community, and home-based components utilizing interdisciplinary treatment teams.

Recapture Excess Profits and Invest in Roads (REPAIR) Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax on any taxpayer with an integrated oil company, or any other producer or refiner of crude oil with gross receipts from the sale of such crude oil or refined oil products exceeding $1 million.

Defines "windfall profit" as the excess of the adjusted taxable income of the taxpayer for the taxable year over the reasonably inflated average profit for such taxable year.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to provide such rules as are necessary for the withholding and deposit of the tax.

Requires the taxpayer liable for such tax to keep such records, make such returns, and furnish such information as the Secretary may by regulations prescribe.

Requires the Secretary to file and the taxpayer liable for such tax returns within a specified time period.

Requires the Secretary to provide for the filing and the time of the tax return of the tax imposed.

Requires the windfall profit tax imposed by this Act to be treated as a deduction for income tax purposes.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) exempt from the windfall profit tax imposed by this Act; and (2) allow a tax deduction for windfall profit tax on crude oil.

Medicare Fracture Prevention and Osteoporosis Testing Act of 2007 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a national minimum payment amount for Medicare and Medicare-eligible Medicaid for treatment of bone mass scans and dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and vertebral fracture assessment.

Directs the Secretary to enter into an arrangement with the Institute of Medicine of the National Academies to study: (1) the ramifications of Medicare reimbursement reductions for DXA and VFA on beneficiary access to bone mass measurement benefits in general and in rural and minority communities; and (2) methods to increase use of bone mass measurement by Medicare beneficiaries.

Stop Illegal Reentry Act or Kate's Law - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to increase the criminal penalties for reentry of alien aliens who have been denied, excluded, deported, or removed entry or application for re-entry.

Defines "reentry" to include an alien who: (1) has been convicted of a drug offense before three or more misdemeanors involving drugs, crimes against the person, or both involving aliens; (2) has been excluded from the United States pursuant to a specified provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act; (3) has been removed from the United States pursuant to a specified provision of the Act; (4) has been denied entry, excluded, deported, or removed three or more times and thereafter entered, attempted to enter, or is at any time found in the United States; or (5) has been denied admission, excluded, deported, or removed three or more times and thereafter entered, attempted to enter, or is at any time found in the United States.

Imposes a mandatory minimum criminal fine of up to five years' imprisonment for aliens convicted of such a reentry offense or of at least two such reentries.

The bill also prohibits a physician from being liable under federal or state law for harm caused by an act or omission of a physician, or attending medical personnel supporting the physician, if such act or omission: (1) occurs in the course of furnishing qualified charity care; and (2) was not grossly negligent.

Homebuyer Tax Credit Improvement Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) prohibit a taxpayer from claiming the first-time homebuyer tax credit until age 18 if the taxpayer has not met the age requirement of purchasing a residence without the assistance of a tax-exempt estate tax exemption; and (2) require tax return preparers to file tax returns electronically if the taxpayer is a nonresident alien or a dependent of a U.S. citizen or permanent resident alien.

Highway Fairness and Reform Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to carry out a direct federal-aid highway program in accordance with the requirements of the Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Improvement (CAQI) Program of the Department of Transportation (DOT).

Authorizes the Secretary to elect to have the state waive its right to receive amounts apportioned or allocated to it under the federal-aid highway program for the fiscal year to which the election relates.

Requires the Secretary to accept an election if the Secretary determines that the state: (1) has an interstate maintenance program and agrees to maintain it; (2) submits a plan to the Secretary describing the purposes, projects, and uses to which amounts received under the program will be put; (3) agrees to obligate or expend amounts received under the program exclusively for projects that would be eligible for funding under CAQI if the state were not participating in the program; and (4) agrees to report annually to the Secretary on the use of amounts received and make the report available to the public in an easily accessible format.

Energy Savings Through Public-Private Partnerships Act of 2014 - Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require each federal energy manager to provide an explanation regarding any life-cycle cost-effective measures that have not been implemented.  Requires each energy manager, as part of the certification system under such Act and using guidelines developed by the Secretary of Energy, to provide an explanation regarding any life-cycle cost-effective measures that have not been implemented. Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require each federal energy manager to limit the recognition of operation and maintenance savings associated with systems modernized or replaced with the implementation of energy conservation measures, water conservation measures, or any series of energy conservation measures and water conservation measures. Children's' Internet Protection Act - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit a universal service (US) service for schools or libraries that fail to implement a filtering or blocking technology for computers with Internet access.

Requires the FCC to adopt rules implementing this Act within 120 days after enactment of this Act.

Amends Federal law to provide for alternative retired pay rates for members of the Armed Forces with a combat-related disability who are entitled to monthly retired pay computed using a specified formula. Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to permit such members to elect a specified replacement military pay base for such members with a combat-related disability who are entitled to monthly retired pay computed using such a formula.

Autofill Act of 2015 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to require the Department of the Treasury to make tax returns available in both a printable document file and in a computer-readable form suitable for automated tax preparation software.  The bill sets deadlines for: (1) the Department to make such tax returns within 15 days after the Department receives them, and (2) the Department to provide on its website a secure function that allows taxpayers to download, as both a printable document file and in a form suitable for input to automatic tax preparation software, the 1040, 1040A, and 1040EZ forms that are populated with information with respect to the taxpayer that is reported under chapter 61 or any other provision of this title under which reporting of information is required.  The bill also sets deadlines for: (1) the Department to provide on its website a secure function that allows taxpayers to download, as both a printable document file and in a form suitable for input to automatic tax preparation software, the 1040, 1040A, and 1040EZ forms that are populated with information with respect to the taxpayer that is reported under chapter 6

Intergovernmental Law Enforcement Information Sharing Act of 2001 - Directs the Attorney General to: (1) expeditiously carry out security clearance investigations for specified persons and grant security clearances to such persons; and (2) study and report to specified congressional committees on methods to enhance the sharing of sensitive Federal law enforcement information with State, territorial, and local law enforcement officials.

Mobile Workforce State Income Tax Fairness and Simplification Act - Prohibits any part of the wages or other remuneration earned by an employee who performs employment duties in more than one State from being subject to income tax in any State other than: (1) the State of the employee's residence; and (2) the State within which the employee is present and performing employment duties for more than 30 days during the calendar year in which the income is earned.

Defines "employee" to include a professional athlete, professional entertainer, or certain public figures.

SIG TARP Small Business Awareness Act of 2009 - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to direct the Special Inspector General for the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) in the Department of the Treasury to examine: (1) the effects of the Troubled Asset Relief Program on small financial institutions and small businesses; and (2) the effects of financial assistance to small businesses on small financial institutions.

Requires the Special Inspector General to include in each quarterly report to Congress information on the activities of the Secretary of the Treasury and any financial institutions receiving financial assistance under the Troubled Asset Relief Program to increase the participation of women, minorities, and women- and minority-owned businesses.

King Cove Road Land Exchange Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the State of Alaska all of its federal land within the Refuge in exchange for all of Alaska's federal land within the Wilderness.

Requires the Secretary and Alaska to select an appraiser to conduct appraisals of the federal land and non-federal land.

Requires the value of the federal land and the non-federal land to be equalized by conveying additional non-federal land to the Secretary, by the state making a cash payment to the United States, or by using specified methods.

Authorizes the Secretary to accept a payment in excess of 25% of the value of the federal land conveyed.

Requires the boundary of the Wilderness to be modified to exclude the federal land and non-federal land.

Requires the route of the road to be modified to follow the southern alignment of the alternative entitled "Alternative 2-Land Exchange and Southern Road Alignment."
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to reduce the estate and gift tax rates to 30 percent.
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through June 30, 1999, the duty on certain organic chemicals.

Veterans Serving Veterans Act of 2018 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the VA Choice and Quality Employment Act to require the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to maintain a single searchable database of qualified members of the Armed Forces who have been determined by the VA to have a military occupational specialty that corresponds to a vacant position in the VA. The database shall include information regarding:  the name and contact information of the qualified member of the Armed Forces; the date on which the members are expected to be discharged and released from active duty; each military occupational specialty currently or previously assigned to the member; and each qualified member who may be recruited to fill the vacancy before such member has been discharged and released from active duty.  The VA shall: (1) establish a Centers of Excellence for the Training of Intermediate Care Technicians in VA Medical Facilities, and (2) certify intermediate care technician veterans to work as VA medical facilities.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the exclusion from gross income of gain from the sale of certain small business stock to:  (1) increase such exclusion to 75 percent of the gain from the sale of such stock; and (2) reduce such exclusion to five years. 
Amends the Code to repeal the minimum tax preference for small business ownership. 
Amends the Code to repeal the per-issuer limitation on the working capital of corporations. 
Amends the Code to repeal the per-issuer limitation on the redemption of stock issued by a corporation. 
Amends the Code to repeal the per-issuer limitation on the working capital of corporations. 
Amends the Code to increase the exclusion from income for tax purposes for incentive stock options granted to certain trade or business oriented small business employees.

Highway Infrastructure Privatization Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow the Secretary of Transportation to exempt from the general tax-exempt financing of qualified highway infrastructure projects a specified amount of the aggregate face amount of bonds issued pursuant to such projects.

National Telecommuting and Air Quality Act - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to a nonprofit private entity to develop a pilot program for the use of telecommunications to perform work functions under circumstances in which the use of telecommunications reduces or eliminates the need to commute. 
Authorizes the Secretary to carry out such program in collaboration with the Environmental Protection Agency and the Secretary of Energy. 
Requires the pilot program to include recommendations for: (1) evaluating and developing methods for reducing emissions of ozone precursors that can be achieved as a result of reduced VMTs by telecommuting employees; and (2) transferring such emissions to other persons and for such purpose issuing certificates indicating the amount of such reductions. 
Requires the Secretary to ensure that the pilot program includes recommendations for carrying out the proposed program in specified geographic areas. 
Requires the Secretary to require the grantee to study and report to the Congress and the Secretary of Transportation the potential significance of the proposed program as an incentive for expanding telecommuting and reducing VMTs in the geographic areas for which the design is developed and the extent to which the program would have positive effects on transportation and air quality.

Cyber Preparedness Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to include in the National Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Center: (1) the national cybersecurity and communications integration center; and (2) the homeland security information sharing center.  The center must: (1) assist, in coordination with the center's national cybersecurity and communications integration center, fusion centers in using information relating to cybersecurity risks to develop a comprehensive and accurate threat picture; and (2) provide the center with information relating to cybersecurity risks.  The homeland security information sharing center must: (1) assist fusion centers in using information relating to cybersecurity risks to develop a comprehensive and accurate threat picture; and (2) provide the center with information relating to cybersecurity risks.  The center must also: (1) assist fusion centers in using information relating to cybersecurity risks to develop a comprehensive and accurate threat picture; and (2) provide the center with information relating to cybersecurity risks.  The bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to include the national cybersecurity and communications integration center within the National Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Center.

Veterans' Access to Child Care Act  (Sec. 2) This bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide child care assistance to a veteran who: (1) is the primary caretaker of a child or children, and (2) is receiving covered health care services from the VA or in need of covered health care services, and is, but for lack of child care services, would receive such services.  The VA shall reimburse the veteran for the cost of providing such care.  (Sec. 3) The VA shall extend the reduction in the amount of the veteran's pension for services furnished by the VA nursing facility.

Federal Agency Anti-Lobbying Act - Prohibits the use of appropriated funds for lobbying by Federal agencies until such activity has been specifically authorized by an Act of Congress and notwithstanding any other provision of law.  Makes exceptions for:  (1) the President and Vice President; (2) congressional communications; (3) public communications on views of the President for or against any pending legislative proposal; and (4) the Comptroller General's assistance in exercising the authority provided in this Act.

Public Good IRA Rollover Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from income tax distributions from individual retirement accounts (IRAs) made directly by the trustee to an IRA beneficiary or to a split-interest entity that are made on or after the date that the individual for whose benefit the account is maintained has attained age 70 1/2 and that are made from an individual retirement account which is: (1) tax-free for purposes of charitable purposes; and (2) treated as qualified charitable distributions only if no person holds an income interest in the amounts in the split-interest entity attributable to such distribution other than the individual for whose benefit such account is maintained, the spouse of such individual, or any organization described in this Act.

Defines a qualified charitable distribution as any distribution from an individual retirement account which is made directly by the trustee to an IRA beneficiary or to a split-interest entity that is made on or after the date that the individual for whose benefit the account is maintained has attained age 70 1/2 and that are made from an individual retirement account which is: (1) tax-free for purposes of charitable purposes; and (2) treated as qualified charitable distributions only if no person holds

Solar Stimulus for Job Creation and Energy Independence Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for investment in property used to manufacture equipment used to manufacture solar energy property. Defines "solar energy property" as property used to manufacture equipment used to manufacture solar energy property.

Excludes from private activity bonds the investment in solar energy property of: (1) certain loans to finance the acquisition, construction, and installation of such property; and (2) certain tax-exempt bonds issued by the Department of Energy.

Excludes from the definition of "private activity bond" any loan to finance the acquisition, construction, and installation of such property.

Excludes from the definition of "government procurement of solar energy property" any contracts for renewable energy.

Workforce Training Enhancement Act of 2016 This bill amends the Trade Act of 1974 to authorize a state to reimburse the state for the costs of providing training to a worker before the worker is approved for training under the federal trade adjustment assistance program paid by the state or local workforce development areas from the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act.

Right of Passage Community Service Act - Amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to establish a right of passage community-based after-school and summer service corps program for young people between the ages of 12 and 16.

Requires such program to offer participants service-learning curricula linked to academic goals, and opportunities to work with older AmeriCorps members who can organize service projects.

Requires such program to be carried out with assistance under the National and Community Service Act of 1990.

Requires such program to be eligible for special awards for participation in the program and service-learning curricula.

Requires the Corporation for National and Community Service to report to Congress on the program.

Health Care Liability Reform Act - Authorizes punitive damages to be awarded against a manufacturer or product seller if the claimant establishes by clear and convincing evidence that the harm suffered was the result of conduct manifesting actual malice.

Prohibits the liability of each manufacturer or product seller of the product involved in such action, with respect to harm caused by a drug or device, if the drug or device was approved under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDA) unless: (1) the manufacturer withholds from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or the health care provider withholds from a patient information relevant to the performance of the drug or device and causally related to the harm suffered; (2) the manufacturer of the drug or device withholds information relevant to the performance of the device and causally related to the harm; or (3) the amount of punitive damages that may be awarded for a claim in any civil action is not greater than twice the amount awarded for the economic injury on which such claim is based, or $250,000, whichever is greater.

Work Force Enhancement for Technology Transfer Act - Directs the Secretary of Commerce, through the Director of the Institute of Standards and Technology, to direct Regional Centers for the Transfer of Manufacturing Technology and, when established, Manufacturing Outreach Centers, to utilize, when appropriate, their expertise and capability to assist managers and other workers in U.S. manufacturing firms in effectively using and operating advanced and modern technologies. 
Directs the Secretary, through the Director and in consultation with appropriate Federal officials and with leaders of industry and labor, to assist managers and other workers in U.S. manufacturing firms in effectively utilizing and operating advanced and modern technologies.

Securing Protections for the Injured from Limitations on Liability Act - Amends the Death on the High Seas Act to provide for the recovery of damages for the care, comfort, and companionship of a seaman who dies while on the high seas.

Revises the Jones Act to provide for the recovery of damages for loss of care, comfort, and companionship in addition to other amounts authorized under the High Seas Act. Repeals the limitation on the amount of recovery for a seaman who dies while on the high seas.

Amends the Federal bankruptcy code to prohibit the trustee of a seaman's estate from selling or leasing significant property of the estate (or, if the court has jurisdiction over any affiliate of the debtor, significant property of such affiliate) unless: (1) creditors holding at least two-thirds of the claims in the estate and more than one-half in number of claims are in agreement to sell or lease the property; or (2) the court finds that sufficient property will remain in the estate or the debtor's anticipated future income will be sufficient.

Authorizes creditors holding at least two-thirds of the claims in the estate and more than one-half in number of claims to sell or lease the property.
Unemployment Assistance Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income distributions from tax-favored accounts during periods of unemployment.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax on imported crude oil and refined petroleum products.  Imposes such tax on the first sale within the United States of such products.  Exempts such tax from sale or resale requirements for the sale of such products in the United States for six months after the date of the sale.  Requires the seller of such products to receive proof that the product has been exported from the United States within the six-month period.

Psychological Kevlar Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement a plan to incorporate evidence-based preventive and early-intervention measures, practices, or procedures that reduce the likelihood that personnel in combat will develop post-traumatic stress disorder or other stress-related psychological pathologies (including substance use conditions) into: (1) basic and pre-deployment training for enlisted members, noncommissioned officers, and officers; (2) combat theater operations; and (3) post-deployment service.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) develop and implement a training program to educate and promote understanding and awareness among commissioned officers and non-commissioned officers about the signs and risks of combat stress; and (2) educate members of the Armed Forces and their families to recognize signs of combat stress, provide members pre-deployment combat stress management training, and increase outreach and access to members and their families about programs and treatment options that mitigate the negative impact of combat stress on the returning member.

Amends the Agricultural Act of 1949 to revise the grazing and wheat and feed grains provisions. Artists' Contribution to American Heritage Act of 1999 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a fair market value determination of certain literary, musical, or artistic charitable contributions created by the taxpayer.

Superfund Research, Development, and Demonstration Act of 1999 - Amends the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA) to authorize the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to enter into agreements with persons, public entities (including the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, and other Federal agencies), and nonprofit private entities, to arrange for the use of other sites appropriate for carrying out hazardous substances research, testing, evaluation, development, and demonstration projects. 
Requires each project to be carried out in a manner that is as part of a technology transfer program. 
Directs the Administrator to strive to enter into agreements with the Departments of Defense, Energy, and the Federal agencies to ensure the effective transfer to those agencies and their contractors of technologies potentially applicable to remediation or containment of hazardous substances at sites owned or operated by such agencies. 
Requires the Administrator to maintain funding for each such research center at a level not less than that funded in FY 1999 until the Administrator completes the next competitive selection process for such centers.

The bill also requires DOD to: (1) implement a discretionary spending reduction program under the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act) for FY2013, and (2) enter into multiyear procurements for authorized DOD projects.  The bill also authorizes the Department of Defense to enter into contracts for multiyear procurements that are authorized by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013.  The bill requires the Department of Defense and the military departments to enter into contracts for multiyear procurements that are authorized by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013. African Free Trade Initiative Act - Amends the African Growth and Opportunity Act to direct the President to develop a plan for negotiating and entering into one or more free trade agreements with all sub-Saharan African countries.  Directs the United States Trade Representative and Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development to consult and coordinate with the Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation regarding countries that have entered into a Millennium Challenge Compact pursuant to the Millennium Challenge Act of 2003 that have been declared eligible to enter into such a Compact for the purpose of developing and carrying out the plan required by this Act. Authorizes funds made available to the United States Agency for International Development under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to be used in consultation with the United States Trade Representative: (1) to carry out this Act, including for the deployment of resources in individual eligible countries to assist such country in the development of institutional capacities to carry it out; and (2) to coordinate the efforts of the United States to establish free trade agreements in accordance with the policy set out in this Act.

Diamond-Blackfan Anemia Research and Care Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), in coordination with the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, and the Office of Rare Diseases, to expand and intensify NIH research and related activities with regard to Diamond-Blackfan anemia.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to establish a comprehensive clinical care center for Diamond-Blackfan anemia where a majority of the patients with the disease are examined, treated, and tracked through the Registry of experts in the disease.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to establish a comprehensive clinical care center for Diamond-Blackfan anemia where a majority of the patients with the disease are examined, treated, and tracked by experts in the disease.

Amends Federal law to prohibit interring a person in any cemetery in the National Cemetery System unless a good faith effort has been made to determine that such person is not interred in any Federal cemetery or is otherwise ineligible for Federal interment. 
Amends Federal law to prohibit interring a person in military cemeteries and funeral homes without parole unless such person is convicted of a capital offense under Federal law. 
Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to prescribe regulations to ensure that a person is not interred in any cemetery in the National Cemetery System unless a good faith effort has been made to determine that such person is not otherwise ineligible for Federal interment or honors under Federal law. 
Directs the Secretary of the Army to remove the remains of Russell Wayne Wagner from Arlington National Cemetery. 
Directs the Secretary of the Army to arrange for the internment or inurnment of those remains in a public or private cemetery or, if requested, relinquish them to the next of kin of record.

Economic Fairness for Seniors Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to extend through calendar 2010: (1) the monthly premium under Medicare part B (Supplementary Medical Insurance) for 2010; and (2) certain economic recovery payments for calendar years 2009 and 2010.

Amends the American Recovery and Reinvestment Tax Act of 2009 to extend through calendar 2012: (1) the special credit for certain government retirees; and (2) the consumer price index for elderly consumers.

Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to reduce the amount of TARP ( Troubled Asset Relief Program) funds that may be allocated to the Troubled Asset Relief Program.

Colombian Temporary Protected Status Act of 2002 - Expresses the sense of Congress that Colombia qualifies for designation as a country eligible for temporary protected status under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) pursuant to which Colombian nationals would be eligible for U.S. temporary protected resident status. Deems Colombia to have been designated if it has been continuously physically present since the enactment of this Act and is admissible as an immigrant and is not ineligible for temporary protected status under the INA. Directs the Attorney General to give the prior consent to travel abroad to an alien who is granted temporary protected status pursuant to this Act, if the alien establishes to the Attorney General that emergency and extenuating circumstances beyond the control of the alien require the alien to depart for a brief, temporary trip abroad.

Authorizes the Chief of the National Guard Bureau to establish and operate up to five National Guard counterdrug schools in specified States and Puerto Rico. 
Directs the Secretary of Defense to report to the Congress on the activities of the National Guard counterdrug schools. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the Carl D. Perkins Vocational and Technical Education Act of 1998 to revise the definition of Indian student count to include the total number of Indian students enrolled in each tribally-controlled postsecondary vocational and technical institution.

Veterans TRICARE Choice Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual who is in eligible to be a covered beneficiary under the TRICARE program to elect to be ineligible to enroll in the program. Allows such an individual to make an election later during a special enrollment period.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to ensure that a covered beneficiary who makes such an election is maintained on the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System, or successor system, regardless of whether the individual is eligible for the TRICARE program during the period of such election.

Requires the Secretary to submit to the congressional defense and appropriations committees a report on elections by covered individuals that includes: (1) the number of such individuals who are ineligible to enroll in the TRICARE program pursuant to an election; and (2) the number of such individuals who made such an election but, as of the report, are enrolled in the TRICARE program pursuant to a change of election.

American Worker Mobility Act of 2014 - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to grant a relocation subsidy to an individual who: (1) is totally unemployed and has been totally unemployed for at least 26 consecutive weeks; (2) has exhausted all rights to regular compensation under the law of a State or Federal law with respect to a benefit year (excluding any benefit year ending before July 1, 2008); (3) has not received a relocation subsidy in the two-year period preceding such date of application; and (4) is able to work, available to work, and actively seeking work.  Prohibits the Secretary from granting a relocation subsidy to an individual under this Act unless: (1) the subsidy will assist the individual in relocating within the United States, at least 60 miles from the individual's current residence, to obtain employment; (2) the individual filed an application with the Secretary before January 1, 2019; and (3) the individual has obtained a bona fide offer of suitable employment affording a reasonable expectation of long-term duration in the area in which the individual wishes to relocate or wishes to relocate to an area that has an unemployment rate that is at least 2%

Native American Commercial Driving Training and Technical Assistance Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to provide grants to tribal colleges or universities and private truck-agencies to provide training and certificates to Native Americans who are members of an Indian tribe or who are indigenous to the United States. Requires the Secretary to give priority to grant applications that: (1) propose training that exceeds proposed minimum standards for training Department of Transportation (DOT) tractor-trailer drivers; (2) propose training that exceeds the entry level truck driver certification standards set by the Professional Truck Driver Institute; and (3) propose an education partnership with a private trucking firm, trucking association, or similar entity to ensure the effectiveness of the grant program.

Prescription Drug Labeling Promotion Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a working group to develop and promulgate guidance on best practices for access to prescription drug labeling for the visually impaired.

Requires the working group to: (1) include representatives of national organizations representing blind and visually impaired individuals, the elderly, and industry groups representing stakeholders; and (2) be divided equally between consumer and industry advocates.

Requires the working group to: (1) promulgate best practices for labels, including for prescribers, in the Federal Register and on the HHS website, and (2) conduct an informational and educational program to inform the public and pharmacists about such best practices.

Directs the Comptroller General to review the guidance and report on the extent to which pharmacies are complying with such best practices and barriers to accessible prescription drug labeling for blind and visually impaired individuals.

Religious Liberty and Charitable Donation Protection Act of 1997 - Amends Federal law to provide that charitable contributions are not covered by the provisions of the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993 (RFRA). 
Sets forth provisions regarding trustee and successor duties of creditors and purchasers of charitable contributions. 
Provides that a transfer of a charitable contribution to a qualified religious or charitable entity or organization shall not be considered to be a transfer under RFRA if the amount of the contribution does not exceed 15 percent of the debtor's gross annual income. 
Prohibits the court, in making a determination whether to dismiss a case under this Act, from taking into consideration whether a debtor has made, or continues to make, charitable contributions to any qualified religious or charitable entity or organization. 
Prohibits the court from taking into consideration whether a debtor has made, or continues to make, charitable contributions to any such entity or organization in the amount of:  (1) 548(d) charitable contributions (that meet the definition of "charitable contribution" under RFRA); or (2) 707 charitable contributions (that meet the definition of "charitable contribution" under RFRA).

Federal Credit Cost Reduction Act of 1994 - Amends the Federal Credit Reform Act of 1990 to provide for the treatment of administrative costs in the President's annual budget submission.

Provides for the treatment of administrative costs in the President's annual budget submission in the same manner as the treatment of administrative costs in the President's annual budget submission for the credit reform program loans and loan guarantees. 
Provides for the treatment of administrative costs in the President's annual budget submission in the same manner as the treatment of administrative costs in the President's annual budget submission for the credit reform program direct loans and loan guarantees.

Requires the USTR to determine whether a foreign country is in compliance with ATPRIP or URGIA when a dispute is initiated with respect to a product covered by ATPRIP or the URGIA. Amends the Caribbean Basin Economic Recovery Act to require the USTR to ensure a timely review and disposition of requests from an interested party that the President reconsider the status of a country as a beneficiary country under ATPRIP or URGIA. Syrian War Crimes Accountability Act of 2014 - Expresses the support of Congress for the people of Syria seeking democratic change and for a U.S.  intervention in Syria and the international community's response to such need.  Directs the Secretary of State to report to Congress on war crimes and crimes against humanity in Syria.

Veterans Life Insurance Opportunity Act of 1998 - Makes any person whose Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance was continued in force after termination of duty or discharge from service under the law as in effect prior to the date on which the Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance program became effective and terminated less than four years prior to such date eligible within one year from the effective date of the Program to apply for and be granted a term period of five years in an amount equal to the amount of the insured's Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance which was not converted to an individual policy under prior law.  Allows any person who did not convert coverage within such period to apply for (within the 20-month period beginning on the last day of such period of separation provided for under this Act) and be granted coverage in an amount equal to the amount of the insured's Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance which was not converted to an individual policy under prior law.  Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide for notice to any member of the uniformed services who purchased a Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance policy and who did not convert such policy to a Veterans' Group Life Insurance policy of the same term and coverage.

Mortgage Insurance Fairness Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to treat mortgage insurance premiums as interest and to phase out the amount of such deduction for taxpayers with adjusted gross incomes exceeding $100,000 ($500 for a married individual filing a separate return). 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to prescribe regulations for the return of mortgage interest received from any individual.

International Rule of Law and Antiterrorism Act of 2003 - Directs the President to: (1) direct the U.S. Permanent Representative to the United Nations to establish negotiations with the United Nations (UN) and UN member states to establish a professional United Nations civilian police corps; and (2) request the Secretary of State to work with the United Nations Secretariat and other UN member states to establish standards and training programs for international civilian police. Expresses the sense of Congress that a professional UN civilian police corps should be composed of the appropriate number of law enforcement professionals trained and equipped for civilian policing functions in UN international peace operations and available for rapid deployment.

Directs the President to report to specified congressional committees on progress of negotiations to establish such corps.

Protecting Seniors' Medicare Choices from Obamacare Act of 2014 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to eliminate the enhanced Medicaid FMAP for prisoners and apply savings to the 2015 Medicare Advantage (MA) stabilization program.  Establishes a Medicare Advantage (MA) stabilization program under which the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) shall provide a PMPM (pre-existing condition monitoring and reporting) stabilization funding amount to each Medicare Advantage (MA) plan to be used by such plan for plan year 2015 to address the beneficiary plan inadequacies applicable to such plan. Requires the Secretary to distribute such funding to each eligible MA plan not later than: (1) October 15, 2014, if the plan satisfies specified criteria for eligibility, and (2) by no later than October 15, 2014, if the plan does not satisfy such criteria. Requires the Secretary to determine which Medicare Advantage plans are eligible Medicare Advantage plans and the PMPM stabilization funding amount to be distributed to each such eligible MA plan by no later than October 15, 2014.

Hygiene Assistance for Families of Infants and Toddlers Act of 2017 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to make grants to eligible entities to conduct demonstration projects to help families with eligible children to address the diapering needs of such children.  Eligible entities are: (1) states or local governmental entities; (2) Indian tribes or tribal organizations; or (3) nonprofit organizations.  A "diaper" is an absorbent garment that is washable or disposable that is worn by a child who is not toilet-trained.

The President may waive such sanctions if: (1) the person is subject to a sanctions regime under its governing foreign law that requires it to eliminate the knowing provision of such messaging services to, and the knowing enabling and facilitation of direct or indirect access to such messaging services for, the Central Bank of the PRK, any financial institution, and any person; (2) the person has terminated the knowing provision of such messaging services to

Requires the data system developed and implemented under this Act to be readily and easily accessible as follows: (1) to any Foreign Service officer responsible for the issuance of visas; (2) to any Federal agent responsible for determining the admissibility of an alien to the United States; and (3) to any Federal agent responsible for determining the inadmissibility of an alien to the United States.
Requires the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, and the Director to establish procedures to restrict access to information in the data system under such circumstances.

Mary Jo Lawyer Spano Mesothelioma Patient Registry Act of 2015 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry to develop a patient registry to collect data on mesothelioma, including information with respect to the incidence and prevalence of the disease in the United States. The agency must use the registry to: (1) enhance and expand infrastructure and activities for tracking the epidemiology of mesothelioma patients; (2) collect, consolidate, and report on health information on mesothelioma patients; (3) better describe the incidence and prevalence of mesothelioma in the United States; (4) facilitate further research on mesothelioma; (5) examine factors that may be associated with mesothelioma; (6) outline key demographic factors associated with mesothelioma; and (7) make the information in the registry available to the public to facilitate and enhance research on, and the prevention and treatment of, mesothelioma. The agency must also make information in and analysis derived from the registry available to the public, including researchers.

Amends the Federal criminal code to provide for the availability of appropriated funds to the Department of Defense (DOD) for the payment of costs incurred by the National Guard in conducting international military-to-civilian contacts, civilian-to-civilian contacts, and comparable activities for purposes as follows:  (1) to support the objectives of the commander of the combatant command for the theater of operations in which such contacts and activities are conducted; (2) to build international civil-military partnerships and capacity; (3) to strengthen cooperation between the Departments of Defense and the Federal agencies of the Governments of the United States and foreign Governments; (4) to facilitate intergovernmental collaboration between the U.S. and foreign governments; (5) to facilitate and enhance the exchange of information between the U.S. and foreign governments on matters relating to defense and security; and (6) to facilitate and enhance the exchange of information between the U.S. and foreign governments on matters relating to defense and security.

Family Farmer Bankruptcy Clarification Act of 2013 - Amends federal bankruptcy law to allow a governmental unit of a bankruptcy estate to discharge a claim by a governmental unit based on the disposition of any property used in the debtor's farming operation.  Defines a "government" as a person, estate, or legal entity.  Provides that the claim shall be considered an unsecured claim arising before the filing of the petition, and shall not be entitled to priority under the bankruptcy code.  Provides for the treatment of claims by a governmental unit of a kind described in this Act.

Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to require the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to study and report to Congress on: (1) the impact of state and local benchmarking and disclosure policies and building efficiency programs on commercial and multifamily buildings; and (2) best practice policy approaches that have resulted in the greatest improvements in building energy efficiency.

Requires the Secretary to maintain a database to store and make publicly available information on commercial and multifamily buildings.

Encouraging Mortgage Modifications Act of 2008 - Amends the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act of 1974 to require a servicer of pooled qualified residential mortgages: (1) owed any duty to determine if the net present value of the payments on the loan, as modified, is greater than the anticipated net recovery that would result from foreclosure to all investors and parties having a direct or indirect interest in the pooled loans or securitization vehicle, but not individual party or group of parties; and (2) acts in the best interests of all such investors and parties, if the servicer agrees to or implements a qualified loan modification or workout plan for a qualified residential mortgage, taking other reasonable loss mitigation actions, including accepting partial payments or short sale of the property.

Defines "qualified loan modification or workout plan" as a contract, modification, or plan relating to a qualified residential mortgage loan consummated on or after January 1, 2004, with respect to which: (1) payment default on the loan or loans has occurred, is imminent, or is reasonably foreseeable; (2) the dwelling securing the loan or loans is the primary residence of the owner; (3) the servicer reasonably believes that the anticipated recovery under the

District of Columbia College Access Improvement Act of 2002 - Amends the District of Columbia College Access Act of 1999 to revise the requirements for the receipt of Federal assistance under such Act.Requires the Mayor of the District of Columbia to establish a dedicated account for the programs under such Act consisting of specified amounts.Prohibits the District of Columbia government from exceeding the aggregate amount authorized for the programs for any fiscal year.

American Heroes Act - Requires each state to provide one statue of an individual representing that state which shall be displayed in the Capitol Visitor Center. 
Directs the Clerk of the House and the Secretary of the Senate to jointly assign to one of their employees the post of the American Hero Administrator, with such term as agreed upon by the Clerk and the Secretary. 
Requires the American Hero Commission to choose, by a majority vote, the individual whose statue will represent the state. 
Directs the Architect of the Capitol to procure and install a statue honoring the passengers of United Airlines flight number 93 who died on September 11, 2001, for their heroic role in protecting Washington, D.C. from attack. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Fair Wage Act This bill amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to increase the minimum wage to: (1) $8.00 an hour beginning 30 days after enactment of this Act, or $9.00 an hour beginning one year after such date; (2) $10.00 an hour beginning two years after such date; (3) $12.00 an hour beginning three years after such date; (4) $13.00 an hour beginning five years after such date; (5) $14.00 an hour beginning six years after such date; (6) $15.00 an hour beginning seven years after such date; and (7) beginning eight years after such date, and annually thereafter, the amount determined. The Department of Labor shall determine the minimum wage for the following year based on the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers for the most recent month, quarter, or year available. The bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers a tax credit for 6.2% of wages paid to employees who are less than $15 per hour.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for $1,000 of the cost of a qualified mentor's services. Limits such credit to $2,000 for taxpayers who are under age 22 and who have the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year.

National Guard Investigations Transparency and Improvement Act of 2014 - Establishes the Office of Complex Administrative Investigations in the Chief of the National Guard Bureau (the Office). Directs the Office to undertake complex administrative investigations of matters relating to members of the National Guard when in state status, including investigations of sexual assault involving a member of the National Guard in such status. Requires the Chief of the National Guard to treat any final report of the Office on a matter under this Act as if such report were the report of an Inspector General of the Department of Defense or a military department on such matter. Requires the Chief to submit annual reports to Congress on such investigations. Directs the Chief to ensure that the Office maintains the personnel and other capabilities necessary for its discharge.
Directs the Customs Service to reliquidate certain entries made on or after December 1, 1993, and before April 1, 2001, for certain purposes.

Home Health Care Planning Improvement Act of 2007 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a physician, or a nurse practitioner or clinical nurse specialist who is working in collaboration with a physician in accordance with state law, or a certified nurse-midwife as authorized by state law, or a physician assistant under the supervision of a physician, to be a member of a Home Health Care Planning Improvement Committee.

Requires a physician, or a nurse practitioner or clinical nurse specialist who is working in collaboration with a certified nurse-midwife, or a physician assistant, to be a member of a Home Health Care Planning Improvement Committee.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a limited increase in the amount of the tax credit for investment in advanced nuclear power facilities. Allocates such credit to facilities placed in service before enactment of this Act.

Strengthening Community Safety Act of 2010 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to authorize the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to make grants to an eligible first responder agency for the costs of operating an additional cost of 1 or more employees who are reservists being placed on active duty.

Prohibits the Administrator from making such grants for costs relating to an employee being placed on active duty if federal funds are used, in whole or in part, for the pay or benefits of the employee.

Allows grants to be used for: (1) pay and benefits for an individual hired to replace an employee placed on active duty; (2) overtime expenses for an employee that performs tasks that would have been performed by an employee placed on active duty; and (3) the cost of equipment, maintenance, or other activities the eligible first responder agency was unable to acquire or perform because of the cost of replacing an employee placed on active duty or the need for which was caused by the employee being placed on active duty.

Requires the Administrator to report to Congress on the placing on active duty of employees of first responder agencies that are reservists, including an evaluation of the effects of the employees' being on active duty

Temporary IRA Distribution Suspension Act of 2008 - Suspends, for calendar 2008 through 2009, the requirement that distributions from a defined contribution plan be made in the form of an iras (individual retirement account), unless the plan has been amended to require distributions to be made from a qualified retirement plan.

Gas Pump Access Act of 2016 This bill requires a gas station or convenience store to provide equal access for a person with a disability to a gas pump if the person with a disability requests a gas pump without charge a gas station or convenience store may not charge a person with a disability a service charge. The bill also prohibits a local government from adopting an ordinance that expands the accessibility, safety, or availability of fueling assistance to a motor vehicle operator with a disability.

Directs the Speaker of the House of Representatives from the House Committee on International Relations and the Judiciary to appoint to the Intellectual Property Assembly of the Americas (IPAA) a United States Delegation of at least 7 Members.  Authorizes appropriations. 
Directs the Chairperson of the House Committee on Foreign Relations and the Vice Chairperson of the Judiciary to submit annual reports to Congress.

Federal Employees' Compensation Reform Act of 2011 - Amends federal law to terminate the payment of compensation under the Federal Employees' Compensation and Retirement System (FERS) to a covered employee who is eligible for an annuity under FERS or the Federal Employees' Retirement System (FERS) after attaining retirement age.

Directs the employing agency of a covered employee to file an application for an annuity with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) in accordance with this Act.

Requires the agency to file an application for an annuity for a covered employee who is eligible for an annuity under FERS or FERS and who is a covered employee as defined under this Act.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to prescribe regulations to carry out this Act.

Caribbean National Forest Wild and Scenic Rivers Act of 2002 - Amends the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate specified river segments as wild and scenic rivers of the Caribbean National Forest, Puerto Rico, and the Rio Mameyes, as well as as a recreational river.Preserves the Commonwealth's authority to make such river designation.

Import Control and Safe Handling of Spent Nuclear Fuel Act of 1995 - Prohibits the importation into the United States of spent nuclear fuel unless:  (1) the Congress has approved a repository or repositories with the capacity to store or dispose of all spent nuclear fuel generated by commercial nuclear reactors in the United States; (2) the appropriate Federal agency or agencies have licensed such repositories for such purpose; and (3) the repository or repositories are operating. 
Prohibits the use of such prohibited materials in national security and export control zones. 
Authorizes the President to notify the House Committee on Intelligence and the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence of the House and the Senate at least three days in advance of the arrival of the fuel. 
Prohibits the use of such prohibited materials in the handling of nuclear materials.

Colonias Improvement Act of 2014 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to issue a proposed rule containing a definition of "colonia" that is the same for each program and that is limited to a community that: (1) is located within 75 miles of the border between the United States and Mexico, or (2) has applied for or received funding under a covered program before this Act's enactment.  Directs the Administrator to ensure that the final rule takes effect within one year.  Directs the Administrator, the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), and the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to establish and regularly update a website that: (1) serves as a clearinghouse for information relating to the covered programs, and (2) includes links to specific information to assist state and local governments in carrying out such programs.  Directs the Administrator to establish a working group to review covered programs, record information relating to each award made under a covered program, and hold public hearings relating to covered programs.  Directs the Administrator to submit to Congress a report that includes recommendations for improving the economic and social development of colonias and the application process for covered programs. Health Care Consumer Protection Act of 1995 - Requires an insurer providing health insurance coverage under a health plan to provide annual notice to each current enrollee regarding the extent of the plan coverage.  Requires such notice to include a copy of the contract between the insurer and enrollee, in addition to information regarding the terms and conditions of the policy and the rights and obligations of the parties. 
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to promulgate regulations to ensure that an insurer providing health insurance coverage under a health plan provide notification to current and potential enrollees as specified. 
Sets forth civil penalties for entities that offer health plans that violate this Act.

Small Business Reform Act of 2010 or the Not Too Small to Succeed in Business Act of 2010 - Amends the Small Business Act to extend the eligibility period of a small business concern for participation in the Small Business Administration (SBA) program for which the small business concerned was eligible to participate before enactment of this Act.

Allows small businesses that graduated from the SBA program under the Small Business Act before enactment of this Act and that are otherwise eligible to participate in the program but that meet specified requirements to participate after enactment of this Act, to participate for up to one year after enactment of this Act.

Increases the maximum net worth of a small business concerned for eligibility as a Program Participant and continues to be eligible after admission to participate in the program for up to one year after enactment of this Act.

Pharmaceutical Supply and Value Enhancement Act or the Pharmaceutical SAVE Act This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to authorize importation of a drug for up to three years if the drug is: (1) a drug subject to certain provisions regarding the temporary importation of prescription drugs, (2) authorized to be lawfully marketed in one or more of the countries included in the list of specified drug manufacturers, and (3) located in the United States. The FDA may deny importation of a drug if it is not safe and effective, is used in conjunction with a device for which there is no reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness, or the authorization to market the drug in one or more of the countries included in the list has been rescinded or withdrawn because of any concern relating to the safety or effectiveness of the drug.

Continuity of Electric Capacity Resources Act - Amends the Federal Power Act to direct the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to submit to each transmission organization a report that includes provisions addressing the procurement of electric capacity resources notice that the transmission organization is required to file with FERC.

Requires the report to identify electric capacity resources that are available to the organization and to describe the operational characteristics of those resources.

Requires the organization to: (1) evaluate, using generally accepted metrics, the financial health, viability, and projected remaining years of service of the available electric capacity resources; (2) identify over the short and long-term periods in the planning cycle of the organization's transmission; (3) identify the projected future needs of the organization for electric capacity resources; and (4) assess the current and projected status of the reliability of the elements of the bulk-power system, over the long- and short-term periods, as determined by the regional reliability coordinator.

Requires the organization to: (1) have been made available to members of the organization and to the public for comment; and (2) have been given the option to comment on specified tariff amendments.

Preservation of Access to Osteoporosis Testing for Medicare Beneficiary Act of 2011 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to extend the minimum payment for bone mass measurement through 2013.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow individual taxpayers a tax credit for the purchase of an automobile or light truck that is: (1) the original use of which commences with the taxpayer, (2) acquired for use or lease by the taxpayer and not for resale, and (3) made by a manufacturer.

Cameron Gulbransen Kids and Cars Safety Act of 2003 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to: (1) evaluate devices and technologies intended to reduce the incidence of child injury and child death occurring outside of parked motor vehicles in nontraffic, noncrash events, including backing-over incidents, that are caused by such vehicles; and (2) report to Congress on the evaluation.Requires the Secretary to: (1) establish a database of, and collect data regarding, the numbers and types of injuries and deaths in nontraffic, noncrash events involving motor vehicles; and (2) evaluate available technologies for detecting and preventing collisions with individuals and objects behind motor vehicles, with respect to the accuracy, effectiveness, cost, and feasibility of installation of such technologies in a wide variety of motor vehicles.Requires the Secretary to prescribe motor vehicle safety standards that require the installation of devices for detecting, and providing to operators of such a vehicle a warning of, individuals and objects behind the motor vehicle to: (1) ensure that operation of power windows, power window switches, and power sunroofs cannot result in deaths and injuries; and (2) require inclusion with power windows and power sunroofs of child-safe switches and auto reverse technology.

Cocopah Lands Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to take specified lands in Yuma County, Arizona, into trust for the Cocopah Indian Tribe of Arizona if the Tribe transfers title to such lands to the Secretary.  Requires the land taken into trust to be considered to be part of the Tribe's initial reservation.  Prohibits the use of such land for gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

Plan B for Plan B Act of 2005 - Requires the Commissioner of Food and Drugs to approve or disapprove the supplemental new drug application for Plan B (a new generic of the over-the-counter drug product emergency contraception) as amended by the non-approvable letter dated May 6, 2004, from Women's Capital Corporation, controlled by Barr Pharmaceuticals, to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Uterine Fibroid Research and Education Act of 2003 - Requires the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to expand, intensify, and coordinate programs for the conduct and support of uterine fibroids research. Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to develop and disseminate uterine fibroids information to the public.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Administrator of the Health Resources and Services Administration, to develop and disseminate uterine fibroids information to health care providers.

Directs the Attorney General to prescribe regulations governing the storage and keeping of such materials by State and local law enforcement agencies. Bond Transparency Act of 2014 - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to require brokers, dealers, and municipal securities dealers that effect a riskless principal transaction to disclose to the customer, in writing, the amount of the difference between: (1) the customer's purchase price and the broker's, dealer's, or municipal securities dealer's purchase price; or (2) the customer's sale price and the broker's, dealer's, or municipal securities dealer's sale price. Alisa's Law of 2014 - Amends the federal criminal code to require a state to install an ignition interlock device in a vehicle while intoxicated to prevent repeat intoxication driving.

Foreign Investment Transparency and Security Act of 2006 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to limit foreign government control of certain critical infrastructure investments to the establishment or operation of a foreign owned general business corporation that meets certain requirements.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to report to Congress on the processes and policies for implementation of a scanning system for 100% of the inbound maritime containers described in this Act.

Bond Financing Renewal Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the amount of qualified small issue bonds permitted for capital expenditures; (2) define "manufacturing facility" for purposes of such provisions; and (3) allow the acquisition of such bonds without the requirement that the proceeds be used to provide such facilities.

Freedom and Human Rights for the Enclaved People of Cyprus Act - Directs the President to: (1) inform the United Nations (UN), foreign governments, and the appropriate U.S. Departments and Agencies of the Government of the restrictions on the enclaved people of Cyprus; (2) enlist the UN and foreign governments in efforts to end such restrictions; and (3) establish U.S. Government programs of assistance to the enclaved people of Cyprus.

Directs the President to use funds allocated for a fiscal year to the government or ethnic community participating directly or indirectly in imposition of such restrictions to assist such people or to establish a foreign assistance program for such people.

Directs the President to: (1) notify in writing each fiscal year the head of government of any foreign country that is participating in the restrictions on freedom and human rights of the enclaved people of Cyprus; and (2) urge the head of such government to cease such restrictions and to work to eliminate such restrictions.

Directs the Secretary of State to include a report on Cyprus as part of the Department of State's annual Country Reports on Human Rights Practices.

Authorizes the President to enact a joint budget resolution (or, if the joint budget resolution is enacted within 15 days after the joint budget resolution, a concurrent budget resolution) before the end of such fiscal year.  Prohibits the joint budget resolution content from being treated in the House of Representatives or in the Senate as a budget resolution or a conference report on a budget resolution.  Requires the joint budget resolution to be considered in the House and Senate as enforceable upon enactment or 15 days following presentment to the President, whichever occurs earlier. Meat Promotion Act of 2005 - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a voluntary program of country of origin labeling for ground beef, ground pork, ground lamb, and fresh muscle cuts of beef, pork, and lamb.

Prohibits the Secretary from designating a covered meat product as having the United States as the country of origin unless the meat product is derived exclusively from: (1) an animal born, raised, and slaughtered in the United States; or (2) an animal born and raised in Alaska or Hawaii, transported for a period not to exceed 60 days outside of those States, and slaughtered in the United States.

Authorizes the Secretary to require participants in the program to maintain a recordkeeping audit trail that will permit the Secretary to verify compliance with the program.

Authorizes the Secretary to assess a civil penalty against a participant in the program for intentionally or knowingly violating program requirements.

Agricultural Credit Act of 2001 - Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to revise the definition of "debt forgiveness" to exclude: (1) consolidation, rescheduling, or deferral of a loan; (2) a write-down during the lifetime of the borrower that is due to a financial problem of the borrower relating to a natural disaster or a medical condition of the borrower or an immediate family member of the borrower; or (3) any write-down provided as part of a resolution of a discrimination complaint against the Secretary of Agriculture.Authorizes the Secretary to make direct or guaranteed farm operating loans for paying annual farm or ranch operating expenses of a borrower who: (1) was restructured with a write-down under this Act; or (2) is current on payments under a confirmed reorganization plan under chapter 11, 12, or 13 of the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) of the United States. Sets forth provisions regarding: (1) allocation of certain funds for socially disadvantaged farmers and ranchers; (2) allotments for jointly advantageous farmers and ranchers; and (3) the percentage of recapture for shared appreciation arrangements.

PTSD/TBI Guaranteed Review For Heroes Act - Directs the Secretary of Defense to establish within the Office of the Secretary of Defense a special review board to review the discharge or dismissal (other than a general court-martial) of a covered individual who: (1) was deployed in support of a contingency operation; (2) was discharged or dismissed from the Armed Forces under a general or other than honorable condition; and (3) has been diagnosed by a health care professional with post-traumatic stress disorder or a traumatic brain injury.

Requires the Secretary concerned, if a physician, clinical psychologist, psychiatrist, or other appropriate health care professional determines that a member who was deployed in support of a contingency operation has (or may have) post-traumatic stress disorder or a traumatic brain injury, to: (1) refer such member for evaluation by a physical evaluation board; and (2) if the board determines that the member is unfit to perform his or her duties, grade, rank, or rating because of such post-traumatic stress disorder or traumatic brain injury, to retire or separate the member.

Prohibits a person from holding a gun show unless the person is licensed to do so under this Act and at least 30 days have elapsed since the person, using a prescribed form, notified the Secretary of the department in which the gun show is to be held. 
Requires the Secretary to approve an application submitted to the Secretary for a license to hold a gun show.  Requires the Secretary to establish to ensure that the fees collected are sufficient to cover the costs of issuing licenses, including the costs of issuing a license to a licensed dealer. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) the Secretary's authority to deny an application or submit a complaint to the Secretary for enforcement; and (2) penalties for violations of this Act.
Obamacare Marriage Penalty Elimination Act This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to eliminate the marriage penalty in the case of a joint return.

Canyon Mountain Land Conveyance Act of 2013 - Requires the United States to hold in trust for the benefit of the Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians and the Oregon and California Railroad up to 17,826 acres of federal land in the Coos Bay District, Oregon, for the development of a public domain land management area.  Requires the Secretary of the Interior to complete a survey of the boundary lines to establish the boundaries of the land.  Requires the Secretary to file a map and legal description of the federal land with the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives.  Requires the map and legal description to have the same force and effect as if included in this Act, except that the Secretary may correct any clerical or typographical errors.  Requires the map and legal description to be filed and available for public inspection in the Office of the Secretary.  Prohibits federal law relating to the export of unprocessed logs harvested from federal land from being used for any gaming activity carried out under Public Law 100-497 (25 U.S.C. 2701 et seq).
