Election Jamming Prevention Act of 2006 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit the use of any telecommunication device (other than a cell phone or landline telephone) to annoy, abuse, threaten, or harass any person at the called number or who receives the communications.

Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit the use of any telecommunication device (other than a cell phone or landline telephone) to prevent or obstruct the broadcast or exchange of election-related information.

Authorizes any person aggrieved by a violation of such prohibition to bring a civil action or other proper proceeding for injunctive or declaratory relief in any court of competent jurisdiction, including an application in a U.S. district court.

Healthy Maternity and Obstetric Medicine Act or the Healthy MOM Act This bill amends the Public Health Service Act and the Internal Revenue Code to require health insurance issuers to allow pregnant women a special enrollment period for coverage under certain health benefits. The bill also amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require a group health plan to allow an eligible employee who is not enrolled in a plan under the terms of which the employee works or studies a special enrollment period for coverage under the plan.

Continuity of Congress Act of 2003 - Authorizes the legislature of each State to enact laws declaring who shall serve in the place of members of the House of Representatives and the Senate as necessary to the State in the event that one-fourth of the members of the House or Senate are killed or incapacitated.

Earmark Reform and Federal Spending Transparency and Accountability Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit any earmark beneficiary from making more than $5,000 of any election year in any odd-numbered year and $5,000 in any even-numbered year of a congressionally directed spending item that benefits the beneficiary.

Defines "earmark beneficiary" as any person who specifically requests and benefits from a congressionally directed spending item, limited tax benefit, or limited tariff benefit (as defined in rule XLIV of the Standing Rules of the Senate, determined by substituting Senator or Member for Senator in such paragraph in such case).

Requires the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House to post on the public website of their respective chambers a link to the earmark database maintained by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).

Requires the head of each federal department and agency to post on the public website of that department or agency a link to a searchable database that lists each expenditure made by the agency listing with respect to the expenditure the amount, purpose, term, and office making the expenditure.

Supporting Emergency Responders Volunteer Efforts Act of 2009 or the SERVE Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for $1,000 of the annual salary of a bona fide volunteer member of a volunteer emergency response organization. Defines "bona fide volunteer member of a qualified volunteer emergency response organization" as an individual who: (1) at any time during the taxable year is a bona fide volunteer member of a qualified volunteer emergency response organization; and (2) has served for more than six months in such organization and provided more than 40 hours of service.

Fuel-Efficient Fleets Act of 2006 - Amends Federal transportation law to require each new passenger automobile purchased, or leased for at least 60 consecutive days, by an executive agency after the date of enactment of this Act to achieve a minimum fuel economy of: (1) not less than 15 miles per gallon; (2) not less than 20 miles per gallon; (3) not less than 24 miles per gallon; and (4) not less than 36 miles per gallon.

Requires the Secretary of Energy to annually evaluate the fuel economy standards under this Act.

Authorizes the Secretary to award grants to assist States to purchase vans, trucks, sport utility vehicles, minivans, or passenger automobiles that meet the fuel economy requirements for new Federal fleet vehicles.

Taxation of Minor Children Simplifcation Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for a tax on the net unearned income of minor children. Includes as a parent of such children an election to claim income of such children on the parent's tax return.

Strengthening Child Welfare Response to Trafficking Act of 2014 - Amends the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act to revise requirements for State child protective services (CWS) reporting requirements.  Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to report to Congress on the specific type and prevalence of severe forms of trafficking in persons to which children who are identified for services or intervention under the placement, care, or supervision of state, Indian tribe, or tribal organization child welfare agencies have been subjected as of enactment of this Act.  Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on the practices and protocols utilized by states to identify and serve children who are victims of trafficking.

Health Care COBRA OffSet Tax Savings Act of 2005 or the Health Care COSTS Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a refundable tax credit for 50 percent of the premium paid for COBRA continuation coverage for individuals.

Requires the Secretary of Labor to prescribe regulations which permit individuals to assign the credit to the administrator of the plan under which COBRA continuation coverage is provided.

Provides for the change in COBRA notice provisions with respect to individuals who become entitled to elect COBRA continuation coverage after the enactment of this Act.

Enhanced Emergency and Enforcement Authority Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and the Securities Act of 1933 to revise emergency orders related to compliance with securities laws in a timely, orderly, or efficient manner. 
Amends the Securities Act of 1933 to revise the nationwide service of process provisions. 
Amends the Investment Company Act of 1940 to revise the nationwide service of process provisions. 
Amends the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 to revise the nationwide service of process provisions.

Safe Medications for the Elderly Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of certain pharmaceutical care services furnished by a pharmacist who is legally authorized to furnish such services under State law or the State regulatory mechanism provided by State law.

Elgin's Law - Requires health care professionals, in the case of a covered individual who is being treated for mental illness, to disclose to a parent (if any) of the individual's mental illness and treatment for mental illness as may be useful for the appropriate parent's involvement with respect to the treatment. Exempts such disclosures in exceptional circumstances where the parent's involvement would be counter-productive to the treatment.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to post information on HHS websites as to this Act's requirements on the public and health care professionals to inform the public and health care professionals on the treatment of a minor child who is being treated for mental illness.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 50% of the cost of the installation of a qualified hydrogen-powered vehicle refueling property. Defines "qualified hydrogen-powered vehicle refueling property" as any property (not including a building and its structural components) for the production, storage, or dispensing of hydrogen fuel into the fuel tank of a motor vehicle propelled by such fuel. Terminates such credit after 2013.Excludes income from the sale of hydrogen fuel sold at retail for use in a hydrogen fuel cell vehicle from the gross income of taxpayers. Terminates such exclusion after 2013.

Energy Savings Through Public-Private Partnerships Act of 2013 - Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require each federal agency to: (1) implement identified energy efficiency measures that are life cycle cost-effective; and (2) use the benchmarking systems selected or developed for the agency to track energy savings realized through the implementation of such measures. Requires the agency to use the systems to: (1) track energy savings realized through the implementation of such measures, and (2) report on progress made in achieving the goal of implementing energy-saving or conservation measures. Requires the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to report to Congress on the progress made in achieving the goal.

Drunk Driving Repeat Offender Prevention Act of 2015 This bill amends the federal criminal code to establish a three-year requirement that a state enact and enforce a law that requires the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence. The bill also requires the Department of Justice (DOJ) to withhold 1% of the amount of funds authorized to be appropriated to a state for FY2018 and FY2019 if the state does not meet the three-year requirement. If the state does not meet the three-year requirement within such time period, DOJ shall withhold the funds that remain available for apportionment to the state.

Small Business Expansion and Job Creation Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2010: (1) the increased limitation on the expensing of depreciable business assets; and (2) the special depreciation allowance for certain property acquired during 2010.

Allows taxpayers who previously elected acceleration of the alternative minimum tax (AMT) and who did not make such election in its first taxable year to elect not to have this Act's special rules for 2010 extension of property apply to 2010 extension property. Allows taxpayers who did not make such election to elect to have such a rule in applying it to their first taxable year ending after December 31, 2009, and each subsequent taxable year, and if they make such election only to apply such rule to eligible 2010 extension property.

A violation of this bill shall be treated as a violation of the Federal Trade Commission Act.  It shall be unlawful to market or advertise, on any medium of electronic communications, for the sale of any of the following:   a firearm receiver casting or firearm receiver blank that does not meet the definition of a firearm in specified federal firearms provisions, and that after purchase by a consumer can be completed by the consumer to the point at which such casting or blank functions as a firearm frame or receiver for a semiautomatic assault weapon or machine gun.   A violation of this bill shall be treated as a violation of a rule defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice described under the Federal Trade Commission Act. Academic, Social, and Emotional Learning Act of 2011 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (ESEA) to require teachers and principals to train teachers and principals in practices that have demonstrated effectiveness in improving student achievement, attainment, and behavior through addressing the social and emotional development needs of students.

Requires such training to include addressing the social and emotional development needs of students to improve student achievement and attainment, such as through social and emotional learning programming.

Requires such training to address the social and emotional development needs of students to improve student achievement and attainment, such as through social and emotional learning programming.

Requires such training to: (1) integrate social and emotional learning into school curriculum; (2) provide systematic instruction whereby social and emotional skills are taught, modeled, practiced, and applied so that students use them as part of their daily behavior; (3) teach children to apply social and emotional skills to prevent specific problem behaviors such as substance use, violence, bullying, and school failure, and to promote positive behaviors in class, school, and community activities; and (4) establish safe and caring learning environments that foster student participation, engagement, and connection to learning and school.
Amends Federal civil service law to extend the probationary period for positions within the competitive service.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to reduce the federal personal income tax rate through calendar 2006.

Great Lakes Navigation System Sustainability Act of 2013 - Directs the Secretary of the Army, acting through the Chief of Engineers, to manage and allocate funding for all of the individually authorized commercial and recreational navigation projects in the Great Lakes Navigation System as components of a single, comprehensive system, recognizing the interdependence of the projects. Requires the Secretary, acting through the Chief of Engineers, to establish a program to fund eligible operations and maintenance (O&M) projects of the Great Lakes Navigation System with the objective of maintaining them to their authorized depths and widths. Requires the Secretary, acting through the Chief of Engineers, to give a higher priority to projects that provide a cost share of: (1) 50% or more for harbors providing a cost share of 50% or less for eligible harbors, and (2) not subject to harbor maintenance fees.

Sweetgrass Hills Protection Act of 1995 - Establishes the Sweetgrass Hills Natural Area in the Bureau of Land Management's Sweetgrass Hills Area of Critical Environmental Concern in eastern Montana. 
Directs the Secretary of the Interior to acquire lands or interests in lands within the boundaries of the natural area that are necessary to carry out the purposes of this Act by donation, purchase with donation or appropriated funds, or exchange.  Allows lands within the boundaries of the natural area only by donation or exchange. 
Prohibits the Secretary from issuing any lease under the mineral leasing or geothermal leasing laws of the United States for lands within the natural area. 
Prohibits the Secretary from offering any mineral or mining claims in the natural area. 
Prohibits any federal lands from being used in connection with any mining or mining related activities within the Natural Area. 
Requires the Secretary to undertake and complete within three years an expedited program to examine all unpatented mining claims, including those for which a patent application has been filed, within the natural area.  Requires the Secretary to determine the validity of such claims, if one is determined to be invalid, and declare such claim null and void. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Hiring Heroes Tax Incentive Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers a 15% tax credit for the salaries of members of the Ready Reserve and the National Guard who serve in a trade or business of the employer for which they are either a member of the Ready Reserve or the National Guard. Defines "qualified employee" for purposes of such credit as an employee who is a member of the Ready Reserve or the National Guard.

Directs the Secretary of State to designate an individual to be responsible for monitoring slavery in Sudan.

Furthering Accountability and Individual Rights within the Military Act of 2014 or the Fair Military Act - Directs the Secretary of a military department to ensure that written performance appraisals of each member of the Armed Forces (whether an officer or enlisted member) include an assessment of the extent to which the member supports the sexual assault prevention and response program of the Armed Force concerned. Directs the Secretary to ensure that such performance appraisals indicate the extent to which the officer or enlisted member has or has not established a command climate in which: (1) allegations of sexual assault are properly managed and fairly evaluated; and (2) a victim can report criminal activity, including sexual assault, without fear of retaliation, including ostracism and group pressure from other members of the command. Clean Up Earmarks Act of 2010 or CUE Act of 2010 - Directs the Comptroller General to audit five percent of Senate earmarks for the current fiscal year chosen at random.

Securing the Cities Act of 2017 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Director of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for Domestic Nuclear Detection to establish the Securing the Cities (STC) program to enhance U.S. detection of and prevent terrorist attacks and other high consequence events using nuclear or other radiological materials that pose a high risk to homeland security in high-risk urban areas. Arapaho-Roosevelt National Forests Land Exchange Act of 2007 - Directs the land exchange between Grand Creek, LLC and the United States of Colorado in the Arapaho-Roosevelt National Forests in Colorado.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) adjust the boundary of the National Forests to reflect such land exchange; and (2) manage the non-federal land acquired as part of the National Forests.

Guaranteed Health Coverage for Pre-Existing Conditions Act of 2014 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit a group health plan or health insurance issuer offering group health insurance coverage from imposing any preexisting condition exclusion with respect to such plan or coverage. Defines "preexisting condition exclusion" as a limitation or exclusion of benefits relating to a condition based on the fact that the condition was present before the date of enrollment in such plan or coverage, whether or not any medical advice, diagnosis, care, or treatment was recommended or received before such date. Applies the same requirements to coverage offered in the individual market. Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to accept every employer and every individual in a group in the state that applies for such coverage. Prohibits a health insurance issuer from restricting enrollment in coverage to open or special enrollment periods. Military Families Act - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to adjust the status of an alien who is: (1) a parent, spouse, child, son or daughter, or daughter-in-law of a living Armed Forces member or a deceased Armed Forces member who died as a result of injury or disease incurred in or aggravated by his or her service; or (2) a son or daughter of such an Armed Forces member or member's surviving spouse or child or a son or daughter of such member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child or member's surviving spouse or child

Senior Nutrition Act of 2002 - Amends the Agriculture and Consumer Protection Act of 1973 to provide that a senior citizen in the United States shall be eligible for a commodity supplemental food program serving elderly persons if the elderly person is at least 60 years of age and: (1) is eligible for food stamp benefits under the Food Stamp Act of 1977; or (2) has a household income that is less than 185 percent of the Federal Poverty Income Guidelines.Authorizes appropriations.

Mortgage Disclosure Simplification Act of 2007 - Amends the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act of 1974 to direct the Secretary of the Treasury to require that: (1) the forms used in transactions involving federally related mortgage loans be used in all transactions in the United States that involve such loans; and (2) the form used in any such transaction be appropriately and accurately completed by the lender or mortgage broker or both, and the completed form be provided to the borrower, together with the form, within three days after the application for the federally related mortgage loan is made.

Requires the standard written forms required under this Act to set forth: (1) a best possible estimate of the total loan amount, the loan-to-value ratio, the final maturity date, the amount and due date for any balloon payment, the amount of any prepayment fee if the loan is paid in full before the final maturity date, the amount of any initial interest rate, and the monthly household income of the borrower; (2) the amount of settlement charges for all settlement services provided in connection with the loan, the amount of lender's fees, and any additional fees or required payments in connection with the loan; and (3) the aggregate amount of lender'

Health Insurance Rate Review Act This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit a state from imposing additional unreasonable, unjustifiable, or unfairly discriminatory rates of health insurance coverage on health insurance issuers. The Department of Health and Human Services must determine whether the state's rate is reasonable and whether it is appropriate to review the state's rate.

Protecting Neighborhoods from Oil Pollution Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (commonly known as the Clean Water Act) to direct the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to require an owner or operator of an oil storage or processing facility located within one mile of 100 or more residential units and two or more covered discharges at such facility to: (1) permanently close such facility if one or both of the facilities are located within 10 years of enactment of this Act, and (2) include in regulations issued under this Act a requirement that such closure be completed by one of the facilities within one year after enactment of this Act.

Prohibits the inclusion of additional closure and post-closure requirements the EPA determines appropriate in regulations issued under this Act for covered discharges resulting from an act of God, an act of war, or negligence on the part of the U.S. Government.

Authorizes the EPA to waive such requirement or grant an extension of the deadline for such closure if it is determined that the owner or operator has taken or is taking all practicable steps to remediate the condition requiring closure.

Veteran Employment Through Technology Education Courses Act or the VET TEC Act - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to carry out a pilot program under which the Secretary shall provide eligible veterans with the opportunity to enroll in high technology programs of education.

Requires the Secretary to contract with multiple qualified providers of high technology programs of education to provide such programs to eligible veterans.

Directs the Secretary to pay to each eligible veteran enrolled in such a program on a monthly housing stipend equal to the product of: (1) the portion of the basic allowance for housing for a member with dependents residing in the military housing area that encloses the institution at which the individual is enrolled; or (2) 50 percent of the amount payable under the veterans' entitlement to educational assistance for which the individual is eligible.

Directs the Secretary to pay to each eligible veteran enrolled in such a program on a full time basis a monthly housing stipend equal to the product of: (1) the portion of the basic allowance for housing for a member with dependents residing in the military housing area that encloses the institution at which the individual is enrolled; or (2) 50 percent of the amount payable under the veterans' entitlement to educational assistance for which the individual is eligible multiplied by (

Veterans' Burial Benefits Enhancement Act of 2003 - Amends Federal veterans' burial benefits provisions to authorize the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to lease to the Secretary of the Interior any unutilized or underutilized Federal land that is part of the National Cemetery Administration.

Authorizes the Secretary to lease to a public or nonprofit organization up to three years of unutilized or underutilized Federal land that is part of the National Cemetery Administration.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) publish in a newspaper of general circulation in the community in which the land is located appropriate public notice of the intention of the Secretary to lease the land; and (2) enter into a lease of such land or facilities to a public or nonprofit organization for the maintenance, protection, or restoration of the land or facilities as part of the consideration for the lease.

Requires the proceeds from such lease to be deposited in the National Cemetery Administration's account.

Requires the Secretary to establish a national cemetery in each geographic area identified by the Secretary in order to ensure that the veterans who reside in such geographic area more than 50 miles from an open national cemetery and who are eligible for burial in such cemetery reside not more than 50 miles from an open national cemetery.

Camera Accountability Maintenance and Transparency in Policing Act of 2017 or the CAM TIP Act of 2017 This bill amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to authorize the Bureau of Justice Assistance to make grants to states, units of local government, and Indian tribes for the acquisition, operation, and maintenance of body-worn cameras for law enforcement officers.  The bill defines "body-worn camera" as a camera that records video of an officer's non-public interactions with the public.  The bill also authorizes the Department of Justice (DOJ) to use grant funds to establish a task force to provide recommendations on community policing, including best practices for creating accountability and transparency. The bill directs the Government Accountability Office to report to Congress on the Department of Defense Excess Personal Property Program.

Improving Corporate Governance Through Diversity Act of 2017 This bill requires a federal agency to require a contractor to submit to the agency at least 60 days after the award of a contract: (1) data on the racial, ethnic, and gender composition of the board of directors and the C-level executives of the contractor; (2) data on the affiliation of any board or executive member to a historically underrepresented group; and (3) any plan or strategy on the date of submission of data to improve the diversity of the board or the C-level executives of the contractor.  The bill amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to require that when a proxy or information statement is submitted in a proxy or information statement relating to the election of directors, the qualities and skills, along with the nominee's gender, race, ethnicity, and affiliation with a historically underrepresented group, should be presented in a chart or matrix form.
Medicaid Mammography Coverage Act of 1993 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to provide for coverage of screening mammography under the Medicaid program.

Smart Water Management Conservation and Efficiency Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to establish and carry out a smart water management pilot program to award grants to utilities, municipalities, water districts, and other water authorities to demonstrate and deploy novel and innovative technology-based solutions that will: (1) increase the energy and water efficiency of drinking water, wastewater treatment, and water reuse systems; (2) improve drinking water, water reuse, and wastewater treatment systems to help communities make significant progress in conserving water, saving energy, and reducing costs; and (3) support the implementation of innovative processes and the installation of advanced automated systems that provide real-time data on energy and water. Directs the Secretary to make competitive, merit-reviewed grants to up to three eligible entities to consider in selecting an eligible entity. Requires the Secretary to annually evaluate each project for which a grant is provided and make best practices identified in the evaluations available to the public.

College Research Education and Teacher Excellence (CREATE) Opportunity Act of 2012 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to make permanent the program of grants to institutions of higher education for research on the effectiveness of teacher quality of education in the public interest (i.e., the creation of a teacher workforce capable of teaching effectively in the public interest).

Increases the percentage of contract research expenses paid to such institutions.

Directs the Secretary of Education to award up to two Federal Pell Grants to students to accelerate their progress toward a degree or certificate if they are enrolled: (1) on at least a half-time basis for a period of more than one academic year, or more than two semesters or an equivalent period of time, during a single award year; and (2) in a program of instruction at the junior or community college for which the college awards an associate degree or a certificate.

Requires the total amount of Pell Grants awarded to such students for the award year to exceed the maximum basic grant level in the appropriate appropriations Act for such award year.

Check the Box for Homeless Veterans Act of 2013 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) establish in the Treasury the Homeless Veterans Assistance Fund to provide services to homeless veterans; (2) allow individual taxpayers to designate on their tax returns a portion of any overpayment of tax (not less than $1) for such tax to be paid over to such Fund; and (3) require the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the Department of Labor Veterans' Employment and Training Service, and the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to include a description of the use of funds from the Fund in their previous fiscal years and the proposed use of such funds for the next fiscal year.

Stop Turning Out Prisoners Act - Amends the federal criminal code to provide that prospective relief in a civil action with respect to prison conditions shall extend no further than necessary to remove the conditions that are causing the deprivation of the federal rights of the individual plaintiffs in the action. Prohibits the court from granting or approving prospective relief unless it is narrowly drawn and the least intrusive means to remedy the violation of the federal right. Directs the court, in determining the intrusiveness of the relief, to give substantial weight to any adverse impact on public safety or the operation of a criminal justice system caused by the relief. Prohibits the court from granting or approving relief whose purpose or effect is to reduce or limit the prison population, unless the plaintiff proves that crowding is the primary cause of the deprivation and no other relief will remedy that deprivation. Directs that any prospective relief: (1) automatically terminate two years after the later of: (1) the date the court found the violation of a federal right that was the basis for the relief; or (2) the date of the enactment of the Stop Turning Out Prisoners Act.

Requires a defendant or intervenor to be entitled to immediate termination of prospective relief if that relief was approved or granted in the absence of a finding by the

Marine Navigation Safety Improvement Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish in the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund a separate Marine Navigation Safety Account.  Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer to such Account not later than 30 days after enactment of this Act an amount not to exceed the sum of:  (1) 8 percent of the amount of the taxes received in the Treasury for FY 1991 and 1992; and (2) 8 percent of such taxes for the ensuing fiscal year.  Requires such amounts in the Account to be made available to carry out the programs and activities of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration of the Department of Commerce related to commercial marine navigation.  Requires the amounts in the Account to remain available until expended, and to be made available to the Secretary of Commerce to support, either directly or by contract, the nautical charting and marine navigational safety programs and other activities of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration related to commercial marine navigation.  Prohibits the use of such funds for offsetting any amounts made available for the purposes of the Operation, Research, and Facilities account of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
Librarian Education and Development Act of 2003 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to extend the loan forgiveness program for public school teachers through FY 2005.

Innovation Protection Act - Establishes the United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Revolving Fund.

Requires the Office to be funded with fees collected by the Office and the Office's Trademark Act of 1946-related fees collected under the Trademark Act of 1946.

Requires the Office to be funded, on an annual basis, with amounts collected by the Office and the Office's Trademark Act of 1946-related fees collected under the Act.

Requires the Office to submit to the President a business-type budget in such manner, and before such date, as the President prescribes by regulation.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the property subject to a liability test and to allow the transfer of property acquired from the corporation to the taxpayer. 
Provides for the determination of the amount of liability assumed in this Act. 
Provides for the application of this Act to provisions other than subchapter C (Stock and Investment Company Securities) of the Internal Revenue Code.

Hazardous Materials Cooperative Research Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish and carry out a hazardous materials cooperative research program.

Requires the Secretary to establish an independent governing board to select projects and studies to be carried out under the program.

Requires the governing board to be comprised of one voting representative from each of the following Federal agencies: (1) the Federal Aviation Administration; (2) the Federal Motor Carrier Administration; (3) the Federal Transit Administration; (4) the Federal Railroad Administration; (5) the Maritime Administration; (6) the Research and Innovative Technology Administration; (7) the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration; (8) the Department of Homeland Security; (9) the Department of Energy; (10) the Environmental Protection Agency; (11) a State department of transportation; (12) a State emergency management agency; (13) a nonprofit organization representing emergency responders; (14) a hazmat employer; (15) a nonprofit representing hazmat employees; (16) a labor union representing members involved in shipping hazardous materials; (17) a hazardous materials manufacturer; (18) an organization representing the hazardous materials manufacturing industry; (19) a research university
Directs the Quinault Indian Nation to distribute certain of its judgment funds to establish a Permanent Fisheries Fund.  Subjects such Fund to the Investment and Financial Policy Act of 1990.

Trail of the Ancients National Heritage Area Study Act of 2005 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to study and report to specified congressional committees on the feasibility and suitability of designating the Trail of the Ancients National Heritage Area in Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and Utah as the Trail of the Ancients National Heritage Area.

Protecting Dissenting Viewpoints and Voices Act of 2017 This bill amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from revoking or otherwise taking action against any person on the basis of viewpoints taken, or not taken, on issues of public importance in content that is broadcast or otherwise disseminated by such person or any person affiliated with such person.  The bill prohibits the FCC from placing on any approval under this Act any condition with respect to viewpoints to be taken, or not taken, on issues of public importance in content broadcast or otherwise disseminated by the person seeking such approval, any successor of such person, or any person affiliated with such person or successor.  The President may not direct an agency to take any action against any person on the basis, in whole or in part, of viewpoints taken, or not taken, on issues of public importance in content that is broadcast or otherwise disseminated by such person or any person affiliated with such person. Skilled Workforce Enhancement Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers a business tax credit for 80 percent of the training expenses incurred by a taxpayer in training an employee in a highly skilled metalworking trades.  Limits the amount of such credit to $100,000 per employee.  Prohibits the credit from being taken into account in determining the credits for the first five taxable years after the taxable year in which the training period ends.  Limits the total amount of credit to $10,000 per employee for all taxable years.  Prohibits the deduction of such credit for the portion of the expenses otherwise allowable as a deduction for the taxable year which is equal to the amount of the credit.

Criminal Antitrust Anti-Retaliation Act - Amends the Antitrust Criminal Penalty Enhancement and Reform Act of 2004 to prohibit a person, or any officer, employee, contractor, subcontractor, or agent of such person, from discharging, demoting, suspending, threatening, harassing, or otherwise discriminating against a whistleblower in the terms and conditions of employment because: (1) the whistleblower provided or caused the person or Government to believe that the person's information was relevant to a violation of antitrust laws; or (2) the whistleblower filed, caused to be filed, testified, participated in, or otherwise assisted an investigation or proceeding relating to the violation.

Defines "whistleblower" as an employee, contractor, subcontractor, or agent protected from discrimination.

Authorizes a whistleblower to seek relief by filing a complaint with the Secretary of Labor or, if the Secretary has not issued a final decision within 180 days after the complaint is filed, bringing an action at law or equity for de novo review in the appropriate U.S. district court.

Provides that a complaint filed with the Secretary shall be governed by the rules and procedures set forth in the Clayton Act.

Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to convey certain lands in Grant and South Dakota Counties, New Mexico, to eligible buyers for business and community development.  Requires the Secretary to sell such lands in tracts of not less than 40 acres and in specified ways, including requiring a market price of the land in its present state of use as agricultural grazing lands.  Requires the Secretary to protect all valid existing rights, reserve easements for roads and telephone lines, reserve easements for roads as necessary to assure access to specified lands, reserve such easements for roads as necessary to meet public needs, and reserve such easements for roads as necessary to meet public needs.  Requires the Secretary to make such a conveyance to eligible buyers if historic or prehistoric cultural properties are located upon such lands.  Requires the Secretary to be responsible for the costs and recovery of such sites and to do so in a timely manner so as not to unduly restrict future use of the selected lands by the acquiring party.  Allows the Secretary to use a deed reservation to retain historic or prehistoric properties in the ownership of the United States if agreeable to the acquiring party. Great Lakes Pipeline Safety Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of Transportation (DOT) to conduct a study to determine the economic and environmental risks to the Great Lakes of spills or leaks of oil or other hazardous liquids in the Straits of Mackinac from a rupture, breakage, or other failure of onshore, underwater pipeline facilities within the Straits.  DOT shall conduct a supplemental study to evaluate the condition and structural integrity of onshore, underwater pipeline facilities in the Straits.  The bill terminates operations of an onshore, underwater pipeline facility located in the Straits if the Administrator of the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) determines that such facility poses a sufficient risk of hazard to life, property, or the environment to necessitate the termination.

Grand Jury Reform Act of 1998 - Amends the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure to instruct the court, upon impaneling a grand jury, to instruct and charge the grand jury on the rights, responsibilities, and duties of the grand jury under such rule, including the right to:  (1) call and interrogate witnesses; (2) request production of an object, including exculpatory evidence; (3) seek to have the attorney for the government draft indictments for charges other than those originally requested; (4) be counsel for a witness; and (5) be allowed assistance of counsel during the questioning of a witness. 
Requires the court to give each witness subpoenaed to appear and testify a reasonable opportunity to be examined and copied. 
Provides that an attorney for the government shall disclose to the grand jury any substantial evidence of which that attorney has knowledge that directly negates the guilt of the accused. 
Provides that a defendant shall, upon request, and as the court determines to be reasonable, be entitled to examine and duplicate a transcript or electronic recording of the grand jury testimony of all witnesses to be called at trial, all statements relating to the defendant's case made to the grand jury by the court, the attorney

Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to develop a plan for the purchase, storage, and rotation of a six-month supply of vaccines routinely recommended for children and adults.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) fully implement such plan; and (2) require manufacturers of vaccines included in the supply to provide at least one year notice of a discontinuance of the manufacture of the vaccine or other factors that may prevent the manufacturer from providing vaccines pursuant to an arrangement made to carry out this Act.

Requires the Secretary to report periodically to specified congressional committees on the progress made in implementing the plan and on impediments to its implementation.
Directs the Secretary of Defense to pay compensation to each living veteran or civilian internee, or to the surviving spouse of a living veteran or civilian internee, in the amount of $20,000.

Classroom Safety Act of 2000 - Amends the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) to authorize school personnel to discipline (including expel or suspend) a child with a disability who: (1) carries or possesses a weapon to or at a school, on school premises, or to or at a school function; or (2) possesses or uses illegal drugs, or sells or solicits the sale of a controlled substance while at a school, on school premises, or to or at a school function. Authorizes such personnel to modify the disciplinary action on a case-by-case basis.Declares that nothing in this Act shall be construed to prevent a child with a disability who is disciplined pursuant to IDEA authority from asserting a defense that the carrying or possession of the weapon, or the possession of an illegal drug or sale of a controlled substance, was unintentional or innocent.Declares that a child expelled or suspended under this Act shall not be entitled to continued educational services, including a free appropriate public education, under IDEA, if the State in which the local educational agency responsible for providing educational services to such child does not require a child with a disability to receive educational services after being expelled or suspended. Duty Suspension Facilitation Act of 2010 - Directs the International Trade Commission (ITC) to submit to the Senate Committee on Finance and the House Committee on Ways and Means proposals for amendments to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTS) in connection with the temporary suspension or reduction of duty.

Requires the ITC to solicit and give consideration to the views of interested federal agencies and the public.

Directs the Commission to: (1) give notice of the proposed amendments, afford reasonable opportunity for interested parties to present their views in writing, and provide for a public hearing; and (2) publish the proposed amendments in the Federal Register.

Requires the Commission to: (1) base its proposed legislation on specified information contained in the Government Printing Office (GPO) report on the Chemical Abstracts Service and the article description and duty rates for each subheading of the SAA, and any other information necessary to carry out the proposed legislation; and (2) submit a summary of information on which the recommendation is based and a summary of the views submitted by interested federal agencies, the public, and other interested parties.

Increases the amount of duty suspension authorized by this Act.

National Park System New Area Studies Act - Amends the National Park System General Authorities Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior to:  (1) submit to specified congressional committees a list of areas recommended for study for potential inclusion in the National Park System (NPS); and (2) give consideration to those areas that have the greatest potential to meet the established criteria of national significance, suitability, and feasibility.  Directs the Secretary to give special consideration to themes, sites, and resources not already adequately represented in the NPS.  Prohibits the initiation of a study of the potential of an area for inclusion in the NPS after this Act's enactment date.  Declares that nothing in this Act shall limit the authority of the National Park Service (NPS) to conduct preliminary resource assessments, gather data on potential study areas, provide technical and planning assistance, prepare or process nominations for administrative designations, update previous studies, or complete reconnaissance surveys of individual areas requiring a total expenditure of less than $25,000.  Requires the Secretary to complete the study for each area within three fiscal years following the enactment of this Act.  Requires each study to be prepared with appropriate opportunity for public involvement and after reasonable efforts to notify affected landowners and state and local governments

DHS Paid Administrative Leave Accountability Act of 2015 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the head of each component of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to submit to the Chief Human Capital Officer of DHS: (1) the number of employees of DHS component who had been on administrative leave, or any other type of paid non-duty status without charge to leave, for a period of six consecutive months or longer as of the last day of the period covered by the report; (2) the total cost to the component associated with such administrative leave and such paid non-duty status for the period covered by the report; and (3) the average duration that employees are placed on administrative leave, or any other types of paid non-duty status without charge to leave, for personnel matters for a period of six consecutive months or longer, as of the last day of the period covered by the report for the component.  The bill requires the Chief Human Capital Officer to: (1) maintain records of the number of DHS employees placed on administrative leave or paid non-duty status for personnel matters and the costs associated with such leave or non-duty status; and (2) in consultation

Work Made For Hire and Copyright Corrections Act of 2000 - Amends Federal copyright law to define "work made for hire" to include in determining whether any work is eligible to be considered a work made for hire, neither the amendment contained in the section concerning the Intellectual Property and Communications Omnibus Reform Act of 1999 nor the deletion of the words added by that amendment. Makes such amendment effective as of November 29, 1999.

Tribal Colleges and Universities Faculty Loan Forgiveness Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to assume or cancel obligations to repay qualified loan amounts for new borrowers on or after enactment of this Act who are: (1) employed as full-time faculty members at a tribal college or university; and (2) not in default on a loan for which the borrower seeks repayment or cancellation.

Requires the Secretary to assume or cancel such obligations: (1) 15 percent of the amount of all loans made, insured, or guaranteed after enactment of this Act to a student under part B or D for the first or second year of such employment; (2) 20 percent of such total amount, for the third or fourth year, for such employment; and (3) 30 percent of such total amount, for the fifth year, for such employment.

Prohibits a borrower from receiving a benefit under both this Act and the National and Community Service Act of 1990 in the same year that the borrower is employed as a faculty member at a tribal college or university.

Taxpayers' Cancer Research Funding Act of 1996 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to permit every individual (other than a nonresident alien) whose adjusted income tax liability for the taxable year is $5 or more to designate that $5 be paid over to the Breast and Prostate Cancer Research Fund. 
Establishes in the Treasury the Breast and Prostate Cancer Research Fund.  Provides that amounts in the Fund shall be available for purposes of making qualified research grants to the National Cancer Institutes of Health for breast or prostate cancer.

Provide Access and Retain Continuity Act or the PARC Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to reimburse States for eligible activities under a specified Memorandum of Understanding (commonly known as a memorandum of understanding) entered into by the Secretary and the State of Utah to provide for the continued operation of certain facilities and programs.

Safe and Secure Border Infrastructure Act - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish a grant program to construct transportation and supporting infrastructure improvements at existing and new international border crossings to facilitate the safe, secure, and efficient cross-border movement of motor vehicles, non-motor vehicles, cargo, and individuals, including pedestrians.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to projects that accomplish one or more specified objectives, including: (1) improving the safety and security at U.S. facilities, including ports of entry; (2) facilitating safe, secure, and legal trade crossings of motor vehicles, non-motor vehicles, cargo, and individuals to alleviate border congestion and reduce the economic effect of border wait times and delays; (3) implementing innovative technologies that enhance safety, security, or efficiency at the border; (4) coordinating a system of projects that improve security and systems efficiency at ports of entry; (5) facilitating economic development strategies with respect to safety and security; (6) implementing congestion relief and air quality management strategies to improve the environment; and (7) implementing specified projects to improve the environment.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose a 5 percent excise tax on the gross receipts attributable to the transportation of passengers by water or land on a cruise vessel.  Establishes the Intermodal Infrastructure Trust Fund in the Treasury.  Requires such Fund to be used to improve transportation infrastructure, including passenger or freight rail lines, highways, bridges, airports, air traffic control systems, port or marine facilities, inland waterways, transmission or distribution pipelines, public transportation facilities or systems, intercity passenger bus or passenger rail facilities or equipment, and freight rail facilities or equipment.

Country-of-Origin Labeling for Fuels Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy to study and report to Congress on methods and standards for requiring motor vehicle fuel suppliers and retailers to disclose country-of-origin information to consumers.

Requires the Secretary to prescribe regulations requiring motor vehicle fuel suppliers and retailers to disclose country-of-origin information in accordance with the Secretary's recommendations in the report.

Authorizes the Secretary to impose a civil penalty on a person that the Secretary determines knowingly violates the regulations prescribed under this Act.

King Holiday and Service Act of 1993 - Amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to establish a commission to assist in the first observance of the Federal legal holiday honoring Martin Luther King, Jr.  Requires the Chairperson of the Commission on National and Community Service to be an ex officio member of the Martin Luther King, Jr. Federal Holiday Commission. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Hass Avocado Quality Assurance Act of 2007 - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to issue regulations to ensure that all Hass avocados sold to consumers in the state of California comply with minimum maturity standards for the sale of such avocados.

Prohibits the Secretary from using existing inspectors to conduct inspections under this Act.

Authorizes the Secretary to divert, export, or repack and reinspect any Hass avocados that do not meet such minimum standards or the regulations issued pursuant to this Act.

Authorizes the Secretary to require any person who violates such regulations to forfeit to the United States a sum equal to the value of the commodity at the time of violation, which forfeiture shall be recoverable in a civil suit brought in the name of the United States.

Authorizes the Secretary to impose a fine and/or imprisonment for each violator.
Help Organ Procurement Expand Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for $2,500 of the cost of organ donation.

Unemployment Compensation, Reemployment, and Fairness Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that, if the State elects to participate, the compensation shall not be denied or reduced to any individual because such individual is participating in a self-employment program with the approval of the State agency (or because of the application, to any such week in such program, of State law provisions relating to availability for work, active search for work, or refusal to accept work).

Responsible Debt Relief and Democracy Reform Act - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to authorize the President to cancel or reduce amounts owed to the United States by a foreign country as a result of concessional or nonconcessional loans only if the requirements of this Act are met.

National Trails System Willing Seller Act - Amends the National Trails System Act to prohibit the Federal Government from acquiring land or interest in land outside the exterior boundaries of any federally administered area for the Oregon, Mormon Pioneer, Lewis and Clark, Iditarod, Nez Perce, and Nez Perce Trace National Scenic Trails.

This bill prohibits a prevailing rate employee from being paid during the period beginning on January 1, 2014, and ending on the normal effective date of the applicable wage survey adjustment that is to take effect in FY2014.  No such employee may be paid during the period beginning on the day after the end of such period and ending on September 30, 2014, in a rate that exceeds the rate payable under the General Schedule. Personal Exemption Fairness Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a regional cost-of-living adjustment in the personal gross income of taxpayers in non-metropolitan statistical areas (NMSA) whose primary place of abode during the taxable year is located in the statistical area.

The Board must meet at least twice each year to advise and consult with the CFPB on emerging practices of small businesses that provide eligible financial products or services. The CFPB must establish a Credit Union Advisory Council to advise and consult with the CFPB on consumer financial products or services that impact credit unions.

Declaration of Official Language Act of 1997 - English shall be the official language of the U.S. Government.  English shall be the language of American citizens.  The Government should promote and support the use of English for communications among U.S. citizens.  Citizens should be encouraged to read, write, and speak English to the extent of their physical and mental abilities.  Declares that it has been the long-standing national belief that full citizenship in the United States requires fluency in English.  States that English is the language of opportunity for all immigrants to take their rightful place in American society.  States that English is the language of American speech.  Declares that:  (1) the Immigration and Naturalization Service shall enforce the established English language proficiency standard for all U.S.  citizens; and (2) the naturalization ceremonies shall be entirely in English.  Declares that this Act shall not affect programs in schools designed to encourage students to learn foreign languages.  Repeals provisions of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 regarding bilingual election requirements and regarding congressional findings of voting discrimination against language minorities. DHS may exclude information from the framework if it may: (1) jeopardize the protection of sources, methods, or activities, (2) compromise a criminal or national security investigation, (3) be inconsistent with other federal laws or regulations, or (4) be duplicative or not serve an operational purpose if included in the framework. Veterans Health Care Budget Reform and Transparency Act of 2009 - Amends the federal budget law to make new discretionary budget authority provided in an appropriations Act for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) specified in this Act available for the fiscal year involved, and to include new discretionary budget authority for such appropriations accounts that first become available for the first fiscal year after such fiscal year.

Directs the Comptroller General to study the adequacy and accuracy of the budget projections made by the Enrollee Health Care Projection Model, its equivalent, or other methodologies, as utilized for the purpose of estimating and projecting health care expenditures of the VA with respect to the fiscal year involved and the subsequent four fiscal years.

Requires the Comptroller General to report to Congress on the basis of such budget projections: (1) whether the amount requested in the President's FY2011 budget is consistent with anticipated expenditures of the VA for health care in such fiscal year; and (2) the basis for such statement.

Native American Housing Enhancement Act of 2005 - Amends the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996 to provide for the preference of Native American tribes for housing programs under title V (Grants) of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and title VI (Housing and Urban Development Assistance) of the Civil Rights Act of 1968.

Black Hills National Forest and Rocky Mountain Research Station Improvement Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to: (1) sell or exchange certain land in South Dakota for Black Hills National Forest and Rocky Mountain Research Station; and (2) make technical corrections to the legal descriptions of certain land.

Veterans Conservation Corps Authorization Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to establish a veterans conservation corps to provide training and employment to eligible veterans, to assist eligible veterans in the transition from service in the Armed Forces to civilian life, and to assist the federal government in maintaining federal land and water.

State Health Care Flexibility Act of 2011 - Allows a qualifying state to opt out of the application of any or all of the provisions of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) with respect to health insurance coverage within such state.

Master Teacher Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Education to conduct a demonstration project under which the Secretary shall award competitive grants to local educational agencies (LEAs) to increase teacher salaries and employee benefits for teachers who enter into contracts with the LEAs to serve as master teachers.

Tax Reduction and Economic Growth Act of 1995 - Directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to notify the President and the Congress if the Director has determined that for any of specified economic growth periods:  (1) economic growth as measured by the change in the real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at an annual rate is estimated to be less than one percent and the rate of national unemployment is estimated to be greater than six percent; and (2) the rate of national unemployment is estimated to be greater than five percent.  Authorizes the President to declare a temporary income tax reduction if the President determines that such economic growth requirements will provide a quick and necessary fiscal stimulus to the economy.  Requires any such declaration to be transmitted to the Congress.  Provides for the temporary surtax where economic growth requirements subsequently satisfied.  Provides for the treatment of any economic growth reduction in the event of a temporary economic downturn.

Children's Products Safety Act of 2007 - Amends the Consumer Product Safety Act to require that a manufacturer of children's products certify to the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) that it complies with consumer product safety rules governing hazardous products for children.

Requires the CPSC to prescribe a rule for children's products that is consistent with the CPSC's policy of requiring independent third-party testing and certification of compliance with all consumer product safety rules.

Amends the CPSC's regulations governing children's products to prohibit the importation into the United States of children's products that are not accompanied by a certificate from a third-party verification entity required by the CPSC.

Choice in Welfare Tax Credit Act of 1995 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer a tax credit for contributions made to a qualifying charity that are made without the assistance of a tax deduction.

Crop Risk Options Plan Act of 2013 - Amends the Federal Crop Insurance Act to require the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation (FCIC) to provide farmers with additional coverage based on: (1) an individual yield and loss basis or an area yield and loss basis, supplemented with coverage based on an area yield and loss basis to cover a part of the deductible under the individual yield and loss policy; or (2) a margin basis alone or in combination with the coverages available in such Act. Requires the FCIC to also provide farmers with information on catastrophic risk and additional coverage in terms of dollar coverage. Requires the FCIC to offer farmers the opportunity to purchase coverage in combination with a policy or plan of insurance that would allow indemnities to be paid to a producer equal to a part of the deductible under the policy or plan of insurance: (1) at a county-wide level to the fullest extent practicable; or (2) in counties that lack sufficient data, on the basis of such larger geographical area as the FCIC determines to provide sufficient data for purposes of providing the coverage. Requires the FCIC to use data collected by the Risk Management Agency or the National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) to determine yields under such coverage.

Flat Alternative Individual Return Tax Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an individual election on the FAIR taxable income of an individual making such an election. Requires the laboratory to: (1) use calibration testing equipment developed by the laboratory for purposes of study; and (2) use commercially available calibration testing equipment as a control.

Requires the Administrator of the TSA to ensure that large, easily readable signs or equivalent electronic displays are placed at the front of airline passenger check point queues where backscatter advanced imaging technology machines are used for screening to inform passengers that they may request to undergo alternative screening procedures instead of passing through a backscatter x-ray machine.

Federal Railroad Safety Authorization Act of 1994 - Amends Federal transportation law to authorize the Secretary of Transportation to provide for the establishment of pilot projects to demonstrate the benefits of implementing alternatives to the strict application of Federal rail safety requirements.  Authorizes the Secretary to waive such compliance requirements for up to two years if the Secretary determines that such waiver is in the public interest and is consistent with railroad safety. 
Directs the Secretary to report biennially to specified congressional committees on the administration of the pilot projects. 
Directs the Secretary to consider whether or not to prescribe regulations and issue orders concerning:  (1) inspection procedures to identify internal rail defects, before they reach imminent failure size, in rail that has significant shelling; and (2) any specific actions that should be taken when a rail surface condition prevents the identification of internal defects.

Directs the Secretary to provide technical assistance and advice to States in the development of model profiling systems and procedures for such systems. 
Authorizes appropriations for nonrepayable advances to the account for Unemployment Trust Fund and Other Funds in the Department of Labor Appropriations Acts.

Ban Poisonous Additives Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require that certain containers of baby food, infant formula, and certain containers for children and infant formula be made of bisphenol A (BPA), as well as certain containers used in the manufacture of certain infant formula products.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to issue a revised safety assessment for food containers composed, in whole or in part, of bisphenol A, taking into consideration different types of food containers and the use of such containers with respect to different foods.

Requires the Secretary to use the safety standard established under this Act to evaluate the proposed uses of alternatives to BPA.

Trade Promotion Authority Extension and Enhancement Act of 2007 - Amends the Bipartisan Trade Promotion Authority Act of 2002 to extend through each of five years after July 1, 2011, trade authorities procedures under such Act to implementing bills submitted with respect to trade agreements entered into during the five-year period beginning on July 1, 2011, and each five-year period thereafter, unless the Congress adopts an extension disapproval resolution.

Directs the International Trade Commission (ITC) to report to Congress on the economic impact of trade agreements implemented after July 1 of the fifth preceding calendar year.

Family Farmer Bankruptcy Clarification Act of 2017 This bill clarifies the rule allowing a governmental unit to discharge a claim arising from the disposition of farm property under the bankruptcy code.  The bill defines a "claim" as an unsecured claim against the debtor or the estate that arises before the filing of the petition, or that arises after the filing of the petition, and that arises because of the sale, transfer, exchange, or other disposition of any property used in the debtor's farming operation.  The bill provides that, subject to specified requirements, a governmental unit may file a proof of claim for a claim that arises after the filing of the petition.  A claim may not be amended after the filing of a petition.  A claim may not be dismissed or allowed to stand without filing a tax return.  A claim may not be considered in bankruptcy proceedings as a claim of a kind specified in the bankruptcy code.  A governmental unit may not file a proof of claim for a claim that arises after the filing of a tax return.  A claim may not be dismissed or allowed to stand without filing a tax return.  A claim may not be considered in bankruptcy proceedings as a claim of a kind specified in the bankruptcy code.

Commit to Opioid Medical Prescriber Accountability and Safety for Seniors Act or the COMPASS Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), beginning not later than two years after enactment of this Act, to provide an annual notification to a prescriber identified by the Secretary as an outlier prescriber of opioids, including resources on proper prescribing methods and other information specified under Medicare prescription drug benefit plans.

Requires the Secretary, using the National Provider Identifiers included on claims for covered part D drugs for part D eligible individuals enrolled in prescription drug plans or, based on the threshold established under this Act, to conduct an analysis to identify prescribers that are outlier opioid prescribers for a period of up to five years.

Authorizes the Secretary to exclude individuals and prescribers from the analysis based on input from stakeholders.

Desert Community Lands Act  This bill directs the Department of the Interior to convey to the town of Apple Valley, California, without consideration, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the surface estate of approximately 4,630 acres of land generally depicted as "Proposed Conveyance to Town of Apple Valley" and dated June 1, 2015.  The land may be used for: (1) a central off-road vehicle recreation park; (2) the public with opportunities for off-road vehicle recreation; and (3) a designated area and facilities that would discourage unauthorized use of off-highway vehicles in areas that have been identified by the federal government, the state of California, or San Bernardino County as containing environmentally sensitive land.  Interior shall convey to the city of Twentynine Palms, California, without consideration, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the surface estate of the land generally depicted as "Proposed Conveyance to the City of Twentynine Palms" and dated September 18, 2015. Local Zoning Decisions Protection Act of 2017 This bill requires the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to develop recommendations to further the purposes and policies of the Fair Housing Act.  The HUD final rule on the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Assessment Tool, published on July 16, 2015, and any successor rule that substantially similar to it, is substantially similar to, is not affected by this bill.  HUD must also consult with state officials, local government officials, and public housing agencies to develop recommendations to further the purposes and policies of the Act.

Honorable Stephanie Tubbs Jones College Fire Prevention Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to establish a demonstration program to award competitive grants to eligible entities for the purpose of installing fire sprinkler systems, or other fire suppression or prevention technologies, in student housing and dormitories owned or controlled by such entities.

Food Sharing Act of 2017 This bill amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to modify requirements for assistance for community food projects. Specifically, the bill adds requirements for: (1) the definition of "community food project" to include projects in which an entity: (1) collects edible, surplus food that would be thrown away and distribute the food to agencies or nonprofit organizations that feed the hungry; or (2) harvests for free distribution to the needy, or for donation to agencies or nonprofit organizations for ultimate distribution to the needy, an agricultural crop that has been donated by the owner of the crop.  The Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 is amended to extend the authorization of appropriations for FY2015-FY2017 for assistance for community food projects.

Social Security COLA Limitation Act of 1994 - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to provide for cost-of-living adjustments to OASDI benefits and contributions with respect to the amounts increased by the Secretary of Health and Human Services for the benefit of beneficiaries in the last month of the year in which the increase is due.

HOPE VI Green Building and Technical Assistance Act of 2007 - Amends the United States Housing Act of 1937 to prohibit the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) from making a grant to an applicant unless the applicant's revitalization plan to be carried out with such grant amounts complies with the following requirements: (1) the plan complies with the green communities criteria checklist of the national Green Communities program that provides criteria for the design, development, and operation of affordable housing; and (2) the plan provides that any nonresidential structure covered by the plan 50,000 square feet or more complies with version 2.2 of the LEED-NC 2.2 green building rating system for new construction and major renovations or version 2.0 of the LEED-CS 2.0 green building rating system for core and shell at the certification level.

Requires the Secretary to verify, or provide for verification, sufficient to ensure that each revitalization plan carried out with amounts from a grant under this Act complies with the requirements of this Act and that the revitalization program is carried out in accordance with such requirements and plan.
