State Temporary Economic Priority (STEP) Act - Authorizes a State to transfer or consolidate funds under specified transportation, education, and job training programs after the United States experiences economic growth at an annual rate of less than one percent for two calendar quarters.

Requires transferred or consolidated funds to be used in accordance with the statutory and regulatory requirements applicable to the program to which the funds are transferred or consolidated.

Authorizes a State to transfer, in amounts as determined by the State, any funds apportioned and allocated from amounts made available from the Highway Trust Fund (HTF), other than the Mass Transit Account, to any of the apportionments and allocations for specified job training programs: (1) the interstate maintenance program under the highway safety improvement program; (2) the National Highway System; (3) the surface transportation program; (4) the highway bridge replacement and rehabilitation program; and (5) the highway safety improvement programs.

Prohibits transfer or consolidation of funds made available for the highway safety improvement programs authorized by the highway safety improvement program and for specified job training programs under the Work Force Investment Act of 1998.

Drunk Driving Repeat Offender Prevention Act of 2009 - Amends the federal criminal code to require a state to install an ignition interlock device in a vehicle while operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated or under the influence of alcohol.

Requires the Secretary of Transportation to withhold specified federal-aid highway funds from a state that does not enact and enforce a law that requires the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual who is convicted of driving while intoxicated or under the influence of alcohol.

Opioid Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to one or more states to carry out a one-year pilot project to develop a standardized peer review process and methodology to evaluate prescribing and dispensing patterns of substances on schedule II or III under the Controlled Substances Act (CSAct).  Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary, acting through the Administrator of the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), to award five-year grants to eligible entities to facilitate training in order to increase the capacity of health care providers to conduct patient screening, brief interventions, and referral to treatment as needed, such as in health care settings to prevent the abuse of prescription drugs, heroin, and other controlled substances.  Directs the Attorney General to request that a registered practitioner under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA) practitioner conduct patient screening for potential drug misuse or abuse before prescribing a listed substance on schedule II or III under the CSAct. Directs the Secretary, acting through the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, to conduct a review of naloxone to consider whether naloxone should cease to be subject to CSA provisions and be available as an over-the-counter drug to increase access to such

Kids 2000 Act - Directs the Boys and Girls Clubs of America to make subgrants to local boys and girls clubs authorizing expenditures associated with providing technology programs, including PowerUp, to provide: (1) constructive technology-focussed activities that are part of a comprehensive program to provide access to technology and technology training to youth during after-school hours, weekends, and school vacations; (2) supervised activities in safe environments for youth; and (3) full-time staffing with qualified personnel.

Joe Testaverde Adult Stem Cell Research Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to expand, intensify, and coordinate NIH activities regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Requires the Director to carry out this Act in collaboration with any appropriate agency that the Director determines to be appropriate.

Requires the Director to make awards of grants and contracts to public or nonprofit private entities to pay all or part of the cost of planning, establishing, improving, and providing basic operating support for centers of excellence regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Requires each center to conduct basic and clinical research regarding qualifying adult stem cells.

Authorizes the Director to provide for the establishment of at least five such centers.

Requires the Director to provide for a program under which samples of tissues and genetic materials that are of use in qualifying adult stem cell research are donated, collected, preserved, and made available for such research.

Requires the Director to provide for means through which the public can obtain information on the existing and planned NIH programs and activities regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Solar Fuels Innovation Act (Sec. 2) This bill requires the Department of Energy (DOE) to carry out a research initiative, the Solar Fuels Basic Research Initiative, to expand the knowledge of useful materials and systems to convert solar energy to chemical energy.  The Department of Energy must organize activities under the Initiative to include multidisciplinary teams leveraging expertise from the National Laboratories, universities, and the private sector.  The Department must also carry out a program to support research needed to bridge scientific barriers and discover knowledge relevant to artificial photosynthetic systems.  The Office of Basic Energy Sciences must support basic research needed to replicate natural photosynthetic processes by using artificial photosynthetic components and materials.  The Department must also carry out a program to support research needed to replicate natural photosynthetic processes by using artificial photosynthetic components and materials. Authorizes the Director to review a captured document before making such document publicly available.

Requires the Director to submit to the relevant congressional committees a report containing: (1) a description of each captured document, and (2) an explanation as to why the Director does not consider it appropriate to make such captured document publicly available.

Requires the Director to make such captured documents available to the relevant congressional committees for review upon request of the Chairman of any of such congressional committees.

Requires the Director to make such captured documents available in either classified or unclassified form.

Requires the Director to begin making captured documents publicly available.

Requires the Director to make such captured documents available for review after the enactment of this Act.

Iran Sanctions Enhancement Act of 2007 - Amends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 to expand the sanctions to include the development of petroleum resources of Iran and export of refined petroleum to Iran.

Directs the President to impose sanctions if a person has: (1) made an investment of $20 million or more (or any combination of investments of at least $5 million each, which in the aggregate equals or exceeds $20 million in any 12-month period) that contributed to Iran's ability to develop petroleum resources of Iran; or (2) on or after December 31, 2007, provided Iran refined petroleum resources or engaged in an activity that could contribute to Iran's ability to import refined petroleum resources.

Directs the President to report to Congress on any person who has provided Iran with refined petroleum or any activity by any person that could contribute to Iran's ability to import refined petroleum resources.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Cultural Resource Programs at the National Park Service, to facilitate the development of guidelines and a program of technical assistance and grants that will set priorities for the preservation of the Route 66 corridor.  Requires the Secretary to designate officials of the National Park Service stationed at locations convenient to the States to perform the functions of the Cultural Resource Programs. 
Directs the Secretary to: (1) support efforts of State and local public and private persons, nonprofit Route 66 preservation entities, Indian tribes, State historic preservation offices, and entities in the States for the preservation of the Corridor by providing technical assistance, participating in cost-sharing programs, and making grants; (2) act as a clearinghouse for communication among Federal, State, and local agencies, nonprofit Route 66 preservation entities, Indian tribes, State historic preservation offices, and private persons and entities interested in the preservation of the Corridor; and (3) assist the States in determining the appropriate form of and establishing and supporting a non-Federal entity or entities to perform the functions of the Cultural Resource Programs after those programs are terminated. 
Directs the Secretary to develop a program of technical assistance in the preservation of the Corridor and interpretation of the Corridor.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for investment in stage 3 aircraft (aircraft that have not been installed in service with the taxpayer since the date of the original construction of the aircraft) for the cost of:  (1) aircraft modification; and (2) the cost of replacement parts.

Taking Account of Institutions with Low Operation Risk Act of 2015 or the TAILOR Act of 2015 This bill requires the Federal financial regulatory agencies to: (1) take into consideration the risk profile and business models of the various institutions or classes of institutions subject to the regulatory action, (2) determine the necessity, appropriateness, and impact of applying such regulatory action to such institutions or classes of institutions, and (3) tailor such action to such institutions or class of institutions in a manner that limits the regulatory compliance impact, cost, liability risk, and other burdens as is appropriate for the risk profile and model.  The bill also requires the agencies to: (1) disclose in every notice of proposed rulemaking and in any final rulemaking for a regulatory action how the agency has applied such requirements, and (2) individually report to Congress on the specific actions taken to tailor the agency's regulatory actions. The Financial Institutions Examination Council shall report to Congress on the extent to which regulatory actions tailored under this bill result in differential regulation of similarly-situated institutions of diverse charter types with respect to comparable regulations.

OPM may not make appropriations or otherwise make funds available for the pay of the Director of OMB, Deputy Director, and the Deputy Director for Management during any period of noncompliance with the budget process.  The OMB, the Deputy Director, and the Deputy Director may not receive pay for any period of noncompliance with the budget process after the end of that period.  OPM may not retroactively pay the Director after the end of the noncompliance period.

Technological Resource to Assist Criminal Enforcement (TRACE) Act - Amends the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act to require a licensed manufacturer or importer of firearms to: (1) test fire firearms manufactured or imported by such licensees; (2) prepare ballistics images of the fired bullet and cartridge casings; (3) make the records available to the Attorney General for entry into a computerized database; and (4) store the fired bullet and cartridge casings in such a manner and for such a period as the Attorney General by regulation.

Directs the Attorney General to assist firearm manufacturers and importers in complying with such requirements by: (1) acquiring, installing, and upgrading ballistics equipment and bullet and cartridge casing recovery equipment; (2) hiring or designating sufficient personnel to develop and maintain a ballistics database; (3) providing education about the role of ballistics; (4) providing for the coordination among law enforcement, regulatory agencies, and the firearm industry to curb firearm-related crime and illegal firearm trafficking; and (5) taking necessary steps to make ballistics testing effective.

Requires the Attorney General to: (1) establish a computer system through which state and local law enforcement agencies can promptly access ballistics records; and (2) require training for ballistics examiners.

Buy America Update Act - Amends Federal transportation law to require the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to: (1) review certain regulations and specifications of manufacturers of rolling stock to determine whether manufactured products other than steel and iron should be considered for purposes of domestic content preferences; and (2) initiate a rulemaking to develop audit procedures for the agency's review of offeror and recipient compliance with domestic content provisions.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) issue guidance on best practices for audits by recipients under such provisions; and (2) consider best practices for documentation requests from bidders by recipients to support certification of compliance from recipients to support pre-award and post-delivery audits by DOT.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) contract with the National Institute of Standards and Technology to conduct a supplier scouting process for compliant products for which a waiver will be sought; and (2) submit to the DOT a scouting report along with the waiver request.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) begin a supplier scouting process for compliant products for which a waiver will be sought; and (2) make the results of the supplier scouting available to the public.

Directs the Secretary of Education to discharge or cancel: (1) the Federal student loan indebtedness of an eligible spouse; (2) the consolidation loan indebtedness of an eligible surviving debtor; (3) the portion of the consolidation loan indebtedness of an eligible parent that was incurred on behalf of an eligible victim, if the amount of such indebtedness with respect to such victim may be reliably determined on the basis of records available to the lender; and (4) the PLUS loan indebtedness of an eligible parent that was incurred on behalf of an eligible victim who became (or becomes) permanently and totally disabled due to injuries suffered in the terrorist attack on September 11, 2001.

Eating Healthy at School Act of 2010 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to study and report to Congress on: (1) the effectiveness and efficiency of administrative review systems to ensure compliance with the school lunch and breakfast requirements of the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act and the school meal programs; (2) alternative processes and procedures for improving the effectiveness and efficiency of such review systems; and (3) the optimal frequency for carrying out reviews of such systems.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer to the Secretary specified amounts to carry out this Act.
Heavy Truck, Tractor, and Trailer Retail Federal Excise Tax Repeal Act of 2017 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the excise tax on heavy trucks, tractors, and trailers.

Rape Survivor Child Custody Act - Directs the Attorney General to make grants to states that have in place a law that allows the mother of any child that was conceived through rape to seek court-ordered termination of the parental rights of her rapist with regard to that child, which the court shall grant upon clear and convincing evidence of rape.

Terminates such grants for one year.

Women and Alcohol Research Equity Act of 1996 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism to obligate not less than $43,997,080 for the purpose of carrying out research on alcohol abuse and alcoholism among women.  Authorizes appropriations.

Airline Passenger Fairness Act - Amends Federal transportation law to require the Secretary of Transportation to include specific practices by a certified air carrier in the Department of Transportation's monthly Air Travel Consumer Report.

HSA Accessibility and Portability Act of 2006 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to authorize a health insurance issuer to elect, with respect to any small employer, instead of complying with the guaranteed issue requirement of the Act, to meet the requirements of this Act and provide coverage to an eligible individual of a small employer.

Requires an issuer to guarantee continuation of coverage to the individual (and to covered dependents), through issuance of individual health insurance coverage, after the date the individual no longer qualifies as an eligible individual of such employer.

Requires an issuer to furnish to the Secretary of Health and Human Services the information required by this Act to monitor the impact of an election on access to, and affordability of, health insurance coverage in the small group market and in the individual market.

Prohibits an election from being made for small employers only with respect to coverage of a small employer under health insurance coverage that consists of a high deductible health plan and a contribution to a health savings account.

Greater Sage Grouse Protection and Recovery Act of 2016 This bill prohibits the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture from making any finding of the Endangered Species Act of 1973 with respect to the Greater Sage Grouse in a state that has not enacted a state management plan for the protection and recovery of the Greater Sage Grouse. Until the state has enacted a management plan, the bill prohibits the Department and the Department from making any modification of any federal resource management plan applicable to federal land in the state.  The bill also prohibits the Department and the Department from extending any withdrawal, nor amending or otherwise modifying any federal resource management plan in a manner inconsistent with the state management plan for a period of at least five years.  The bill sets forth the governor's notification requirements for any state that has not enacted a state management plan.  The bill also prohibits any major federal action consistent with a state management plan from having a preclusive effect on the approval or implementation of the major federal action in that state.

Safe, Convenient, Reliable, Efficient, Effective, Next-Generation, Functional, and Secure TSA Act of 2016 or the SCREEN FAST Act - Directs the Administrator of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to establish a pilot program at three airports to reconfigure and install security systems that increase efficiency and reduce vulnerabilities in airport terminals, particularly at airports that have large open areas where screening is conducted. Directs the Administrator to: (1) select airports from among airports classified by the TSA as category X airports and that are able to begin the reconfiguration and installation of security systems expeditiously; and (2) give priority to an airport that submits a proposal that seeks federal funding for reconfiguration of the airport's security systems, has the space needed to reduce vulnerabilities and reconfigure the existing security systems, and is able to enter into a cost-sharing arrangement with the TSA under which the airport will provided 25% of the cost of the pilot program. Directs the TSA to establish a pilot program at three airports to develop and test prototypes of screening security systems and security checkpoint configurations to expedite the movement of passengers by deploying a range of technologies including passive and active systems, new types of security baggage and personal screening systems, and new systems to review and address passenger

Fort Stanton and Rio Bonito Corridor Vegetation Management Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior, in managing land within Fort Stanton and the Rio Bonito Corridor that is under the Secretary's jurisdiction, to solicit competitive bids for and enter into vegetation sales contracts for the purpose of using livestock grazing as a vegetation management tool.

Pay Accountability Act - Requires the payroll administrator of a House of Congress to withhold from the payments otherwise required to be made with respect to the pay period for the compensation of each Member of Congress serving in that House of Congress an amount equal to the product of one day's worth of pay under the annual rate of pay applicable to the Member under the legislative reorganization act of 1946 and the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown is in effect or the public debt limit is reached which occur during the pay period.

Requires the transfer of any withheld amounts to the Secretary of the Treasury in the event of a government shutdown.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to provide the House of Congress with assistance in order to enable the payroll administrators to carry out this Act.

Agricultural Credit Expansion Act - Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to provide for the eligibility of certain operating-only entities and certain embedded entities for farm loans.

Makes such entities eligible for farm operating loans.

Makes such entities eligible for emergency loans.

Breast Cancer Patient Education Act of 2012 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to provide for the planning and implementation of an education campaign to inform breast cancer patients regarding the availability and coverage of breast reconstruction, prostheses, and other options.

Requires such campaign to include dissemination of information regarding: (1) breast reconstruction is possible at the time of surgery or in a delayed fashion; (2) prostheses or breast forms may be available; (3) federal law mandates both public and private health plans to include coverage of breast reconstruction and prostheses; (4) the patient has a right to choose their provider of reconstructive care, including the potential transfer of care to a surgeon that provides breast reconstructive care; and (5) the patient may opt to undergo breast reconstruction in a delayed fashion for personal reasons, or after completion of all other breast cancer treatments.

Specifies that such campaign shall not be designed to limit the health care providers available to patients.

Judicial Transparency and Ethics Enhancement Act of 2006 - Establishes the Office of Inspector General for the Judicial Branch of the federal government to: (1) conduct investigations of matters pertaining to the Judicial Branch, including possible misconduct in office of judges and proceedings under this Act, that may require oversight or other action within the Judicial Branch or by Congress; (2) conduct and supervise audits and investigations; (3) prevent and detect waste, fraud, and abuse; and (4) recommend changes in laws or regulations governing the Judicial Branch.

Requires the Inspector General to have the power to: (1) make investigations and reports; (2) obtain information or assistance from any federal, state, or local governmental agency, or other entity, or unit thereof, including all information kept in the course of business by the Judicial Conference of the United States, the judicial councils of circuits, the Administrative Office of the United States Courts, and the U.S. Sentencing Commission; (3) require, by subpoena or otherwise, the attendance and testimony of witnesses, and the production of such books, records, correspondence memoranda, papers, and documents; (4) administer oaths, affirmations, or affidavits; (5) employ officers and employees, subject to the provisions governing

Cormorant Management and Natural Resources Protection Act - Amends the Migratory Bird Treaty Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to delegate authority to the governor of a State to the governor's state to implement management plans for cormorants in the state.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) approve or disapprove such a management plan if it is in accordance with U.S. obligations under treaties and federal law; and (2) provide the governor who submitted the plan the reasons for the disapproval and an opportunity to revise and resubmit the plan.

Requires the Secretary to review every five years each management plan approved for a state and the governor's exercise of delegated authority.

Authorizes the Secretary to revoke such approval and delegation if the Secretary determines that the plan or the governor's exercise of such authority is not in accordance with this Act or any treaty implemented by this Act.

Requires the Secretary to conduct educational and informational activities for the owners and operators of aquaculture facilities to improve their efforts to prevent cormorants from consuming aquatic species being reared in aquaculture facilities.

Tax Relief for Victims of Disasters Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make the natural person who is a taxpayer in a disaster area eligible for a special tax deduction for lost income if the area was declared a disaster area by the President on December 29, 2010; (2) make the natural person who is a taxpayer in a disaster area subject to a tax deduction for the housing expenses of a taxpayer who is displaced by the disaster; and (3) reduce the tax deduction for housing expenses for taxpayers taking into account the housing expenses of a taxpayer displaced by the disaster.

Defines "disaster area" as any area in the United States where at least 100,000 people have been displaced by natural disasters since 1992.

Hospice Evaluation and Legitimate Payment Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise the Medicare hospice benefit payment system to require a Medicare hospice physician, nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist, or other health professional, or other designated person, has a face-to-face encounter with the individual to determine continued eligibility of the individual for hospice care prior to the first 60-day period and each subsequent recertification under such system. National Neurological Diseases Surveillance System Act of 2010 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to: (1) enhance and expand infrastructure and activities to track the epidemiology of neurological diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease; and (2) incorporate information obtained through such activities into a National Neurological Diseases Surveillance System.

Requires the Secretary to ensure that the System is designed in a manner that facilitates further research on neurological diseases.

Requires the Secretary to provide for the collection and storage of information on neurological diseases, including information on demographics and other information associated with neurological diseases, risk factors, and diagnosis and progression markers.

Authorizes the Secretary to award grants to, or enter into contracts or cooperative agreements with, public or private nonprofit entities to carry out activities under this Act.

Requires the Secretary to make information and analysis in the System available to federal agencies, including the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and the Department of Defense (DOD).

Amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to require new penalties and administrator verification of eligibility for subsidy programs.

Requires the Secretary of Agriculture for a period of at least five years, or permanently, to deny the issuance of payments to the person or legal entity.

Requires the Secretary to request the Administrator of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to verify the average adjusted gross income, average adjusted gross farm income, and average adjusted gross nonfarm income of the person or legal entity.

Requires the Administrator to determine whether the average adjusted gross income, average adjusted gross farm income, and average adjusted gross nonfarm income of the person or legal entity is within the applicable limitations established under this Act.

Requires the Administrator to notify the results of such determination to the Secretary.

Requires a person or legal entity subject to such a denial to request a reconsideration of the denial by the Farm Service Agency (FSA) office serving the location in which the person or legal entity resides or operates.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer with long-term care needs a tax credit for $1,200 multiplied by the number of individuals who are eligible for such care.

Chickasaw National Recreation Area Land Exchange Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey all right, title, and interest in and to the Chickasaw National Recreational Area lands and interests therein, identified as Tract 102-25 on the Map, to the Chickasaw Nation.

Requires the fair market values of the Federal and non-Federal lands to be determined by an appraiser and the Chickasaw Nation.

Requires the conveyance of the non-Federal land to be authorized only if the City of Sulphur, Oklahoma, conveys all right, title, and interest in and to the non-Federal land to the Chickasaw Nation.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) revise the boundary of the Recreation Area to reflect such conveyance; and (2) administer the acquired lands in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Immigration Anti-Discrimination Improvement Act of 1993 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require the use of funds under such Act to be credited to the appropriation to be used in carrying out the Act. 
Authorizes appropriations for specified enforcement activities. 
Directs the Special Counsel for Immigration-Related Unfair Employment Practices to provide for agreements with Federal and State agencies involved with enforcement of laws relating to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of national origin under which such agencies would receive charges respecting unfair immigration-related employment practices and promptly forward such charges to the Special Counsel. 
Directs the Special Counsel to establish a national, toll-free telephone service to receive charges of unfair immigration-related employment practices and to provide for such outreach efforts. 
Directs the Attorney General to provide technical assistance to States and local governments concerning the provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act and the roles provided for receipt of charges of violations of such provisions. 
Directs the Special Counsel to establish a monitoring panel to monitor the application of the anti-discrimination provisions in the Act and to report to the Attorney General and the Congress.

Ronald Reagan Memorial Act of 2000 - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to establish the Ronald Reagan Memorial Commission to: (1) design and construct the memorial; (2) select a design for the memorial from proposals received from qualified American architects; and (3) issue a report to Congress and the President on its activities every six months after its first meeting and on a final report to Congress and the President, including a recommended location and final design for the memorial.

This bill directs the Department of the Interior to offer for sale to qualified entities, for fair market value, the remaining right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the land conveyed. Bodegas as Catalysts for Healthy Living Act - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to carry out a program under which the Administrator makes grants to: (1) a locally-based organization that represents small businesses; (2) a local redevelopment agency; and (3) a state or local government for assistance in carrying out certain activities related to small business ownership, including the provision of assistance in expanding inventory and consumer education and outreach activities.

Amends title XVIII (Medicare) and title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to provide for additional primary and preventive services under such programs.

The BEST unit shall be composed of at least one member of each of the following:   the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the geographically responsible Coast Guard Sector Intelligence Office;  the Coast Guard Sector Intelligence Office;  the Coast Guard  Sector Intelligence Office;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;  the Coast Guard Investigative Service;

Clean Energy Technology Manufacturing and Export Assistance Act of 2011 - Directs the Under Secretary for International Trade of the Department of Commerce to establish a Clean Energy Technology Manufacturing and Export Assistance Program to: (1) promote policies to reduce production costs and encourage innovation, investment, and productivity among U.S. businesses that produce or export clean energy technologies or related services; (2) implement a national strategy with respect to the exportation of clean energy technologies and related services from the United States; and (3) ensure that U.S. businesses that produce or export clean energy technologies and related services have the information and assistance necessary to compete and create and maintain clean energy technology jobs in the United States.

Requires the Under Secretary to report to Congress on the program's effectiveness in: (1) encouraging the production and exportation of clean energy technologies and related services in the United States; (2) encouraging the creation and maintenance of clean energy technology jobs in the United States; and (3) assisting U.S. businesses in exporting clean energy technologies and related services.

Medicare Certified Registered Nurse First Assistant Direct Reimbursement Act of 2001 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000, to provide for coverage of surgical first assisting services furnished by a certified registered nurse first assistant.

Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to extend through December 31, 2007, the Medicare prescription drug initial enrollment period for 2006 and 2007.

Suspends, through December 31, 2007, the late initial enrollment penalty through December 31, 2007.

Allows enrollees to change their enrollment into another prescription drug plan during the first 12 months of enrollment.

Prohibits the PDP sponsor of a prescription drug plan from removing a covered part D drug from the plan or imposing a restriction or limitation on coverage (such as through the application of a preferred status, usage restriction, step therapy, prior authorization, or quantity limitation) other than at the beginning of each plan year, except as the Secretary of Health and Human Services permits to take into account new therapeutic uses and newly covered part D drugs.

Requires the PDP sponsor of a prescription drug plan to provide notice of any such changes to affected enrollees, physicians, pharmacies, and pharmacists.

Waco Mammoth National Monument Establishment Act of 2011 - Establishes the Waco Mammoth National Monument in Texas as a unit of the National Park System.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into cooperative management agreements with Baylor University and the city of Waco, Texas, to acquire by donation any land or interest in land owned by Baylor.

Requires the Secretary to complete a general management plan for the Monument.

Prohibits the use of federal funds to pay the costs of: (1) carrying out a cooperative agreement, (2) acquiring land for inclusion in the Monument, (3) developing a visitor center, (4) operating or maintaining the Monument, (5) constructing exhibits, or (6) developing the general management plan.

Terminates the designation of the Monument as a unit of the National Park System if federal funds are required to operate and maintain the Monument.

Methane Hydrate Research and Development Amendments Act of 2015 This bill amends the Methane Hydrate Research and Development Act of 2000 to modify the methane hydrate research and development program.  The bill authorizes the Department of Energy (DOE) to award grants to, or enter into contracts or cooperative agreements with, institutions that:   conduct basic and applied research to identify, explore, assess, and develop methane hydrate as a commercially viable source of energy;  identify and characterize methane hydrate resources using remote sensing and seismic data, including the characterization of hydrate concentrations in marine reservoirs in the Gulf of Mexico or the Atlantic Ocean Basin by the date that is four years after the enactment of this bill;  develop technologies required for efficient and environmentally sound development of methane hydrate resources;  conduct basic and applied research to assess and mitigate the environmental impact of hydrate degassing (including natural degassing and degassing associated with commercial development);  develop technologies to reduce the risks of drilling through methane hydrates;  conduct exploratory drilling, well testing, and production testing operations on permafrost and nonpermafrost gas hydrates in support of the activities authorized by this bill, including drilling of a test well and performing a long-term hydrate production test on land in the United States Arctic region by

Local Emergency Health Services Reimbursement Act of 2002 - Amends the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 to provide for allotments to States based on the highest number of undocumented aliens and the number of undocumented aliens apprehended in each fiscal year.

Student Credit Card Transparency Act of 2009 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to require each creditor to submit an annual report to the Board containing the terms and conditions of all business, marketing, and promotional agreements and college affinity card agreements with an institution of higher education or an alumni organization or foundation affiliated with or related to such institution, with respect to any college student credit card issued to such institution.

Requires the Comptroller General to review periodically the reports submitted by creditors and the marketing practices of creditors to determine the impact that college affinity card agreements and college student card agreements have on credit card debt.

Small Business Jobs Act of 2015  Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers in a small business tax credit for the wages of employees hired by such employer.  The credit applies to wages paid or incurred in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2015.

Gas Price and Refinery Capacity Relief Act of 2013 - Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to revise the definition of "planned refinery outage" to mean a refinery's removal, scheduled before the date on which the removal occurs, of a refinery's or any unit of a refinery's service for maintenance, repair, or modification. Requires the owner or operator of a refinery to submit to the Administrator of the Energy Information Administration (EIA) information describing: (1) the refinery's schedule for any planned refinery outage, including the dates for the planned refinery outage at least one year in advance of the date of the expected outage; and (2) the estimated inventories and production of refined petroleum products during the period in which the planned refinery outage occurs. Requires the Administrator, on an ongoing basis, to: (1) review information on planned refinery outages and unplanned refinery outages; (2) analyze that information to determine whether the scheduling of a planned refinery outage or an unplanned refinery outage may substantially affect the price or supply of any refined petroleum product by decreasing the production of the refined petroleum product and causing or contributing to a retail or wholesale supply shortage or disruption; and (3) alert the Secretary of any refinery outage that

School-Based Respiratory Health Management Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to give additional preference to a State that requires that each public elementary school and secondary school in the State: (1) has in place a plan for having on the premises a school nurse or one or more other school personnel trained in the administration of emergency medical services for all school-related emergencies; and (2) has in place a comprehensive school-based allergy and reversible lower airway disorders management program that includes a method to identify all students of the school with allergies and an individual student allergies and reversible lower airway disorders action plan for each student.

Requires the Secretary to give such State additional preference also to a student who is reasonably believed to have an allergy or disorder.

Includes at least short-acting bronchodilators in the list of medications the Secretary may give to a student reasonably believed to have a diagnosis of allergies or disorder.

USDA Civil Rights Resolution Act of 2000 - Amends the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1999 to authorize the Director of the Bureau of Agriculture and Food Research to waive the time limit to review a complaint by a complainant if the complainant seeks a determination by the Department of Agriculture (USDA) on the merits of the complaint within 270 days after the complaint has been investigated by USDA. Authorizes the complainant to petition the Civil Rights Division of the Department of Justice (DOJ) to review the complaint and make recommendations to the USDA to resolve it. Directs the DOJ to conduct the review within 30 days after the complainant files a petition. Makes DOJ the review facility.
Amends the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 to modify the goal of the take reduction plans of commercial fishermen.

Rapid DNA Act of 2014 - Amends the DNA Identification Act of 1994 to revise the definition of "reference DNA sample" to include tissue, fluid, or other bodily sample of an individual on which a DNA analysis can be carried out. Defines "sample-to-answer DNA analysis systems" as fully automated systems that after input of a DNA sample can perform all necessary sample preparation and analysis with no operator intervention. Revises the definition of "qualified agency" to require a qualified agency to: (1) be a law enforcement organization, including a detention center, outside of forensic laboratories, and a facility that can perform DNA analysis using sample-to-answer DNA systems; and (2) be trained to operate a sample-to-answer DNA system. Defines "qualified agencies" as booking stations, jails, prisons, detention centers, other law enforcement organizations, and facilities outside of forensic laboratories that can perform DNA analysis using sample-to-answer systems. Revises the definition of "qualified laboratory" to require a qualified laboratory to be one that can perform DNA analysis using sample-to-answer systems. New Economy Workforce Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make available to certain family-sponsored immigrant students in the United States a program of priority for diversity immigration. 
Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require the Secretary of State to promulgate regulations regarding the allocation of immigrant visas, made available under the Immigration and Nationality Act, pursuant to the amendments made by this Act. 
Requires the Attorney General to promulgate regulations implementing the amendments made by this Act. 
Directs the Attorney General and the Secretary of Education to make available revised forms, as appropriate, that prominently include instructions regarding procedures for establishing an alien's level of educational attainment for purposes of the amendments made by this Act.

Preserving Access to Manufactured Housing Act of 2013 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to redefine the meaning of "mortgage originator" to include a retailer of manufactured or modular homes or its employees.  Amends the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act to revise requirements for disclosure of greater amount or percentage of a loan amount (currently, for a personal property transaction) that is high-cost mortgage.  Amends the Truth in Lending Act to revise requirements for high-cost mortgages to require a first mortgage on a consumer's principal dwelling that is considered personal property (or is a consumer credit transaction that does not include the purchase of real property on which the dwelling is to be placed) to exceed the average prime offer rate for a comparable transaction by more than: (1) 8.5% in the case of a transaction in an amount of $50,000 or more, but less than $75,000 (as such amounts are adjusted by the Bureau to reflect the change in the Consumer Price Index); (2) 10.5% in the case of a transaction in an amount of more than $30,000, but less than $50,00

Marine Mammal Rescue Assistance Act of 1999 - Amends the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 to direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish the John H. Prescott Marine Mammal Rescue Assistance Grant Program to provide grants to eligible stranding network participants for the recovery or treatment of marine mammals, the collection of data from living or dead marine mammals for scientific research regarding marine mammal health, and facility operation costs that are directly related to those purposes. Directs the Secretary to establish an advisory group to advise the Secretary regarding the implementation of this Act. Limits the amount of a grant to $100,000.  Authorizes appropriations.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude dividends from investment income.

Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area Act of 2014 - Establishes in Utah, the Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area, a specified Bureau of Land Management (BLM) land management area.  Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the BLM, to: (1) administer the Area and parcel of BLM land identified as "Proposed Exchange Parcel"; and (2) allow only uses of the Area that are consistent with the purposes of the Area.  Requires the land to remain open, in perpetuity, to the use of off-highway vehicles.  Requires the BLM to: (1) accept the offer of conveying to the United States title to non-federal land, and (2) convey to the State all interest in the Federal land.  Requires the non-federal land to be added to, and administered by, the Area as part of, the Recreation Area.

Drug Price Competition Act of 2009 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to exclude from the first application for approval of a new drug (first applicant) and from subsequent applications (non-applicant) any drug that: (1) is submitted for approval on the first day on which a certification for the drug is submitted to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as the first applicant; (2) submits a certification for the drug that is lawfully maintained or a statement for each unexpired patent for which a first applicant had submitted a certification; and (3) has not been previously evaluated in a phase 1/2 trial in a manner that would result in a significant adverse effect on the efficacy or safety of the drug.

Veterans' Compensation Rate Amendments of 2001 - Makes specified increases in veterans' compensation rates.Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to increase the rates of veterans' disability compensation.Provides additional compensation for veterans' dependents.Makes the following veterans eligible for the additional compensation: (1) service as a member of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard; and (2) at the applicable time designated by this Act, Chairman or Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Chief of Staff of the Army, Chief of Naval Operations, Chief of Staff of the Air Force, Commandant of the Marine Corps, or Commandant of the Coast Guard.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior to offer to enter into cooperative agreements with the University of New Mexico to lease the Chacoan Archaeological Museum in New Mexico to the National Park Service for storage, research, and offices.
Authorizes appropriations.

Workplace Religious Freedom Act of 1999 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to define "employee" to include a prospective employee, an "undue hardship accommodation," an employer's "committed unlawful employment practice," and an "accommodation by the employer" for an employee if the accommodation will result in the employee's inability to perform the essential functions of the employment position. 
Declares that an accommodation by the employer shall not be deemed to be reasonable if it does not remove the conflict between employment requirements and the employee's religious observance or practice. 
Requires an employer to provide reasonable accommodation to an employee if the employer refuses to permit the employee to utilize leave of general usage to remove such a conflict solely because the leave will be used to accommodate the employee's religious observance or practice. 
Declares that an employer shall not be required to pay premium wages or confer premium benefits for work performed during hours to which such premium wages or premium benefits would ordinarily be applicable, if work is performed during such hours only to accommodate religious requirements of an employee. 
Declares that the term "premium benefit" includes overtime pay and compensatory time off, premium pay for night, weekend, or holiday work, and premium pay

National Fish and Wildlife Policy Fellowship Program Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to award fellowships to qualified graduate and post-graduate level students engaged in advanced degree programs concerning freshwater and anadromous fish, wildlife, conservation management, or biology.

Requires the Secretary to seek to achieve, with respect to fish and wildlife conservation, specified educational and training objectives.

Requires the fellowships to be awarded pursuant to guidelines established by the Secretary.

Requires the Director of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to administer such fellowships.

Voluntary Protection Program Act - Directs the Secretary of Labor to enter into cooperative agreements with employers to encourage establishment of comprehensive safety and health management systems that include: (1) requirements for systematic assessment of hazards; (2) comprehensive hazard prevention, mitigation, and control programs; (3) active and meaningful management and employee participation in the voluntary program; and (4) employee safety and health training.

Directs the Secretary to establish and carry out a voluntary protection program to encourage excellence and recognize its achievement in: (1) the technical and managerial protection of employees from occupational hazards; and (2) the achievement of excellence in both the technical and managerial protection of employees.

Requires employers who volunteer for the program to be required to submit an application to the Secretary to demonstrate that the worksite meets such requirements for program participation.

Requires periodic reevaluations by the Secretary of Labor of the employers for continued participation.

Scotchman Peaks Wilderness of 2016 This bill designates certain land in Idaho as the Scotchman Peaks Wilderness and as the wilderness and as a component of the National Wilderness Preservation System.  The bill prohibits the wilderness and the component from being treated equally.  The bill withdraws the wilderness and component from Idaho.  The Department of Agriculture may carry out management activities to maintain or restore fish and wildlife populations and habitat to support fish and wildlife populations within the wilderness.  The bill allows the Department to take measures within the wilderness to protect the privacy of the members of the Indian tribes.  The bill requires the Department to ensure that the wilderness and the wilderness and its associated lands are accessible to the public.

Federal Land Exchange Improvement Act of 1995 - Amends the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to exchange up to equal amounts of real and personal property for the purchase of certain land. 
Requires the Secretary concerned to:  (1) make an environmental assessment of any such exchange; and (2) complete such an exchange within one year. 
Requires the Secretary concerned to:  (1) complete the processing of any land exchange; and (2) make a final decision on any exchange within one year from the date of submission of the application for the exchange. 
Allows the Secretary concerned to dispose of lands by exchange to make such minor adjustments to the boundary of a unit of the public lands or the National Forest System as may be necessary to reflect actual conditions in the unit which are not of comparable character to the unit. 
Amends the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act to authorize the Secretary of Agriculture to waive the requirements of this Act that lands be sold, exchanged, or granted only to public authorities and agencies and only on condition that the property is used for public purposes after the Secretary consults with the head of any other Federal agency that has a property interest in the

Reciprocity and Fairness in Foreign Investment Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to issue regulations as necessary to carry out this Act.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to impose civil penalties for violations of this Act.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to report annually to the Congress on the laws of each foreign country regarding permissible investment by foreign persons in enterprises organized under the laws of the country and in real property in that country and permissible control by foreign persons of operations and management of critical infrastructure in that country.

Sets forth standards for arbitrators.  Requires use of the mechanism whenever at least one party to the dispute requests.  Requires each party to pay its own costs and the arbitration and other administrative costs of arbitration to be equally split between and among the parties.  Requires any party to a dispute to have an unqualified right to appeal any decision to the Board. Requires each party to pay its own costs and the arbitration and other administrative costs of arbitration to be equally split between and among the parties.  Requires the Board to adopt a final decision within 180 days after being appointed.

Authorizes the Architect of the Capitol to construct, operate, and maintain on a reimbursable basis battery recharging stations in parking areas under the jurisdiction of the House of Representatives on Capitol Grounds for use by Members of the House of Representatives or covered employees.

Authorizes the Architect to use one or more vendors on a commission basis.

Requires the Architect to charge fees or charges for electricity provided to Members and covered employees sufficient to cover the Architect's costs to carry out this Act.

Authorizes the Architect to establish and adjust fees or charges after: (1) submission of written notice detailing the number and locations of the stations to the appropriate House Committee; and (2) approval by that Committee.

Requires the Architect to report on the financial administration and cost recovery of activities under this Act with respect to that fiscal year to the appropriate House Committee.

Requires the Architect to submit a report to the appropriate House Committee determining whether Members (including any Delegate or Resident Commissioner to Congress) and covered employees using battery charging stations are receiving a subsidy from the taxpayers.

Limits the source of payments received from a borrower or related party under such Act to a loan or other debt obligation that is made or guaranteed by the Federal Government.

No Qualified Teacher Left Behind Act of 2004 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to revise the eligibility requirements for highly qualified teachers in rural schools.

Requires a plan developed by a state or local educational agency (LEA) to ensure that all rural elementary and secondary school teachers are highly qualified to teach in such schools to ensure that rural teachers are highly qualified to teach in core academic subjects.

Requires LEAs to make grants to rural school districts to hire experienced teachers who teach in core academic subjects and to provide other support services to rural teachers.

Housing Opportunity and Mortgage Equity Act of 2013 - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to each carry out a program to provide for the refinancing of qualified mortgages on single-family housing owned by such enterprises through a refinancing mortgage, and for the purchase of and securitization of such refinancing mortgages, in accordance with policies and procedures that the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) shall establish. Requires such refinancing mortgage to be a mortgage that: (1) is an existing first mortgage that was made for purchase of, or refinancing another first mortgage on, a one-to four-family dwelling; (2) is owned or guaranteed by the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) or the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac); and (3) was originated on or before the enactment of this Act.  Requires such refinancing mortgage to have a principal loan repayment of which is secured by the mortgage and be used to satisfy all indebtedness under an existing qualified mortgage.  Requires the principal loan amount repayment of which is secured by the mortgage to be used to satisfy all indebtedness under an existing qualified mortgage. National Nurse Act of 2011 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to establish within the Office of the Surgeon General the National Nurse for Public Health.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to appoint the National Nurse for Public Health in accordance with Commissioned Corps Instruction CC23.4.6 (relating to Chief Professional Officer Nominations).

Requires the National Nurse for Public Health, in cooperation with the Surgeon General, to: (1) provide leadership and coordination of Public Health Service nursing professional affairs for the Office of the Surgeon General and other service agencies; (2) represent the Surgeon General and the service agencies in communications with groups and societies concerned with nursing issues at the local, state, national, and international levels; (3) provide guidance and advice to the Surgeon General and the Nurse Professional Advisory Committee on matters such as standards, recruitment, retention, readiness, and career development of nurses employed by and contracted with service agencies; (4) conduct media campaigns and make personal appearances for purposes of such responsibilities; (5) provide guidance and leadership for activities to promote the public health; and (6) provide guidance and leadership for activities that will increase public safety and emergency preparedness.

White House Inspector General Act of 1996 - Amends the Inspector General Act of 1978 to establish the position of Inspector General of the Executive Office of the President.  Directs the President to appoint an Inspector General of the Executive Office of the President.  Specifies that the Inspector General of the Executive Office of the President shall be under the President's authority, direction, and control regarding audits or investigations, or the issuance of subpoenas, which require access to information concerning:  (1) ongoing criminal investigations or proceedings; (2) undercover operations; (3) the identity of confidential sources; (4) deliberations and decisions on policy matters; (5) intelligence or counterintelligence matters; or (6) other matters the disclosure of which would constitute a serious threat to the national security or cause significant impairment to the national interests of the United States.  Authorizes the President to prohibit the Inspector General from carrying out or completing any audit or investigation, or issuing any subpoena, after the Inspector General has decided to initiate, carry out, or complete such audit or investigation or to issue such subpoena, if the disclosure of such information would interfere with the core functions of the constitutional responsibilities of the President and the prohibition is necessary to prevent the disclosure

Ensuring Quality in the Unemployment Insurance Program (EQUIP) Act This bill amends title III (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require the state law of a state to provide no regular compensation to an applicant for unemployment compensation (UOC) before the receipt of any such compensation: (1) if the applicant has completed a substance abuse risk assessment; and (2) if the state determines that the applicant is a high-risk applicant based on the results of such assessment. If a high-risk applicant tests positive for any controlled substance: (1) no regular compensation may be paid to such applicant for 30 days; and (2) no regular compensation may be paid to such applicant during the remainder of such benefit year, unless the applicant tests negative for controlled substances at the end of the period. A high-risk applicant who is determined to have a high risk of substance abuse must be responsible for the cost of such test if the individual tests positive for any controlled substance. The bill also prohibits the state from paying merit staffing requirements to the Board for the purpose of implementing such requirements.

Olympic Commemorative Coins Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to:  (1) make biennially five-year periodic Olympic coins; and (2) develop an expanded multi-coin commemorative coins program in consultation with the Olympic Committee and the Citizens Commemorative Coin Advisory Committee. 
Prohibits the Secretary from issuing other commemorative coins during the first two months of each period in which the Olympic Games are held in a nation other than the United States. 
Requires the Secretary to obtain silver for minting Olympic coins from sources determined to be appropriate, including stockpiles established under the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act. 
Requires the Secretary to determine the costs incurred with respect to Olympic coins, including overhead costs. 
Mandates that the Secretary determine the estimated profit to be included in the sale price of each coin. 
Prohibits judicial review of the procurement of goods and services necessary to carry out the Olympic programs and operations. 
Expresses the sense of the Congress that each Olympic coin should be self-sustaining and should be administered so as not to result in any net cost to the Numismatic Public Enterprise Fund.

Bridge Ice and Snow Prevention Pilot Program Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish and implement a pilot program to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of the use of technologies to prevent ice, snow, and other adverse weather effects associated with freezing temperatures on bridges on the National Highway System (NHS).

Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to up to five states to conduct projects under the pilot program.

Requires the Secretary to select not more than 20 highway bridges for participation in the program.

Directs the Secretary to select technologies that are likely to improve bridge safety, extend the life of a bridge, and promote energy efficiency.

Requires the Federal share of a project carried out under the pilot program to not exceed 80% of the total cost of the project.

Requires the Secretary to carry out the pilot program for a period of no more than five fiscal years.

Authorizes appropriations.

Strategic Deterrent Sustainment Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to report to the congressional defense and appropriations committees on the capability of the U.S. industrial base to achieve specified levels of each of the following: (1) to maintain, modernize, and sustain the Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) system until at least 2030; (2) to replace the ICBM with a follow-on land-based strategic deterrent system after 2030; and (3) to maintain the ICBM system after 2030 and replace it with a follow-on land-based strategic deterrent system after 2030.

Requires the Comptroller General to report to such committees on the Comptroller General's assessment of the matters contained in the report, including an assessment of the consistency of the President's FY2009 budget with the matters contained in such report.

Television Violence Reduction Through Parental Empowerment Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require that:  (1)  apparatus designed to receive television signals be equipped with circuitry designed to enable viewers to block the display of channels, programs, and time slots; and (2) such circuitry enable viewers to block display of all programs with a common rating. 
Requires such requirements to apply when such circuitry is manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States and its television picture screen is 13 inches or greater. 
Prohibits the shipment of such apparatus in interstate commerce, manufacture, assembling, or importing from any foreign country into the United States, any such apparatus except in accordance with rules prescribed by the Federal Communications Commission. 
Requires the Federal Communications Commission to promulgate rules to implement such amendments within 180 days after its enactment.

Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund Amendments Act of 1997 - Amends the Solid Waste Disposal Act to direct the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to distribute to States at least 85 percent of the funds appropriated to the Environmental Protection Agency from the Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund each fiscal year for the reasonable costs under cooperative agreements for:  (1) States' actions under such Act; (2) necessary administrative expenses directly related to corrective action and compensation programs under such Act; and (3) enforcement of a State or local program under such Act or similar State or local provisions by a State or local government.  Prohibits the use of such funds by States for purposes of providing financial assistance to an owner or operator in meeting such requirements or State programs under such Act.  Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) the process for a State that the Administrator has entered into a cooperative agreement with under such Act; and (2) the cost recovery rules for such agreements.  Prohibits the Administrator from revising such allocation process after consulting with State agencies responsible for overseeing corrective action for releases from underground storage tanks and with representatives of owners and operators of leaking underground storage tanks.  Makes such funds provided to States owners or operators for such programs not

Jobs Now Act of 2017 This bill amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to direct the Department of Labor to carry out a two-year pilot program to award competitive grants to units of general local government or community-based organizations to retain, employ, or train employees providing a public service for such units.  The grants may be used to: (1) retain or train employees who are providing a public service for the units, and (2) employ or train individuals with disabilities, unemployed or otherwise, or displaced workers.

Helping Individuals Return to Employment Act or the HIRE Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to eligible entities in specified areas to hire unemployed individuals to benefit communities.

Allows such grants to be awarded to entities located in or primarily serving in: (1) a renewal community; (2) an empowerment zone; (3) a historically underutilized business zone; or (4) a designated business zone.

Requires such grants to be used to hire unemployed individuals residing in such areas, including individuals age 16 and older, with priority going to individuals who have been unemployed for more than a year.

Prohibits an individual whose employment is funded under a grant from working for an employer at which a collective bargaining agreement is in effect covering the same or similar work, unless: (1) the consent of the employer is obtained; and (2) negotiations have taken place as to the terms and conditions of such employment.

Prohibits an individual whose employment is funded under this Act from displacing other employees whose employment is not funded under this Act.

Prohibits a grant recipient from hiring an employee or employees with funds under this Act for any employment which the grant recipient would otherwise hire an employee who has been furloughed.

Prohibits

Congressional Medal of Honor Memorial Coin Act of 2003 - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to mint and issue $5 gold coins and $1 silver coins emblematic of the values and abilities necessary to earn the Congressional Medal of Honor.

Requires the design of such coins to be selected by the Secretary after consultation with the Commission of Fine Arts and the Citizens Coinage Advisory Committee.

Authorizes the Secretary to issue such coins only during the period beginning on January 1, 2005, and ending on December 31, 2005.

Requires the proceeds from such surcharges to be paid promptly to the Riverside National Cemetery Support Committee, a nonprofit organization established under the laws of California, for the purposes of: (1) maintaining the National Medal of Honor Memorial at Riverside National Cemetery; and (2) constructing and maintaining such memorials as the Cemetery and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs may jointly designate.

Amends Federal bankruptcy law to provide for priority of claims for the reimbursement of retired Federal employees and their spouses and dependents for medical, surgical, or hospital care benefits under any plan, fund, or program maintained or established by the debtor prior to filing a petition commencing a case under this title. 
Provides for the priority of claims for such retirees and their dependents in the order specified in the bankruptcy case file. 
Provides for the priority of claims for retirees and dependents in the liquidation of a bankruptcy case in which the debtor has already provided such benefits.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt an organization from tax for disclosures of the identities of its officers, directors, trustees, and highly compensated employees involved in a terror finance scheme.

Eating Disorders Awareness, Prevention, and Education Act of 2003 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to require the Secretary of Education to carry out a program to develop, distribute, and promote the broadcasting of public service announcements to improve public awareness, and to promote the identification and prevention, of eating disorders.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to study the impact eating disorders have on educational advancement and achievement.

Extends the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 (FSRAI) through FY2009.

Defines the term "crop program" to include all programs under the FSRAI, including crop insurance, direct spending programs, and authority and appropriations programs.

Defines "automatic one-year extension" and "conditional additional year extension" for each direct spending program or authority under the FSRAI.

Defines "automatic extension" for each authorization of appropriations contained in the FSRAI or an amendment made by such Act that would otherwise expire on September 30, 2007.

Defines "automatic extension" for each authorization of appropriations contained in the FSRAI, or an amendment made by such Act, that is deemed to expire on September 30, 2008.

Defines "automatic extension" for each authorization of appropriations contained in the FSRAI, or an amendment made by such Act, that is deemed to expire on September 30, 2009.
