Voluntary Opportunities for Increasing Contributions to Education Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 75 percent of the charitable contributions of the taxpayer for the taxable year. Limits such credit to $500 for individuals and $100,000 for corporations.

Veterinary Workforce Expansion Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to award competitive grants to eligible entities to improve public health preparedness through increasing the number of veterinarians in the workforce.

Requires the Secretary to give preference to applicants that: (1) demonstrate a comprehensive approach by involving more than one school of veterinary medicine, department of comparative medicine, department of veterinary science, school of public health, or school of medicine that offers postgraduate training for veterinarians in a public health practice area; and (2) increase capacity in research on high priority disease agents or in other areas necessary to prepare for such a position.

Second Chance Voting Rights Act of 2006 - Provides that the right of an individual who is a citizen of the United States to vote in any federal election shall not be denied or abridged because that individual has been convicted of a criminal offense.

Authorizes the Attorney General to obtain declaratory or injunctive relief to remedy a violation of this Act.

Authorizes a person aggrieved by a violation of this Act to provide written notice of the violation to the chief election official of the state involved.

Authorizes a person aggrieved by a violation of this Act to obtain declaratory or injunctive relief with respect to the violation within 90 days after receipt of such notice if the violation occurred within 120 days before the date of an election for federal office.

Provides that a person who is entitled to relief under this Act may obtain such relief in a civil action.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax deduction for interest on qualified medical education loans by qualified medical professionals practicing in rural areas.

Cocopah Lands Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior to take specified lands in Yuma County, Arizona, into trust for the Cocopah Indian Tribe if the Tribe transfers title to such land to the Secretary.

States that if the transfer of title to such land does not result in environmental conditions or contamination related concerns and no adverse legal claims to such land, the land shall be considered to be part of the Tribe's initial reservation.

Prohibits the use of such land for gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

National Icebreaker Fund Act of 2015 This bill establishes the National Icebreaker Fund in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to be used for the construction, alteration, and renovation of icebreakers for the Coast Guard, as well as for lease or charter of icebreakers.  DHS may transfer any unobligated funds remaining from funds under DHS's administrative control.  DHS may accept from foreign governments, or international organizations, any contribution of money, personal property, or assistance in-kind for support of icebreaking in the polar regions.  DHS may not use funds in any other way to lease, charter, construct, alter, renovate, or in any other way acquire any vessel built in a foreign country.  DHS may expend from the Fund amounts deposited, as well as amounts deposited for activities for lease or charter of icebreakers, only for the lease, charter, construction, alteration, or renovation of icebreakers capable of search and rescue, saving life at sea, maritime safety and security, drug and migrant interdiction, fisheries law enforcement, and environmental response in the Arctic.  No part of an appropriation that is deposited in the Fund shall remain available for more than ten years after the end of FY2010.

Authorizes the United States-Mexico Border Health Commission to:  (1) conduct a needs assessment in the United States-Mexico border area for identifying, evaluating, preventing, and resolving health problems that affect the general population; (2) implement actions recommended by the needs assessment by assisting in the coordination of efforts of public and private persons to prevent and resolve such problems, educating the population concerning such problems, and developing and implementing programs to prevent and resolve such problems and educating the population concerning such problems where a program is necessary to meet a need that is not being met by other public or private persons; and (3) formulate recommendations to the governments of the United States and Mexico concerning a fair and reasonable method by which the government of one country would reimburse a public or private person in the other country for the cost of a health care service furnished by the person to a citizen or resident alien of the first country who is unable, through insurance or otherwise, to pay the service. 
Requires the Commission to establish at least two regional border offices in locations selected by the Commission. 
Directs the Commission to submit an annual report to both the U.S. and Mexican governments regarding Commission activities.

Authorizes the Secretary of Education to award a grant to Teach For America, Inc., the national teacher corps of recent college graduates who commit to teach for two years in underserved communities in the United States.

EQIP Improvement Act of 2018 This bill amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to extend through FY2018 the Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP).  The bill amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to extend through FY2018 the Food and Nutrition Act of 1990, the National Food Marketing Act of 1969, and the National Organic Program of the Department of Agriculture (USDA).  The bill amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to extend through FY2018 the program for the conservation of energy derived from biomass and the conservation of soil and water.  The bill amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to extend through FY2018 the program for the conservation of wildlife habitat.  The bill amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to extend through FY2018 the program for the conservation of water and the allocation of funding for wildlife habitat.

Directs the Secretary of Transportation to investigate and hold a public hearing on a petition by the sponsor of a commercial service airport (or by the attorney general of a State on behalf of one or more persons, including governmental entities, with respect to an airport) claiming that fares for scheduled air transportation at the airport are unreasonably high or that competition between air carriers is inadequate.

Requires a hearing to be held in the community served by the airport if practicable.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) hold a hearing in the community served by the airport if requested in the petition and if practicable; and (2) provide written findings in response to such petitions, including findings as to whether air carrier costs to provide air transportation at the airport appear substantially higher than at comparable airports, whether barriers to entry are discouraging or preventing other air carriers from initiating competitive air transportation at the airport, and whether any programs under the Secretary's authority could be helpful to airports in marketing their facilities to air carriers, reducing fares for air transportation, or minimizing barriers to entry by other air carriers seeking to provide air transportation at the airport.

Authorizes the Secretary to decide not to conduct a subsequent investigation and public hearing in response to a new petition.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on the results

Jason's Law - Directs the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to implement a pilot program to address the shortage of long-term parking for commercial motor vehicles on the National Highway System (NHS).

Requires the Secretary to allocate funds among States, metropolitan planning organizations, and local governments.

Requires funds allocated to be used for projects that serve NHS and may include construction of: (1) safety rest areas that include parking for commercial motor vehicles; (2) commercial motor vehicle parking facilities adjacent to commercial truck stops and travel plazas; (3) the opening of existing facilities to commercial motor vehicle parking; (4) the promotion of the availability of publicly or privately provided commercial motor vehicle parking on NHS; (5) construction of turnouts along NHS for commercial motor vehicles; (6) making capital improvements to public commercial motor vehicle parking facilities that are closed on a seasonal basis; and (7) improvement of the geometric design of interchanges on NHS to improve access to commercial vehicle parking facilities.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to applicants that: (1) demonstrate a severe shortage of commercial motor vehicle parking capacity in the corridor to be addressed; (2) have consulted with affected State and local governments, community groups, private providers of commercial motor vehicle parking, and motorist and truck

Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to carry out a program of training to provide eligible veterans with skills relevant to the job market.

Requires the Secretary to enter into contracts with employers to provide programs of apprenticeship or on-the-job training for veterans who are not otherwise eligible for education or training services.

Authorizes appropriations for FY2009-FY2018.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the expensing allowance for Gulf Opportunity Zone property.

Enhanced Veteran Healthcare Experience Act of 2011 - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) the current health care system of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is neither fiscally efficient nor effective in providing easily accessible treatment for all veterans; (2) health care can be provided more efficiently to provide veterans with care that is available closer to where they live and to allow veterans more flexibility in choosing their own doctors; and (3) better health care can be provided to veterans at little-to-no increased cost to the taxpayer by replacing the VA fee-based care system with the veterans enhanced care program.

Directs the Secretary of Veterans to provide an eligible veteran with covered health services provided by a non-VA provider if the Secretary determines that the VA is not capable of providing such services because of geographical inaccessibility or the lack of required personnel, resources, or ability.

Authorizes the Secretary to contract with a non-VA provider if the provider demonstrates the ability to provide non-VA health care services to veterans.

Requires the Secretary to submit to the congressional veterans committees a report on care provided under this Act, including: (1) the cost to the VA; (2) the number of veterans receiving care; (3) the

National Fab Lab Network Act of 2013 - Directs the National Fab Lab Network (NFLN) to facilitate the creation of a national network of local fab labs and serve as a resource to assist stakeholders with the effective operation of fab labs.

Post-Deployment Health Assessment Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to provide for in-person mental health screenings to each member of the Armed Forces who is deployed in connection with a contingency operation at a time during the period beginning 180 days before the date of deployment in connection with the contingency operation and ending 90 days before the date of deployment in connection with the contingency operation.

Excludes from such mental health screenings certain members who were not subjected or exposed to combat stress during deployment.

Requires the Secretary to share with the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) information derived from confidential mental health screenings, including mental health screenings provided pursuant to such provisions, as the Secretary and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs jointly consider appropriate to ensure continuity of mental health care and treatment of members of the Armed Forces during their transition from health care and treatment provided by the Department of Defense (DOD) to health care and treatment provided by the VA.

Requires the Secretary to submit to Congress a report on the guidance provided by the Secretary and the military departments to achieve the purpose of such screenings.

Drinking Water Affordability Act of 2016 This bill amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to revise the national primary drinking water regulation to require the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to transfer ownership of any water treatment plant that has been transferred to the EPA's National Drinking Water Information Service.  The bill also amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to exempt a public water system that receives financial assistance under the Safe Drinking Water or the Safe Drinking Water Financing Initiative from a federal cross-cutting requirement for the purpose of ensuring that the drinking water in the drinking water supply meets federal drinking water standards.

Consumer Credit Card Protection Act of 2005 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to prohibit any creditor from using any adverse information concerning any consumer report or any change in the credit score of the consumer, as the basis for increasing any interest rate applicable to a credit card account, or removing or increasing any introductory interest rate applicable to such account, for reasons other than actions or omissions of the consumer that are directly related to such account.

Defines "credit card account" to include any outstanding balance on the account, including any outstanding balance on an open end consumer credit plan.

Requires a creditor to apply any applicable interest rate in effect on the date of the disclosure to any outstanding balance on the account, taking into account the different rates that may be applicable with respect to different portions of the outstanding balance, without regard to whether any such rate is a fixed or variable rate.

Requires the creditor to apply any interest rate in effect on the date of the disclosure to any outstanding balance on the account as of the date of the notice of the increase in the interest rate and impose a fee on any outstanding balance of credit under such plan.

Requires any notice required under this Act to be mailed (or e-mailed, if the consumer has requested to receive such notices

American Textile Technology Innovation and Research for Exportation (ATTIRE) Act - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish a competitive grant program to fund textile research and innovation and to promote increased textile exports.

Requires the grant program to be limited to institutions of higher education and not-for-profit research institutions, including industry associations whose core mission is to support textile research and innovation.

Requires the funds authorized to be appropriated for the program to be used for research and development activities that achieve at least one of the following goals: (1) to build and sustain innovation, competitiveness, and best practices in the U.S. textile industry; (2) to contribute to transforming the U.S. textile and apparel industry into a highly flexible supply chain capable of responding to rapidly changing market demands; (3) to discover, design, and develop new materials, and innovative and improved manufacturing and integrated systems, essential to the success of a modern U.S. textile industry; (4) to train personnel, establish industrial partnerships, and create transfer mechanisms to ensure the utilization of technologies developed; (5) to strengthen the nation's textile research and educational efforts by uniting diverse experts and resources in unique collaborative projects; and (6) to facilitate the creation of domestic jobs in

Veterans Benefits Network Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make grants to an eligible entity to establish or expand a regional technology system to provide an active database and enrollment system that can be used by a coordinated network of private, public, and nonprofit entities to assist veterans and their family members in applying for benefits and services offered by such entities that participate in the network.

Requires the recipient of a grant to use the grant to establish a coordinated network of private, public, and nonprofit services and resources, as described in this Act, for veterans and their families designed to facilitate awareness and understanding of benefits that are available to members of the Armed Forces, veterans, and their family members who are eligible for benefits, and have the capacity to be replicated at other locations or regional networks.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to an eligible entity that provides services to individuals residing in a geographic area where a large number of veterans and members of the Armed Forces reside.

Counseling in Shelters Act of 2002 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Assistant Secretary for the Administration on Children, Youth, and Families, to make grants to eligible entities for the purpose of providing on site mental health and substance abuse counseling and referral services.

Social Security Protection and Tax Relief Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose a 12 percent tax on an individual's social security taxable income for a taxable year if the individual's gross income is reduced by the greater of the standard deduction (currently $12,000) and the deduction for personal exemptions (currently $15,000). Defines "exempt income" as amounts received as a pension or annuity from a qualified plan, amounts received as a social security benefit, and amounts received as earned income.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow the use of distributions from individual retirement plans (IRPs) for first home purchases or educational expenses.

Lamprey Wild and Scenic River Act - Amends the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate the 11.5-mile segment extending from the southern Lee town line to the confluence with the Piscassic River near the Durham-Newmarket town line as a recreational river. Requires the Secretary of the Interior to coordinate the management responsibilities of the Secretary of the Interior and the Lamprey River Advisory Committee.

Police Gun Buyback Assistance Act - Authorizes the Attorney General to make grants to States or local governments to: (1) assist States and local governments in purchasing new firearms without transferring decommissioned firearms to any person; and (2) destroy decommissioned firearms. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the Bretton Woods Agreements Act to direct the Secretary of the Treasury to: (1) instruct the U.S. Executive Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to seek an agreement to include the Bank of England as a holder of Special Drawing Rights; and (2) provide for the contribution of such Rights to the IMF.

United States-Israel Homeland Security Foundation Act - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to authorize the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish a United States-Israel Homeland Security Foundation to award conditional grants to joint business ventures between U.S. and Israeli private corporate entities to develop, manufacture, sell, or otherwise provide products and services with applications related to homeland security.

Requires the Secretary to administer the grant program through the Directorate of Science and Technology.

Authorizes the Secretary to establish the Foundation if the Secretary decides not to establish it under this Act.

Requires the Secretary to use not less than $25 million of the Foundation's grant funds to administer the Foundation.

Requires any expenditure by the United States under this Act to be equal to the expenditure by Israel for the same purpose.

STEM Network Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to make grants to eligible networks to expand STEM education. Defines "eligible network" as a state-based STEM network or similar organization which: (1) may include the participation of state officials, educators, administrators, parents, industry leaders, and representatives from the STEM communities; and (2) aims to increase student achievement in the STEM disciplines at the elementary and secondary schools in its state, particularly at schools with a high concentration of low-income students and at rural schools (within the meaning of part B of title VI of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (ESEA) of 20 U.S.C. 6201 et seq.) and at secondary schools with a high concentration of low-income students and at institutions of higher education.

Requires each grant recipient to use the funds to: (1) test, validate, share, and scale up STEM education research, promising practices, and exemplary programs among the network's members and with other grantees; (2) identify points of weakness and strength among state STEM education efforts, prioritizing strategies for addressing problem areas, and communicating state needs to the Secretary; (3) assist in the implementation of rigorous common content standards in

Supporting Education for Returning Veterans Act of 2008 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award three-year grants to institutions of higher education to establish programs that support veterans by providing and coordinating services that address their academic, financial, physical, and social needs.

Requires each program to include: (1) establishing a Center of Excellence for Veteran Student Success on the campus of the institution of higher education that provides a single point of contact to coordinate comprehensive support services for veterans; (2) establishing a support team for veterans who are students, including representatives from the student veteran association and veteran service office of such institution; (3) providing a full-time or part-time coordinator whose primary responsibility is to coordinate the program; and (4) monitoring the rates of enrollment, persistence, and completion of programs of education at such institutions.

Requires each program to include: (1) establishing a support team for veterans who are students, including representatives from the student veteran association and veteran service office of such institution; (2) providing a full-time or part-time coordinator whose primary responsibility is to coordinate the program; and (3) monitoring the rates of enrollment, persistence, and completion of programs of education

Export Enhancement Act of 1999 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to extend the authority of the Board of Directors of the Corporation for National Development to deny a grant or contract to any entity that is likely to have adverse environmental impacts that are sensitive, diverse, or unprecedented unless for at least 60 days before the date of the vote: (1) an environmental impact assessment or initial environmental audit has been completed by the project applicant and made available to the Board; and (2) such assessment or audit has been made available to the public of the U.S., local affected groups in the host country, and host country nongovernmental organizations. 
Directs the Corporation to hold a public hearing to afford an opportunity for persons to present views regarding the Corporation's activities. 
Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to require the Board of Directors of the Corporation to: (1) hold a public hearing to permit the Board to present its views regarding the Corporation's activities; and (2) in conjunction with each Board meeting, to hold a public hearing to permit any person to present views regarding the Corporation's activities. 
Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 196

Great Falls Preservation and Redevelopment Act of 1993 - Establishes the Great Falls Historic District in Paterson, New Jersey, to be administered through cooperative agreements. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to make grants to, and enter into cooperative agreements with, nonprofit entities for:  (1) the purchase of property or easements; (2) emergency stabilization; and (3) the establishment of a coordinated fund. 
Requires the Secretary to evaluate the condition of historic and architectural resources on the date of enactment of this Act, and the environmental and flood hazard conditions within the District. 
Authorizes the Secretary to enter into cooperative agreements with the owners of properties within the District of historical or cultural significance as determined by the Secretary. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Authorizes the Commandant of the Coast Guard to transfer to Presque Isle Township, Michigan, possession of the Historic Fresnel Lens (in this case, the Lens) from the Lighthouse.  Requires the Township to install the Lens and operate the Lens and Lighthouse as private aid to navigation.  Requires the Commandant to convey to the Township all U.S. interest in the Lens.  Requires the Lens to be retained by the Township for preservation and conservation.  Requires installation of the Lens within two years after the transfer of the Lens to the Township.  Requires the Lens to be returned to the Coast Guard if the Township does not install the Lens within the time specified.  Requires the Commandant to enter into an agreement with the Township for the operation of the Lens as a Class I private aid to navigation and for the holding of the United States harmless for any claim arising with respect to personal property conveyed under this Act.

Katie Sepich Enhanced DNA Collection Act of 2010 - Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to provide for an incentive program for states to implement minimum and enhanced DNA collection processes.

Defines "minimum DNA collection process" as a process under which the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is searched at least once against samples from certain individuals who are at least 18 years of age: (1) who are arrested for, charged with, or indicted for a criminal offense that consists of murder or voluntary manslaughter; or (2) who have an element of kidnapping or abduction that is punishable by imprisonment for more than five years.

Defines "enhanced DNA collection process" as a process under which the state provides for the collection of DNA samples from the following individuals who are at least 18 years of age: (1) arrested for or charged with a criminal offense that consists of murder or voluntary manslaughter; (2) arrested for or charged with a criminal offense that has an element of kidnapping or abduction that is punishable by imprisonment for five years or more; or (3) arrested for or charged with a criminal offense under state law that consists of a specified offense against a minor (as defined in the Sex Off

Hardship Outlays to protect Mortgagee Equity (HOME) Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt distributions from the tax on early distributions from certain tax-exempt retirement plans for mortgage payments to a principal residence of an individual whose mortgage payments are used to pay qualified mortgage costs with respect to a principal residence.

American Opportunity Tax Credit Extension Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the Hope Scholarship Tax Credit to: (1) 100% of qualified tuition and related expenses paid during the taxable year, plus 25% of expenses exceeding $2,000, and (2) the lifetime learning tax credit to $40,000 ($80,000 in the case of a joint return).

Increases the amount of such credit to offset the cost of inflation.

Kissimmee River Wild and Scenic River Study Act of 2018 (Sec. 3) This bill amends the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate the segment from Lake Kissimmee to its confluence with Lake Okeechobee as the Kissimmee River.  The bill also requires the Department of the Interior to complete a study of the Kissimmee River and report on the results to Congress.

Small Company Capital Formation Act of 2011 - Amends the Securities Act of 1933 to direct the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to add a class of securities to the securities exempted pursuant to such Act in accordance with specified terms and conditions.

Directs the SEC to increase the aggregate offering amount of securities exempted from regulation under this Act from $50 million to $500 million.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on the impact of State laws regulating securities offerings.

Custodial Interrogation Recording Act - Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to direct the Attorney General to make grants to States and local governments to take whatever steps the Attorney General determines necessary to achieve the complete and accurate recording, by both audio and video means, of every custodial interrogation occurring within the State or unit of government. Limits the portion of the costs of a program funded by a grant under this Act to 75 percent.

Worker-Executive Parity Act of 2009 - Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to provide that, in any case in which a limitation applies, the plan shall provide to a covered deferred executive compensation arrangement which is comparable to certain funding-based limitations on benefits and benefit accrual, and which is established during or after the one-year period preceding the plan year.

Defines "covered deferred executive compensation arrangement" as any arrangement providing for the deferral of compensation of a qualified individual, whether or not: (1) compensation of such individual is subject to substantial risk of forfeiture, (2) the individual's rights to the deferred compensation are no greater than the rights of a general creditor of the plan sponsor, (3) all amounts set aside for paying the deferred compensation (including income), and (4) certain amounts remain (until made available to the individual or other beneficiary) solely the plan sponsor's property.

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to establish a community-based overweight and obesity prevention program.

Authorizes the Secretary to award grants and contracts to eligible entities to plan evidence-based programs for the prevention of overweight and obesity among children and their families through improved nutrition and increased physical activity.

Requires the Secretary to give preference to eligible entities that serve communities with high levels of overweight and obesity and that will plan or implement activities for the prevention of overweight and obesity in school or workplace settings.
Tax Equity Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide regional cost-of-living adjustments in individual income tax rates.

Mud Dump Permanent Closure and Remediation Act of 2000 - Amends the Marine Protection, Research, and Sanctuaries Act of 1972 to prohibit the dumping of dredged material at the Site of the Prohibition on Ocean Dumping at the Historic Area Remediation Site, New Jersey, until the Secretary of the Interior has issued permits authorizing the transportation of dredged materials to the Site solely for the purpose of providing for remediation of the Site.

Emergency Mortgage Loan Modification Act of 2008 - States that a servicer of a residential mortgage loan that acts in a manner consistent with the duty to maximize, or to not adversely affect, the recovery of total proceeds from pooled residential mortgage loans is deemed to be acting on behalf of the vehicle in the best interest of all investors and holders of beneficial interests in the pooled loans, in the aggregate, if for a loan that is in payment default under the loan agreement or for which payment default is imminent or reasonably foreseeable, the loan servicer makes reasonable and documented efforts to implement a modification or workout plan or, if such efforts are unsuccessful or such plan would be infeasible, engages in other loss mitigation, including accepting a short payment or partial discharge of principal, or agreeing to a short sale of the property, to the extent that the servicer reasonably believes the particular modification or workout plan or other mitigation actions will maximize the net present value to be realized on the loan, including over that which would be realized through foreclosure.

Prohibits a servicer of a residential mortgage loan that acts in a manner consistent with this Act from entering into a qualified loan modification or workout plan, to: (1) any person, based on that person's ownership of a residential mortgage

International Commerce Enhancement Act - Amends the Arms Export Control Act to revise the military export controls applicable to foreign and national security policy objectives and restraints. 
Revises the military export controls applicable to:  (1) the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO); and (2) major non-NATO countries. 
Revises the military export controls applicable to:  (1) the United States; and (2) any organization or country other than a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), Japan, Australia, or New Zealand, or any other organization or country.

Rush Hour Congestion Relief Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish and implement a traffic incident management program to assist States and localities in: (1) regional traffic incident management program planning; and (2) projects to mitigate the effects of traffic delays resulting from accidents, breakdowns, and other non-recurring incidents on highways.

Requires funds apportioned to a State under this Act to be used for: (1) regional collaboration and coordination activities that lead to regional traffic incident management policies, programs, plans, procedures, and agreements; (2) purchase or lease of telecommunications equipment for first responders as part of the development of a regional traffic incident management program; (3) payments to contractors for towing and recovery services as part of a regional traffic incident management program; (4) rental of vehicle storage or staging areas immediately adjacent to roadways as part of a regional traffic incident management program; (5) traffic service patrols as part of a regional traffic incident management program; (6) enhanced hazardous materials incident response; (7) traffic management systems in support of traffic incident management; (8) traffic incident management training; (9) crash investigation equipment; (10) other activities under a regional traffic incident management plan; and (11

Safer Trucks and Buses Act of 2015 This bill directs the Department of Transportation (DOT) to ensure that covered motor carrier data is not made available to the public.  The National Academy of Public Administration shall report to Congress on the results of a study on how to improve the Compliance, Safety, Accountability initiative of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA).
Colorectal Cancer Detection Act of 2018 This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of certain approved screening blood-based tests.

Infertility Research Centers Act of 2002 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Director of the Institute to make grants to, or enter into contracts with, public or nonprofit private entities for the development and operation of centers to conduct activities for improving methods of preventing infertility. Requires the Director to provide for the establishment of two such centers. Authorizes each center to use funds provided under this Act to provide stipends for health and allied health professionals enrolled in specified programs. Directs the Director to provide for the coordination of information among such centers. Authorizes each center to use such funds to provide fees to individuals serving as subjects in clinical trials. Directs the Director to provide for the coordination of information among such centers. Authorizes the Director to make a loan repayment program for research with respect to infertility prevention. Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a loan repayment program for research with respect to infertility prevention.

Forest Service Administrative Review Act - Amends the Healthy Forests Restoration Act of 2003 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish by regulation a pre-decisional administrative review process for a proposed action that is: (1) in the environmental assessment or environmental impact statement of a federal-aid timberland and timber and timber and timber management project; and (2) that is not later than the date of the issuance of the final decision approving the action.

Requires the Secretary to provide notice of, and distribute, the proposed decision along with the final environmental assessment or environmental impact statement, if the Forest Service determines that an emergency situation exists for which immediate implementation of a proposed action is necessary.

Exempts from the pre-decisional administrative review process any action that: (1) has its own special administrative review process under the Healthy Forests Restoration Act of 2003; and (2) is not later than a specified time period after the issuance of the final decision approving the action.

Requires the Forest Service to: (1) provide notice of the final decision for an action that is exempted under this Act; and (2) provide for an expedited judicial review of an action challenging an action.

Federal Reserve Accountability Act of 2009 - Authorizes the Comptroller General to conduct reviews of the accounting, financial reporting, and internal controls of credit facilities of the Federal Reserve System (FRB) and any Federal Reserve bank, including when such activities are carried out by or on behalf of the Board or any official of a federal reserve bank.

Authorizes the Comptroller General to make and retain copies of records as the Comptroller General deems appropriate.

Requires the Board to place on its home Internet website a link to a repository of information that shall be available to the public for a reasonable period of time, not less than six months following the date of release, including: (1) the Comptroller General's reports; (2) the annual financial statements prepared by an independent auditor for the Board; and (3) such other information as the Board reasonably believes is necessary or helpful to the public in understanding the accounting, financial reporting, and internal controls of the FRB and the federal reserve banks.

Cures Can Be Found Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for expenses related to qualified stem cell research, storage, and donation. Defines "qualified stem cell" as a human stem cell obtained from a human placenta, umbilical cord blood, an organ or tissue of a living or deceased human being who has been born, or an organ or tissue of unborn human offspring who died of natural causes (such as spontaneous abortion).

Regulatory Integrity Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill requires each executive agency to make publicly available in a searchable format in a prominent location: (1) any pending agency regulatory action, and (2) the following information:  a list of each pending agency regulatory action and with regard to each such action, the date on which the agency first began to develop or consider the agency regulatory action, the status of the agency regulatory action, an estimate of the date of upon which the action will be final and in effect, a list of agency regulatory actions that duplicate or overlap with the action, and if a regulatory impact analysis has been conducted, the findings of such analysis, including any data or formula used for purposes of such analysis.  The bill requires each executive agency to publish such information within 24 hours after a public communication relating to a pending agency regulatory action and to maintain the public availability of such information for at least five years after the action is finalized.  Any public communication issued by an executive agency that refers to a pending agency regulatory action must specify whether the agency is considering alternatives, including alternatives that may conflict with the intent, objective, or methodology of the agency regulatory action, whether the agency is accepting or will be accepting comments, and

Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop and issue public service announcements (broadcast through appropriate media outlets) that advertise and promote the pharmacist profession, highlight the advantages and rewards of being a pharmacist, and encourage individuals to enter the pharmacist profession.

Directs the Secretary to award grants to support State and local advertising campaigns through appropriate media outlets to promote the pharmacist profession, highlight the advantages and rewards of being a pharmacist, and encourage individuals to enter the pharmacist profession.

Requires the Secretary to establish a demonstration project to enhance the participation of pharmacists in the National Health Service Corps Loan Repayment Program.

Knife Owners' Protection Act of 2017 This bill prohibits a person from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a knife or knives (or knives designed for enabling escape in an emergency) that is not otherwise prohibited by federal law from transporting a knife or knives to any place where such person may lawfully transport such a knife or knives if: (1) the knife or knives are not directly accessible from the passenger compartment of a transporting vehicle, or, in the case of a motor vehicle without a compartment separate from the passenger compartment, the knife or knives shall be contained in a locked container, glove compartment, or console; or (2) in the case of transporting by other means, the knife or knives are contained in a locked container.  A person may assert this bill as a claim or defense in any civil or criminal action. When a person asserts this bill as a claim or defense, the state or political subdivision shall bear the burden of proving that the person was not in compliance with this bill.  A person may not be arrested or otherwise detained for violation of state law or any rule or regulation related to the possession, transportation, or carrying of knives unless there is probable cause to believe that the person is not in compliance with this bill. Child Modeling Exploitation Prevention Act - Amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to prohibit employment in exploitive child modeling.

Imposes a fine and/or prison term of up to 10 years for anyone who violates such prohibition.

Excludes from such prohibition an image taken as a whole, which has serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value.

Presidential Transition Act of 2000 - Amends the Presidential Transition Act of 1963 to provide for the transition of presidential appointees from campaign and other prior activities to assuming the responsibility for governance after inauguration. 
Directs the Office of Government Ethics to study and report to specified congressional committees on improvements to the financial disclosure process for presidential nominees.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to transfer specified land to the Standing Rock Indian Reservation, North Dakota, for the Oahe Dam and Reservoir Project.  Prohibits the United States from being responsible for any damage to the transferred land caused by flooding, sloughing, erosion, or any other change to the transferred land as a result of the Project or any Pick-Sloan Missouri River Basin Program activities.  Requires the United States to retain the right to inundate with water or cause erosion to the transferred lands.  Requires the Secretary of the Army to prepare a map of the transferred land.  Requires the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe to be responsible for the payment of all costs and administrative expenses associated with the transfer authorized by this Act.

International Remittance Services Enhancement and Protection Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Credit Union Act to require federal financial institutions and money transmitting businesses to provide certain disclosures to consumers before they consummate a transaction in order to advertise, solicit, or negotiate at the institution's office or business at which the transaction is initiated.

Requires the appropriate federal banking agency, in the case of an insured depository institution, to: (1) prescribe regulations that require any financial institution or money transmitting business which initiates an international money transfer on behalf of a consumer to provide the following disclosures to the consumer before the consummation of the transaction; and (2) enforce such requirements.

Requires the Federal Trade Commission to enforce compliance with such disclosures.

Animal Agriculture Environmental Incentives Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business tax credit for 25 percent of the eligible nutrient management costs of a taxpayer for the taxable year.  Allows such credit for the cost of manure spreader equipment.

Prohibits a health care provider from being considered to be in noncompliance with the applicable requirements of subparts I through N of the Medicare prescription drug benefit program before October 16, 2003, and a health care clearinghouse from being considered to be in noncompliance with such requirements before October 16, 2003.

Requires a health care provider, a health care clearinghouse, or a small health plan or a health care clearinghouse to be considered to be in noncompliance with the applicable requirements of subparts I through N of the Medicare prescription drug benefit program before October 16, 2003, and to comply with such requirements no later than October 16, 2003.

Declares that during the period that begins on April 14, 2003, and ends on October 16, 2003, a health care provider or, subject to such requirements, a health care clearinghouse that processes or facilitates the processing of information in connection with a Medicare prescription drug benefit transaction shall comply with the applicable requirements of subparts E (requiring that the transmission meet certain standards formats) and N (requiring that the transmission meet certain standards formats).

Protection from Sexual Predators Act of 1997 - Amends the Federal criminal code to provide that whoever violates this Act or engages in conduct that would violate it, if the conduct occurred in the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, and that conduct is in interstate or foreign commerce, shall be imprisoned for life. 
Amends the Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act of 1994 to provide that a State is not eligible for a grant under such Act unless such State has provided assurances to the Attorney General that such State has in effect laws which allow the court to impose a sentence of life in prison without parole on a defendant in a criminal case who is convicted of a State offense for conduct that:  (1) is an offense under the Act or the Code; or (2) would have been an offense under either of such sections if the offense had occurred in the special maritime or territorial jurisdiction of the United States. 
Directs the National Institute of Justice to study and report to the Congress and the President on persistent sexual predators.

Meat and Poultry Products Traceability and Safety Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Meat Inspection Act to define "traceability" as the ability to retrieve the history, use, and location of an article through a recordkeeping and audit system or registered identification.

Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a traceability system for all stages of production, processing, and distribution of meat and meat food products that are produced through the slaughter of animals.

Prohibits the Secretary from: (1) restricting entry into any slaughtering establishment inspected under this Act of any cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules, or other equines not identified as prescribed; or (2) altering, detaching, or destroying any records or other means of identification prescribed for use in determining the premises at which were held any cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules, or other equines, or the carcasses thereof.

Veterans Timely Access to Health Care Act - Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to prescribe an appropriate standard for access to care for a veteran seeking primary care from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) health care facility.

Directs the Secretary to periodically review the performance of VA health-care facilities in meeting such standard.

Requires the Secretary to submit to the congressional veterans committees an annual report providing an assessment of VA performance in meeting such standard.

Historically Women's Public Colleges or Universities Historic Building Restoration and Preservation Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to award grants to historically women's public colleges or universities for the preservation and restoration of historic buildings and structures on their campuses. Requires such grants to be made from amounts appropriated to carry out the National Historic Preservation Act for FY 2001 through 2005.

Global Investments in America's Cities Act This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to: (1) increase the number of EB-5 (environmental, social, and tribal development visas) investment companies authorized for each fiscal year to 3,000, and (2) set forth a schedule for the expedited processing of such petitions.

Small Business Expansion and Hiring Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business-related tax credit for the cost of training and rehiring a newly-hired employee. Defines "retained worker" as any qualified individual who: (1) was employed by the taxpayer on any date during the taxable year, (2) was so employed by the taxpayer for a period of at least 52 consecutive weeks, and (3) whose wages (as defined in this Act) for such employment during the last 26 weeks of such period equaled at least 80% of such wages for the first 26 weeks of such period.

Limits the amount of such credit to $400,000 for a taxable year ending after January 1, 2013.

Making Education Affordable Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award grants to institutions of higher education that carry out dual or concurrent enrollment programs or early college high school programs that enable them to earn college credits while in high school.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to institutions that serve students from low-income families, students from rural communities, or students who are the first in their family to receive postsecondary education.

Allows grantees to use grant funds to: (1) provide teachers, principals, and other school leaders with professional development activities that enhance or enable the provision of postsecondary coursework through a dual or concurrent enrollment program or an early college high school program; and (2) support activities such as designing the curriculum and sequence of courses in collaboration with teachers from the local educational agency (LEA) and faculty from the institution, establishing a course articulation process for defining and approving courses for high school and postsecondary credit or credentials for both-year and four-year institutions of higher education in the state, and helping students meet eligibility criteria for postsecondary courses and ensuring that they understand how credits earned will transfer to such institutions.

Permits grantees to use grant funds for any costs associated with carrying out dual or concurrent enrollment

Helping Responsible Homeowners Act - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to provide for the refinancing of qualified mortgages on single-family housing owned or guaranteed by such enterprises. Prohibits the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) from charging a mortgage lender any up-front fee beyond the standard guarantee fee for the refinancing of the mortgage.

Women's Human Rights Protection Act of 1993 - Declares the sense of the Congress that the State Department should designate within the appropriate bureau a special assistant to the Assistant Secretary to promote international women's human rights within the overall human rights policy of the Government. 
Makes the following findings and declarations:  (1)  The purpose of assigning a special assistant on women's human rights issues is not to segregate such issues, but rather to assure that they are considered along with other human rights issues in the development of U.S. foreign policy; (2) A specifically designated special assistant is necessary because within the human rights field and the foreign policy establishment, the issues of gender-based discrimination and violence against women have long been ignored or made invisible; (3) The Congress believes that abuses against women would have greater visibility and protection of women's human rights would improve if the advocate were responsible for integrating women's human rights issues into U.S. human rights policy in ways including, but not limited to:  the designation of women's human rights advocates in the designated women's human rights advocate position, the development of strategies to bring pressure to bear on governments that engage in violence or systematic discrimination against women or fail to

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to define "infrastructure property" as roads and related improvements, airports, dams, tunnels, and traffic control equipment.  Exempts from the tax deduction for income from publicly traded partnerships any income derived from any such partnerships.  Makes infrastructure property eligible for the tax deduction for income from partnerships.  Reduces the tax deduction for income from partnerships for oil related qualified production activities.  Excludes from the tax deduction for income from such partnerships the activities of a publicly traded partnership.  Treats real property which is infrastructure property and which is held for productive use in a trade or business or for investment as like-kind property.  Treats such property as of a like kind to every other such property which is infrastructure property and which is so held.

Independent Pharmacy Protection Act of 2006 - Amends part D (Voluntary Prescription Drug Benefit Program) of title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require each contract entered into with a Medicare Advantage organization under part D to provide for the following: (1) availability of direct deposit payments; (2) increased payment of dispensing fees for generic drugs; (3) payment within 10 days for certain pharmacies; and (4) a plan payment of $10 for a generic covered part D drug that is therapeutically equivalent and bioequivalent to a brand name drug dispensed through a participating pharmacy.

Applies the provisions of this Act to Medicare Advantage plans entered under part D.

Return of Talent Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish the Return of Talent Program to permit eligible aliens to temporarily return to their country of citizenship in order to make a material contribution to that country's post-conflict or natural disaster reconstruction activities, unless an exception is granted under specified circumstances.

Authorizes the Secretary to extend the 24-month period for such temporary return.

Subjects to naturalization the spouse, parents, siblings, and minor children of such an alien who participates in the Program.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on the countries of citizenship of the Program participants, the post-conflict or natural disaster reconstruction efforts that benefitted, or were made possible, through Program participation, and any other information the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

Lifelong Improvements in Food and Exercise (LIFE) Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to carry out a national program to conduct and support activities regarding individuals who are overweight or obese in order to make progress toward the goal of significantly reducing the number of cases of obesity among individuals in the United States.

Directs the Secretary to carry out the following activities with respect to individuals who are overweight: (1) to train health professionals to recognize that patients are overweight and to recommend prevention activities regarding such condition, including educating patients on the relationship between such condition and cardiovascular disease, diabetes and other health conditions, and on proper nutrition and regular physical activities; (2) to educate the public regarding the condition of being overweight; (3) to develop and demonstrate intervention strategies for use at worksites and in community settings; and (4) to develop and demonstrate strategies for use in hospitals and community health centers.

SOAR to Health and Wellness Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a pilot program to provide training to health care providers and other related providers on human trafficking. HHS must collect and report on the number of facilities operating under the pilot program and the number of health care providers and other related providers trained through the program.

Seniors Financial Fraud Prevention Act of 2010 - Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to establish a separate office within the FTC to prevent fraud targeting seniors and to assist the FTC with: (1) oversight; (2) consumer education; (3) complaints; (4) information; and (5) law enforcement action.

Requires the FTC to: (1) disseminate information on fraud targeting seniors and on means of referring complaints to appropriate law enforcement agencies; (2) provide information on fraud, including mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet, to seniors and their caregivers; (3) maintain a website to serve as a resource for information for seniors and caregivers regarding mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud; and (4) establish procedures to log and acknowledge receipt of complaints by individuals who have a reasonable belief that they have been the victim of fraud in connection with the conduct of mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet.

Community Health Center Volunteer Provider Protection Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the General Accounting Office to study the adequacy of funding for liability coverage for community health centers and other health centers operated by the Public Health Service.

Directs the Comptroller General to study the adequacy of funding for liability coverage for community health centers and other health centers operated by the Public Health Service.

Dru Sjodin National Sex Offender Public Database Act of 2004 or Dru's Law - Directs the Attorney General to: (1) make publicly available in a registry from information contained in the National Sex Offender Registry (NSOR) of the Department of Justice (DOJ) all information concerning convicted sex offenders who reside in a specified geographic area; and (2) allow users of the registry to determine which registered sex offenders are currently residing within a specified radius of the location.

Requires the public registry to provide the name and any known aliases of the person, the date of birth, and the current address of the person and any subsequent changes of that address.

Requires any person convicted of a criminal offense against a sex offender or a sexually violent predator to register with a specified program within a state. Requires the public registry to provide the name and any known aliases of the person, the date of birth, and the current address of the person and any subsequent changes of that address.

Requires any state that provides for a civil commitment proceeding, or any equivalent proceeding, to issue notice to the attorney general of that state of the impending release of any person who is a sexually violent predator or who has been deemed by the state to be at high-risk

Gerardo Hernandez Airport Security Act of 2014 - Directs the Assistant Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to: (1) conduct outreach to all U.S. airports at which DHS performs or supervises the implementation and performance of security measures and provide technical assistance to verify such airports have in place individualized working plans for responding to security incidents inside the perimeter of the airport, including active shooters, acts of terrorism, and incidents that target passenger-screening checkpoints; and (2) report to Congress on the findings from such outreach and on the implementation of best practices to airports nationwide. Requires the Assistant Secretary to: (1) identify best practices that exist across airports for security incident planning, management, and training; and (2) establish a mechanism through which to share such best practices with other airport operators nationwide. Directs the Assistant Secretary to certify to Congress that all screening personnel have participated in practical training exercises for active shooter scenarios. Directs the Assistant Secretary to: (1) review the interoperable communications capabilities of the law enforcement, fire, and medical personnel responsible for responding to a security incident, including active shooter events, acts of terrorism, and incidents that target passenger-screening checkpoints; and (2)

Stock Option Accounting Reform Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to require that all executive officers of an issuer of securities register their stock options with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Directs the SEC to award a fair value to each executive officer to the extent that an option to purchase the stock of the issuer would be subject to specified accounting standards.

Prohibits the expensing of stock options and requires the SEC to study and report to Congress on the economic impact of the mandatory expensing of all employee stock options.

Livestock Concentration Report Act - Establishes a Commission on Concentration in the Livestock Industry to:  (1) determine whether the study of concentration in the red meat packing industry adequately examined and identified procurement markets for slaughter cattle in the continental United States, analyzed the effects that slaughter cattle procurement practices, and concentration in the procurement of slaughter cattle have on the purchasing and pricing of slaughter cattle by beef packers; (2) examine the use of captive cattle supply arrangements by beef packers and the effects of such arrangements on slaughter cattle markets; (3) examine the economics of vertical integration and of coordination arrangements in the hog slaughtering and processing industry; (4) review the pertinent research literature on issues relating to the structure and operation of the meat packing industry; and (5) represent the current situation in the livestock industry compared to the situation reflected in the data on which the study is based. 
Directs the Commission to:  (1) request the Attorney General to report on the application of the antitrust laws and operation of other Federal laws applicable to concentration and vertical integration in the procurement and pricing of slaughter cattle and of slaughter hogs by meat packers; (2) review laws and regulations relating to the operation of the meat packing industry regarding the concentration, vertical integration, and vertical coordination in

Law Enforcement Protection Act of 1997 - Amends the Federal criminal code to authorize qualified current and former law enforcement officers carrying appropriate written identification to carry concealed firearms. 
Declares that nothing in this Act shall be construed to supersede or limit any Federal or State law prohibiting the possession of a firearm on any Federal property, installation, building, base, or park. 
Authorizes the consent of the Congress to any two or more States to enter into compacts or agreements for cooperative effort in enabling individuals to carry concealed weapons as dictated by laws of the State within which the owner of the weapon resides and is authorized to carry a concealed weapon. 
Declares that the right to alter, amend, or repeal this Act is expressly reserved by the Congress.

Art-in-Architecture Act of 1993 - Requires the Administrator of the General Services Administration or a designee of the Administrator to make available for new construction, building purchase, acquisition, or prospectus-level repair and alteration projects at at least one-half percent of the funds made available for new construction, building purchase, acquisition, or prospectus-level repair and alteration projects in the case of a building project that receives funding from sources other than the Federal Government.  Authorizes the Administrator to decrease the percentage amount specified in the Act for a project requiring more artwork, such as a building with exceptional public space whose architectural character and scale would accommodate and be significantly enhanced by large-scale, high-quality artwork. 
Authorizes the Administrator to commission works of art by living American artists to be placed in Federal buildings. 
Requires the Administrator to:  (1) commission works of art by living American artists to be placed in Federal buildings; and (2) establish procedures to commission works of art, with an emphasis on the participation of community representatives. 
Requires the Administrator to provide for necessary services to maintain and preserve the works of art in a state of high quality. 
Directs the agency fine arts officer to maintain a registry of portfolios and statements

Promoting Self-Reliance for the World's Poorest Act of 2002 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to reauthorize through FY 2006: (1) the Microenterprise Development Grant Assistance program; and (2) the poverty measurement methods under such programs.Directs the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development to develop poverty measurement methods to measure the level of poverty of clients of sustainable poverty-focused programs under such Act.Requires the Administrator to report to Congress on the interim and final poverty measurement methods implemented under such Act.

Northern Yukon-Arctic International Wildlife Refuge Act - Establishes an international wildlife refuge area in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR) to be known as the Northern Yukon-Arctic International Wildlife Refuge.

Bright Idea Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to initiate a project to establish technical standards for general service lamps.

Requires the Secretary, if the Secretary determines that lamps meet such standards are generally available for purchase in the United States at substantially the same cost and replacement life as they would cost to replace them, to require that at least 95% of such lamps be sold in the United States by manufacturers that meet such standards.

Provides that such standards shall not apply to lamps used in applications in which compliance with such standards is not feasible.

Directs the Secretary to consult periodically with the interested parties with respect to whether those standards should be changed.

Authorizes the Secretary to carry out a lighting technology research and development program to support the research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of lamps and related technologies sold, offered for sale, or otherwise made available in the United States.

Directs the Secretary to carry out a comprehensive national program to educate consumers about the benefits of using light bulbs that have improved efficiency ratings.

Directs the Secretary to report to Congress on the means by which the Federal Government may reduce or prevent the release of mercury during the manufacture, transportation, storage, or disposal of light bulbs.

Traveler Redress Improvement Act of 2017 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to ensure the availability of DHS TRIP redress process to adjudicate inquiries for individuals who are citizens or aliens lawfully admitted for permanent residence who have been wrongfully identified as being a threat to aviation security.  (Sec. 3) The TSA shall: (1) report to Congress on the implementation of the redress process, and (2) review and update the Privacy Impact Assessment for the Secure Flight programs to ensure such assessment reflects the operation of such programs. The TSA shall conduct a comprehensive review of its intelligence-based screening rules. (Sec. 4) The TSA shall: (1) ensure that its risk analysis for the Federal Air Marshal mission scheduling process includes intelligence-based screening of the Transportation Security of the United States (TSUS) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in coordination with other relevant entities, and (2) submit to Congress a report on how its intelligence-based screening rules are incorporated in the risk analysis conducted during the Federal Air Marshal mission scheduling process. Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend temporarily the duty on certain organic chemicals.

Teacher Tax Credit Act of 2007 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to allow a teacher a refundable tax credit for up to 50% of certain elementary and secondary education expenses, including books, supplies, computer equipment, and supplementary materials used in the classroom. Defines "qualified elementary and secondary education expenses" as expenses for books, supplies, equipment, and other materials used in the classroom.

This bill requires the United States to take steps to ensure the safety of the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya, including by providing necessary and appropriate assistance to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to process refugee and humanitarian applications for the residents of the former Camp Ashraf in Iraq.  The United States shall also admit as refugees the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya in the United States and shall not delay or bar such resettlement because any such resident was a member or supported or has supported organizations or groups that were subject to the Department of State's decision of September 21, 2012, in Public Notice 8049.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to expand the operation of the immigrant visa program to all five (currently, all but one) of the 50 States.
Directs the Secretary to report to the congressional defense committees on the immigrant investor program created under the Immigration and Nationality Act.

Enhancing Nutrition in Medical Education Act of 2004 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to award grants to accredited schools of medicine to integrate innovative curricula on nutrition into medical education.

Directs the Secretary to ensure that innovative curricula on nutrition developed and implemented under this Act focus on preventive health measures, including the following: (1) education on the causes, treatment, and prevention of obesity; (2) office education and counseling to ensure appropriate diet for mostly healthy people; (3) prevention and treatment of common nutritional deficiencies; (4) appropriate and inappropriate use of herbs and supplements; (5) office recognition and treatment of common eating disorders; and (6) identification of special dietary needs, eating disorders, and appropriate routes of referral for medical nutrition therapy.

Prohibits the Secretary from making a grant unless the school involved agrees to expend the grant: (1) to develop innovative curricula on nutrition in accordance with such curriculum, to integrate such curricula, to the maximum extent possible, into each of the school's medical education, and to evaluate the results achieved; and (2) to evaluate the results achieved.

Requires a school of medicine receiving a grant to establish a multidisciplinary planning committee to develop

Dismemberment Abortion Ban Act of 2015 This bill amends the federal criminal code to prohibit a physician from knowingly performing a dismemberment abortion and thereby killing an unborn child. A physician who performs such an abortion must also be imprisoned for two years. This prohibition does not apply to a dismemberment abortion that is necessary to save the life of a mother whose life is endangered by a physical disorder, illness, or injury, including a life-ending physical condition caused by or arising from the pregnancy itself. A woman upon whom an abortion has been performed in violation of this bill may obtain appropriate relief from the court by filing a civil action against any person who committed the violation. A parent of a minor may also obtain appropriate relief from the court by filing a civil action against any person who committed the violation.
