Requires the Secretary to: (1) review an application submitted under this Act; (2) approve or disapprove the application in accordance with specified requirements within 90 days after receipt of the application; and (3) transmit to the State notice of the approval or disapproval, together with a statement of the reasons for the approval or disapproval.

Witness Security and Protection Grant Program Act of 2011 - Directs the Attorney General to make competitive grants to eligible state, tribal, and local governments to establish or maintain programs that provide protection or assistance to witnesses in: (1) court proceedings involving homicide, or involving a serious violent felony or serious drug offense; and (2) court proceedings involving gangs or organized crime.

Requires the Attorney General, upon request of a grant recipient, to direct the appropriate Department of Justice (DOJ) offices to provide technical assistance to the recipient to the extent such technical assistance is needed to establish or maintain such a program.

Requires each grant recipient to submit a report that evaluates each program, including policies and procedures under the program.

Requires the Attorney General to develop best practice models to assist states and other relevant entities in addressing witness protection and witness assistance.

Requires the Attorney General to disseminate to states and other relevant entities such models.

Expresses the sense of Congress that states and other relevant entities should use the best practice models developed and disseminated in accordance with this Act to evaluate, improve, and develop witness protection or assistance as appropriate.

Makes the federal share of the cost of a project carried out using a grant under this Act not more than 75%.

Oil Industry Merger Antitrust Enforcement Act - Amends the Clayton Act to require the Federal Trade Commission and the Antitrust Division of the Department of Justice to jointly review and revise all enforcement guidelines and policies, including the Horizontal Merger Guidelines issued April 2, 1992, and the Non-Horizontal Merger Guidelines issued June 14, 1984, to ensure that:  (1) the application of such guidelines will prevent any merger and acquisition in the oil industry, when the effect of such merger or acquisition may be to substantially lessen competition, or tend to create a monopoly; and (2) the application of such guidelines will reflect the special conditions prevailing in the oil industry. 
Requires the Federal Trade Commission and the Antitrust Division to report to specified congressional committees regarding the review and revision of such guidelines.

Amends the Clean Air Act to define "renewable biomass" as materials, pre-commercial thinnings, or invasive species from National Forest System land and public lands that are byproducts of preventive treatments that are removed to reduce hazardous fuels, reduce or contain disease or insect infestation, or restore ecosystem health.

Defines "renewable biomass" as materials, pre-commercial thinnings, or invasive species from non-Federal land or land belonging to an Indian or Indian tribe that are harvested in accordance with applicable law and the requirements for old-growth forest restoration and management.

States that the term "renewable biomass" shall apply in any Federal law enacted after this Act's enactment date: (1) to establish a renewable electricity standard; or (2) to regulate the emission of greenhouse gases.

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to require each local educational agency (LEA) receiving assistance under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to provide to military recruiters or institutions of higher education access to the name, address, and telephone listing of each secondary school student served by the LEA, unless the parent of such student has submitted the prior consent request. Allows a parent of a secondary school student to submit a written request that the student's name, address, and telephone listing not be released for the purpose of the requirement that the student's name, address, and telephone listing be released for military recruiting purposes. Prohibits the LEA from releasing the student's name, address, and telephone listing for such purposes without the prior written parental consent of the parent.

Requires the Secretary of Education to notify the Governor of the LEA's state and the Secretary of Education of any failure of LEAs to comply with this requirement.

American Freedom Agenda Act of 2007 - Repeals the Military Commissions Act of 2006 and the President's authorized use of torture or coercion in the trial of war crimes.

Prohibits the President from detaining an individual indefinitely as an enemy combatant absent proof that the individual has directly engaged in active hostilities against the United States.

Requires the House and Senate to file a declaratory judgment action in an appropriate federal district court to challenge the constitutionality of a presidential signing statement that declares the President's intent to disregard provisions of a bill he has signed into law because he believes they are unconstitutional.

Prohibits the use of secret evidence by the President or any other executive branch member to designate an individual or organization with a U.S. presence as a foreign terrorist or foreign terrorist organization for purposes of the criminal law or otherwise imposing criminal or civil sanctions.

Creating Opportunities for Military Members to Use Transportation Efficiently Act of 2014 or the COMMUTE Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Defense (DOD), acting through the Director of the Office of Economic Adjustment, to establish a Military Community Infrastructure Program to provide grants to eligible entities for transportation infrastructure improvement projects in military communities. Requires such grants to be used for the construction of roads, mass transit and parking facilities, and pedestrian access and bicycle access.  Requires the Secretary to give consideration to: (1) the magnitude of the problem addressed by the project; (2) the proportion of the problem that is caused by military installation growth since the year 2000; (3) the number of servicemembers and civilian employees of the Department of Defense (DOD) affected by the problem; (4) the size of the community affected by the problem; (5) the ability of the relevant entity to execute the project; and (6) the extent to which the project resolves the transportation problem.  Prohibits the Federal share of the cost of a project carried out using grant amounts made available under this Act from exceeding 80%.  Directs the Secretary to conduct a traffic impact study for any urbanized area

Amends the San Luis Rey Indian Water Rights Settlement Act to require the Secretary of the Interior to arrange for the development of at least 16,000 acre-feet of supplemental water from public lands within the boundaries of the State of California outside the service area of the Central Valley Project. Requires such contractors to reimburse the Participating Contractors in an amount equal to the sum of:  (1) the annualized amounts of their respective contributions funded by the conservation of water so used; (2) any added costs of operation and maintenance; and (3) related mitigation costs. 
Requires the water identified in the Supplemental Water Supply to be made available, subject to the approval requirement, for consumptive use by California Contractors within their service areas according to their priorities under the Seven Party Agreement

Broadband Internet Regulatory Relief Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit an incumbent local exchange carrier from being subject to the requirements of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) rules concerning advanced service.  Prohibits the carriers from offering advanced service in any State in which 70 percent of the carriers' loop territory is DSL-capable.  Requires the carriers to file a schedule of charges and practices for advanced service in a manner prescribed by the FCC.  Declares that the rates, terms, and conditions of advanced service offered by an incumbent local exchange carrier or its affiliate are not subject to regulation in any geographic area in which that carrier was not the local incumbent exchange carrier on February 8, 1996.

Protecting Domestic Violence and Stalking Victims Act - Amends the federal criminal code to expand the definition of "intimate partner" and "misdeemant," and to expand the prohibition against possessing or receiving a firearm or ammunition in a relationship with a person subject to court order.

Revises stalking prohibitions to include conduct that would be prohibited if committed within the U.S. territory of the defendant.

Insider Trading Prohibition Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to make it unlawful for a person to purchase, sell, or enter into, or cause the purchase or sale of, security-based swap, security-based swap agreement, or security-based swap agreement while in possession of material, nonpublic information relating to such security, swap, or agreement, or relating to the market for such security, swap, or agreement, if such person knows, or recklessly disregards, that such information has been obtained wrongfully, or that such purchase, sale, or entry would constitute a wrongful use of such information. Makes it unlawful for any person whose purchase or sale of a security, security-based swap, or entry into a security-based swap agreement would violate such prohibition to communicate material, nonpublic information relating to such security, swap, or agreement to any other person if: (1) the other person purchases, sells, or causes the purchase or sale of, any security or security-based swap or enters into or causes the entry into any security-based swap agreement; or (2) such a purchase, sale, or entry while in possession of such information is reasonably foreseeable.

Desalination Energy Consumption Reduction Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to make incentive payments to the owners of qualified desalination facilities to encourage the utilization of the best available technology to reduce the consumption of electrical energy in the desalination process.

Authorizes the Secretary to make such payments for up to 10 years, with an option to extend for up to 20 years.

Requires the Secretary to establish a formula for making incentive payments to owners of qualified facilities producing potable water from source waters ranging from 1,000 to 35,000 milligrams per liter total dissolved solids or more.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to any project that: (1) uses innovative technologies to reduce the energy demand of the project; (2) uses renewable energy supplies in the desalination process; (3) provides regional water supply benefits; (4) provides a secure source of new water supplies for national defense activities; (5) reduces the threat of a water supply disruption as a result of a natural disaster or acts of terrorism; (6) uses technologies that minimize the damage to marine life; or (7) provides significant water quality benefits.

Customs Training Enhancement Act - Requires the Commissioner of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to establish and carry out educational seminars at U.S. ports of entry to improve the CBP's ability to classify and appraise articles imported into the United States in accordance with the customs laws of the United States, including to improve the CBP's ability to identify and prevent the mislabeling and transshipment of articles.

Requires the Commissioner to establish at least 15 educational seminars each year under which the Commissioner and selected interested parties should provide instruction and related instructional materials to U.S. Customs and Border Protection personnel and, as appropriate, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement personnel on specified topics, including: (1) the country of origin of an article; (2) the industry supply chain of an article; (3) the accuracy of the manifest or other accompanying documentation; (4) the accuracy of the importation of the article; (5) the importation of the article; (6) the cost of the article; (7) the selection process for interested parties; and (8) other related matters.

Seeds for the Future Act - Amends the Competitive, Special, and Facilities Research Grant Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to ensure that not less than $50 million is allocated each fiscal year for competitive research grants that support the development of public cultivars.

Directs the Under Secretary for Research, Education, and Extension to coordinate research activities relating to the breeding of public cultivars.

Requires the Under Secretary to: (1) convene a working group to carry out coordination functions; (2) promote collaboration among the various entities involved in the public breeding program; (3) ensure that the analysis and activities are made available to the public not later than 60 days after the last day of each fiscal year; (4) develop a strategic plan to establish public cultivar research targets; (5) convene a working group to implement such coordination functions; (6) convene stakeholder listening sessions to provide input on national and regional priorities for public cultivar breeding research activities; and (7) evaluate and make recommendations to the Under Secretary on training and resource needs to meet future breeding challenges.

Patient Access to Durable Medical Equipment Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to extend through June 30, 2017, the transition period for durable medical equipment (DME) under the Medicare program.  The CMS shall, for each item or service furnished with a competitive bid, base its bid on such bids on the basis of such items and services.  The ceiling for a bid submitted for applicable covered items may not be less than the fee schedule amount that would otherwise be determined under Medicare's Patient Access to Durable Medical Equipment Act of 2016 (DME).  The CMS shall, in making any adjustments to the adjustment of a DME item or service, take into account stakeholder input and the highest amount bid by a winning supplier in a competitive acquisition area and a comparison of each of the following with respect to non-competitive acquisition areas and competitive acquisition areas: (1) the average travel distance and cost associated with furnishing items and services in the area; (2) the average delivery time in furnishing items and services in the area; (3) the average volume of items and services furnished by suppliers in the area; and (4) the number

Organic Farmer and Consumer Protection Act of 2017 This bill amends the Organic Foods Production Act of 1990 to revise the National Organic Program to authorize the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to: (1) make appropriations to carry out activities under the program, (2) modernize international trade tracking and data collection systems, and (3) improve the international trade technology systems and data collection system.  The bill also amends the Organic Foods Production Act of 1990 to direct the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to modernize international trade tracking and data collection systems.  The bill also amends the Organic Foods Production Act of 1990 to require USDA to: (1) limit the type of operations that are excluded from certification under the program, and (2) require an accredited certifying agent to obtain additional documentation or verification before granting certification.  USDA must issue regulations to limit the types of operations that are excluded from certification and any corresponding sections of the Act.

Survivor Benefits Improvement Act of 2013 - Amends the federal criminal code to extend the initial period for increasing the dependency and indemnity compensation (DIC) for veterans who die while on active duty in the Armed Forces.  Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide to a surviving spouse of a veteran who dies while on active duty any health care, vocational training, and rehabilitation, and monetary allowance required to be paid to a child of a Vietnam veteran who is suffering from spina bifida.  Directs the Secretary to carry out a pilot program to assess the feasibility and advisability of providing grief counseling services in group retreat settings to surviving spouses of veterans who die while serving on active duty.
Veterans Tobacco Trust Fund Act of 1998 - Amends Federal law to establish in the Treasury the Veterans Tobacco Trust Fund to be funded by appropriations and donated to the fund.

Medicaid Directory of Caregivers Act or the Medicaid DOC Act This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require a state Medicaid plan to include a directory of providers that includes:  the name of the provider, specialty, address, and telephone number of the provider; and  information regarding any participating provider who is accepting new patients and the provider's cultural and linguistic capabilities.  A provider is: (1) in the case of a provider of a provider type for which the state agency requires the enrollment of the provider with the state agency, a provider that is enrolled with the agency and received payment under the state plan in the 12-month preceding the date on which the directory is published or updated, and a provider that received payment under the state plan in the 12-month period preceding the date on which the directory is published or updated; and (2) in the case of a provider of a provider type for which the state agency does not require such enrollment, a provider that received payment under the state plan in the 12-month period preceding the date on which the directory is published or updated.

Fluke Fairness Act of 2013 - Directs the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (the Commission) to submit to the Secretary of Commerce a modified fishery management plan for the commercial and recreational management of summer flounder or an amendment to such plan that: (1) shall be based on the best scientific information available; (2) reflects changes in the distribution, abundance, and location of summer flounder in establishing distribution of the commercial and recreational catch quotas; (3) considers regional, coastwide, or other management measures for summer flounder that comply with the National Standards; and (4) prohibits the allocation of commercial or recreational catch quotas for summer flounder on a State-by-State basis using historical landings data that does not reflect the status of the summer flounder stock, based on the most recent scientific information.  Directs the Secretary to prepare and submit such modified plan or amendment to Congress if the Commission fails to submit a modified plan or amendment that may be approved by the Secretary.  Directs the Comptroller General to report on the implementation of such modified plan or amendment that includes an assessment of whether such implementation complies with the National Standards.

Ending Maternal Mortality Act of 2018 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop and submit to Congress a national plan to reduce the rate of preventable maternal mortality, with the goals of:   cutting the rate in half over the next 10 years; and eliminating preventable maternal deaths by the date that is 20 years after enactment of this Act. HHS must include in each plan:   a list of objectives for meeting the goals, and a strategy for implementing the plan across HHS and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS); and   a list of specified issues related to the plan, including increasing public understanding of maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity, improving data collection, and identifying at-risk populations and eliminating disparities that persist based on a mother's race, ethnicity, socioeconomics, and geographic location. HHS must make each plan publicly accessible on HHS's website.

Backcountry Landing Strip Access Act - Prohibits the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture from taking any action that would permanently close, restrict, or render or declare as unserviceable any aircraft landing strip located on federal land under their respective jurisdictions unless: (1) the action has been approved by the head of the aviation department of the state in which the aircraft landing strip is located; (2) the Secretary publishes notice of the proposed action in the Federal Register, including notice that such action would permanently close, restrict, or render or declare as unserviceable the aircraft landing strip; (3) the Secretary provides for a 90-day public comment period on such action; and (4) the Secretary and the head of the aviation department of the state in which the affected aircraft landing strip is located have taken into consideration any comments received during such period.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) establish a national policy for backcountry aviation issues relating to the management of federal land under the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture; and (2) require officials with jurisdiction over such land to adhere to such policy.

Medicare and Medicaid Hospital Self-Referral Amendments of 1996 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require the discharge plan for a hospital which receives payments under Medicare to include the availability of those services through individuals and entities that participate in the Medicare program and that serve the area in which the patient resides and that request to be listed by the hospital as available.  Requires the discharge plan to:  (1) not specify or otherwise limit the qualified provider which may provide post-hospital care, and (2) identify any provider in which the hospital has a disclosable financial interest or which has such an interest in the hospital.  Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to maintain and disclose to the public certain information on the nature of the financial interest of each individual who was discharged from the hospital and who was identified as requiring the type of post-hospital services provided by the hospital.

Veterans Acquiring Community Care Expect Safe Services Act of 2017 or the Veterans ACCESS Act  (Sec. 2) This bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to deny or revoke the eligibility of a health care provider to provide non-VA health care services to veterans if the provider: (1) was removed from VA employment due to conduct that violated a policy of the VA relating to the delivery of safe and appropriate health care; (2) violated the requirements of a medical license; (3) had a Department credential revoked and the grounds for such revocation impacts the ability of the provider to deliver safe and appropriate health care; or (4) violated a law for which a term of imprisonment of more than one year may be imposed.  The VA may deny, revoke, or suspend the eligibility of a health care provider to provide non-VA health care services if the VA believes that such action is necessary to protect the health, safety, or welfare of veterans and: (1) the provider is under investigation by a state medical licensing board; (2) the provider has entered into a settlement agreement for a disciplinary charge relating to the practice of medicine by the provider; or (3) the VA otherwise determines that such action is appropriate

Scenic Columbia Gorge Restoration Act of 2017 This bill directs the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to begin proposing response activities within a National Scenic Area (NSA) that are adversely impacted by a catastrophic event, including salvage operations and reforestation activities. USDA must allow 30 days for public scoping and comment on such an activity.  An environmental assessment prepared by USDA concerned under this bill must be completed within 60 days after the catastrophic event's conclusion.  A categorical exclusion for an NSA response activity that does not adversely impact a listed species or critical habitat is available for any NSA response activity that: (1) does not exceed 10,000 acres within the NSA, and (2) includes lands that are visible from key viewing areas and are part of a municipal watershed.  USDA must implement the response activity within 15 days of its filing of an objection to it.  An environmental assessment prepared by USDA concerned under this bill must be completed within 60 days after the catastrophic event's conclusion.  No restraining order, preliminary injunction, or injunction pending appeal shall be issued by any U.S. court with respect to any decision to prepare or conduct a response activity. Treatment of Indian Tribal Natural Resource Income Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for a Federal tax treatment of income derived from a natural resources-related activity by Indians directly or through a qualified Indian entity or by a qualified Indian entity.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish a five-person Selection Commission to recommend individuals to the President for appointment to the vacant office of Commissioner of Internal Revenue.  Requires the Commission to be composed of five individuals from among individuals having contacts with the Internal Revenue Service in a professional capacity.  Sets a minimum number of such individuals to be selected from among individuals having contacts with the Service in a specified manner.  Authorizes the President to request the Commission to recommend additional individuals.  Requires the Commission to make its recommendations within 60 days after it is created.  Sets a deadline for the Commission to make its recommendations for the Commissioner.  Terminates the term of the Commissioner.

Government Audit Reform Act of 2010 - Expresses the sense of Congress that the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) should follow the recommendations of the Government Accountability Office report entitled "Single Audit: Opportunities Exist to Improve the Single Audit Process and Oversight."

Amends the federal criminal code to direct the Director to: (1) monitor the risk, cost-benefit, efficiency, and effectiveness of the implementation by federal agencies of this Act by: (1) evaluating such implementation governmentwide; and (2) identifying additional guidance and resources necessary to improve such implementation, including revisions to regulations, best practices, and processes.

Directs the Director to designate an office in the OMB or another federal entity to act on behalf of the Director and submit a report describing such office and the resources made available to adequately implement this Act.

Requires the Director to evaluate the process for the single audit and the program-specific audit to identify simplified alternatives for achieving the purposes of the Single Audit Act of 1984 for the audits of small recipients that also achieve the proper balance between risk and cost-effective accountability for small and large recipients.

Andrew Prior Act or Andrew's Law - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to discharge a private educational loan borrower of a cosigner if the borrower is totally and permanently disabled.

Prohibits the estate of the borrower or any cosigner of such loan from being obligated to repay the outstanding principal or interest on the loan.

Critical Infrastructure Protection Act or CIPA (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to include in national planning scenarios and education programs the threat of EMP events.  The bill also requires DHS to conduct outreach to educate owners and operators of critical infrastructure about the threat of such events.  The bill defines "EMP" as an electromagnetic pulse caused by intentional means, including acts of terrorism, and a geomagnetic disturbance caused by solar storms or other naturally occurring phenomena.  The bill requires DHS, acting through the Under Secretary for Science and Technology, to conduct research and development to mitigate the consequences of such events.  The scope of such research and development shall include: (1) an objective scientific analysis of the risks to critical infrastructures from a range of EMP events; (2) determination of the critical national security assets and vital civic utilities and infrastructures that are at risk from such events; (3) an evaluation of emergency planning and response technologies that would address the findings and recommendations of experts, including the Commission to Assess the Threat to the United States from Electromagnetic Pulse Attack; and (4) an analysis of technology options that are available to improve the resiliency of critical infrastructure to such events

Professional's Access to Health Workforce Integration Act of 2015 This bill authorizes the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to eligible entities to provide services to assist unemployed and underemployed skilled immigrants, who have legal, permanent work authorization and who are internationally educated health professionals, in the American health workforce.

Veterans Benefits Administration Improvement Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit to the Committees on Veterans' Affairs of the Senate and the House of Representatives, the Majority Leader of the Senate, and the Speaker of the House of Representatives a comprehensive plan for the improvement of the processing of veterans compensation and pension claims.

Healthy Schools Partnerships Act of 2010 - Amends the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to require the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to establish a demonstration project to make grants to eligible entities to collaborate with local partner organizations to test and evaluate innovative models to improve school nutrition, student decision making, and healthy school environments.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to entities that demonstrate: (1) a severe need to improve the school environment, as demonstrated by high numbers of students receiving free or reduced price meals, high levels of obesity or other indicators of poor health status, and health disparities in the community served by the school; (2) a commitment by community partners to make in-kind or cash contributions; and (3) the ability to measure results.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to entities that: (1) assess the problem of childhood obesity and poor nutrition in the school environment; (2) develop an innovative plan or intervention to address specific causes of the problem in coordination with outside partners, including by developing and testing innovative models to improve student health and nutrition as measured by changes in school environments, increased access to healthy food, increased physical activity, and increased recess; and (3) changes in school policies that promote access to healthier food and

Small Business Investment Improvement Act of 1999 - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to include among the types of business loans the interest of a small business may receive for purposes of determining whether it is making a net income investment.  Requires such small business to pass through equitable owners of the business to the owners of the business. 
Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to require a small business to make a deduction equal to the net income of the business less State and local taxes.

Pro-Growth Budgeting Act of 2012 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to direct the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to prepare for each major legislation or resolution reported by any congressional committee a macroeconomic impact analysis of the budgetary effects of such legislation or resolution for the ten fiscal-year period beginning with the first fiscal year for which an estimate is prepared and each of the next three ten fiscal-year periods. Requires such estimate to be predicated upon the supplemental projection of such legislation or resolution.

Requires the CBO to submit to the House and Senate Budget Committees a supplemental projection assuming extension of current tax policy for the fiscal year commencing on October 1 of that year with a supplemental projection for the 10 fiscal-year period beginning with that fiscal year, assuming the extension of current tax policy.

Directs the CBO to submit to the House and Senate Budget Committees, for the purposes of this Act, the Long-Term Budget Outlook for the fiscal year commencing on October 1 of that year and at least the ensuing 40 fiscal years.

Federal Land Freedom Act of 2015 This bill authorizes any state that has established a state leasing, permitting, and regulatory program to:   submit a declaration that a state leasing, permitting, and regulatory program has been established, and  seek to transfer responsibility for leasing, permitting, and regulating oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy development from the federal government to the state.  A state may lease, permit, and regulate the exploration and development of oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy on federal land in lieu of the federal government.  Any action by a state to lease, permit, or regulate the exploration and development of oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy pursuant to this Act shall not be subject to, or considered a federal action, federal permit, or federal license under:  the Administrative Procedure Act, the National Historic Preservation Act, the Endangered Species Act of 1973, or the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969.  Any lease or permit issued by a state pursuant to this Act shall include provisions for the collection of royalties or other revenues in an amount equal to the amount of royalties or revenues that would have been collected if the lease or permit had been issued by the federal government.

Pink Tax Repeal Act - Prohibits any person from selling or offering for sale in interstate commerce any two consumer products from the same manufacturer that are substantially similar if such products are priced differently based on the gender of the individuals for whose use the products are intended or marketed. Treats a violation of this prohibition as a violation of the Federal Trade Commission Act defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice in or affecting interstate commerce.

Defines an "unfair or deceptive act or practice" as one in which a practice or term is prohibited by law, regulation, or a rule of practice that is deceptive, with respect to goods or services, or that is not reasonably practicable, to the greatest extent practicable.

Defines a "substantially similar product" as one that: (1) has the same materials and functions; and (2) is sold at a lower or higher price or in a different color or design than the rest of the product.

Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act - Amends Federal law to provide for competitive service for Federal employees in the land management agencies of the Department of the Interior, the Department of Agriculture (USDA), the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), the National Park Service (NPS), and the Fish and Wildlife Service.

Provides for the appointment of employees of such agencies to competitive service successor permanent positions.

Amends the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA) to require that:  (1) the operator of a hazardous substance release facility notify the National Response Center (NRC) established under the Clean Water Act and the State emergency response commission (SERC) established under the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act of 1980 (the Act); and (2) the NRC, the SERC, or the appropriate state agency designated by state law notify the governor of any state affected by the release. 
Requires the NRC, the SERC, or the appropriate state agency designated by state law to convey notification to the NRC and the NRC, if the NRC is notified directly of a release, within two hours to all appropriate government agencies, including the governor of any affected state. 
Requires the NRC, if the state emergency response commission receives notification of such release from a person in charge of a vessel or an offshore or onshore facility, to convey notification to the NRC and the NRC, if the NRC is notified of such release to the NRC and the NRC is notified of the NRC's response to the release, within two hours to the NRC and the NRC. Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a common trust fund to be used to pay dividends to a regulated investment company without the common trust fund receiving a tax deduction for such dividends.

Nuclear Power Plant Safety Act of 2011 - Amends the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to require the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to initiate a rulemaking to revise its regulations to ensure that each licensed utilization facility can withstand and adequately respond to an earthquake, tsunami, strong storm, or other event that threatens a major impact to the facility, a loss of the primary operating power source for at least 14 days, and a loss of the primary backup operating power source for at least 72 hours.

Requires the revision of such regulations to provide for: (1) a requirement that each licensed facility include resilient containment, safety, and diagnostic systems sufficient to withstand such conditions; (2) a requirement that licensees have at least 14 days worth of emergency power system fuel onsite with which to power the facility in the event of a loss of the primary operating power source; (3) a requirement that licensees have sufficient secondary emergency power to power the facility in the event of a loss of both the primary operating power source and the emergency power system for at least 72 hours; (4) a requirement that licensees develop and obtain approval from the NRC for a plan to obtain sufficient additional fuel or batteries in the event of a long duration

Peer Support Communities of Recovery Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to revise requirements for grants to national nonprofit entities focused on substance use disorder (substance misuse grantees) with a network of local affiliates and partners that are geographically and organizationally diverse to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to such entities to establish regional technical assistance centers to provide regional technical assistance for: (1) implementation of regionally driven, peer-delivered addiction recovery support services before, during, after, or in conjunction with addiction treatment; and (2) establishment of recovery community organizations. HHS must reduce the amount of funds awarded to recovery community organizations to allow grantees to use such funds to carry out the activities described in this Act.

Child Care Criminal Background Check Act of 2009 - Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to require a state child care provider licensing board to: (1) certify that the state will require each eligible child care provider (excluding one eligible provider described in this Act) that is licensed by the state or receives funds under the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to obtain a comprehensive criminal background check of: (1) each employee who provides child care services; (2) each applicant for employment; and (3) each family child care provider who provides or applies to provide such services.

Requires a state child care provider to refuse to employ an individual to provide such services if the individual was convicted of a crime of violence or a crime against a child for which a penalty exceeding one year is established.

Requires a state child care provider to carry out at the request of an eligible child care provider a comprehensive criminal background check of each employee of, and each applicant for employment, a child care provider that is licensed by the state.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to reduce by 10% the allotment for the fiscal year following the fiscal year in which noncompliance is found.

Volunteer Emergency Services Recruitment and Retention Act of 2006 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a plan for length of service awards to bona fide volunteer employees to be treated as an eligible deferred compensation plan.

Exempts such plans from the employer retirement income security tax deduction for compensation received for such services.

Medicaid Reform and Personal Responsibility Act of 2017 This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require states to apply a work requirement for able-bodied adults without dependents under Medicaid. A "work requirement" is participation in activity specified by the state as work for purposes of this Act for 20 hours or more per week, averaged monthly.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Commerce to develop and implement a comprehensive program for fish screens, fish passage devices, and other measures agreed to by local interests and relevant Federal agencies for water diversions by local governmental entities in Oregon, Washington, Montana, and Idaho.  Requires non-Federal participation in such program to be voluntary. 
Requires the Secretary to take no action that would result in non-Federal entities being held financially responsible for any action unless the entity applies to participate in the program. 
Requires the program to consist of:  (1) inventory of screened and unscreened diversions and evaluation of the effectiveness of fish screens, fish passage devices, and other measures in existence on the date of enactment of this Act; (2) identification and prioritization of critical areas for improvement; and (3) development and execution of an implementation and construction program. 
Requires a recommended fish screen, fish passage device, or other measure to meet the requirements of the United States Fish and Wildlife Service or the National Marine Fisheries Service and be agreed to by all interested Federal and non-Federal entities. 
Requires the cost of studies conducted with respect to such program to be shared in accordance with the Water Resources Development Act of 1986

DMZ War Veterans Recognition Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service (NPS), to place a plaque on or near the grounds of the Korean War Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., to commemorate the sacrifices of those who served, were wounded, or were killed from 1953 until the present in the defense of the Republic of Korea.

Hydrographic Services Improvement Act Amendments of 2008 - Amends the Hydrographic Services Improvement Act of 1998 to revise the functions of the Coast and Geodetic Survey (CGTS) and the National Geodetic Survey (NGS) to include the provision of hydrographic data and the provision of hydrographic services.

Authorizes the Administrator of the U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey to acquire hydrographic data and provide hydrographic services to: (1) support the conservation and management of coastal and ocean resources; (2) save and protect life and property; (3) support the resumption of commerce in response to emergencies, natural disasters, and man-made disasters; and (4) meet homeland security and maritime domain awareness needs.

Authorizes appropriations.

Authorizes the Administrator to carry out nautical mapping and charting functions under such Act.

Amends the Act to include in the CGTS and the NGS functions of the tide and current measurement functions.

Amends the Act to add the functions of the tide and current measurement functions to include the functions of the data acquisition and the provision of hydrographic services.

Community Gardening and Nutrition Act of 2014 - Amends the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973 to authorize the Assistant Director of the National and Community Service Administration to establish a Community Garden Pilot Program to carry out 40 community garden projects.  Requires the Director of the National and Community Service Administration to give priority to projects in varied geographic regions and to selecting a balance of urban and rural projects.  Authorizes appropriations.

Federal Internship Improvement Act - Requires the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to: (1) make publicly available on the Internet specified information regarding the names and contact information of the coordinator of an internship program and the individual who will serve as such coordinator, and information regarding application procedures and deadlines for each internship program; (2) establish and maintain a centralized electronic database containing the names, contact information, and relevant skills of individuals who have completed or are nearing completion of an internship program and are currently seeking full-time Federal employment; (3) conduct an annual exit interview and administer a survey to ensure uniformity across agencies; (4) report annually to the Office on the number of interns who participated in an internship program at such agency, the demographic characteristics of interns, agency steps taken to increase the percentage of interns who are offered permanent Federal jobs, and barriers encountered; and (5) report to Congress on the information submitted to the Office.

Concussion Treatment and Care Tools Act of 2010 or the ConTACT Act of 2010 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to establish concussion management guidelines that address the prevention, identification, treatment, and management of concussions in school-aged children, including standards for such children to return to play after experiencing such a concussion.

Directs the Secretary to convene a conference of medical, athletic, and educational stakeholders to assist in the establishment of such guidelines.

Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to states for: (1) providing for the collection by target entities of information on the incidence and prevalence of concussions among school-aged children; (2) adopting, disseminating, and ensuring the implementation by target entities of the guidelines; (3) funding implementation by target entities of preseason baseline and post-injury testing, including computerized testing, for school-aged children; and (4) any other activity or purpose specified by the Secretary.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on the implementation of such guidelines.

Hunter and Farmer Protection Act of 2015 This bill amends the Migratory Bird Treaty Act to prohibit the taking of migratory bird species by any person who knows or should reasonably should know that the area is a baited area.  The Department of the Interior may promulgate regulations to implement this bill.

International Money Transfer Disclosure Act - Requires the appropriate Federal agencies to jointly prescribe regulations that require any financial institution or money transmitting business which initiates an international money transfer on behalf of a consumer (whether or not the consumer maintains an account at such institution or business) to make a good faith effort to provide the following disclosures to the consumer before the consummation of the transaction: (1) fees to be charged to the recipient, including exchange rate or currency conversion fees; (2) a final itemization of all costs to the consumer, including all fees charged, for the remittance; and (3) the exact amount of foreign currency to be received by the recipient in the foreign country.

Requires such disclosures to be in English and in the same language, if other than English, as the language principally used by the financial institution or business to advertise, solicit, or negotiate, at the institution or business's office at which the international money transfer is initiated.

Requires compliance with such requirements to be enforced under: (1) the Federal Deposit Insurance Act, in the case of an insured depository institution; and (2) the Federal Credit Union Act, in the case of any insured credit union.

Requires compliance with this Act to be exercised by any agency, for the purpose of enforcing

Mental Health First Act of 2013 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to states, political subdivisions of states, Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and nonprofit private entities to initiate and sustain mental health first aid training programs. Requires such training to be designed to train individuals in the categories of: (1) emergency services and other first responders, (2) law enforcement personnel, (3) teachers and school administrators, (4) human resources professionals, (5) nurses and other primary care personnel, and (6) students enrolled in elementary, secondary, or an institution of higher education. Requires the training to be designed to accomplish the following objectives: (1) to assist individuals in crisis to connect with appropriate local mental health care services; (2) to identify and report to appropriate local mental health care services; and (3) to refer to such services when appropriate. Requires the training to be provided by trained trainers licensed and credentialed by nonprofit entities as designated by the Secretary. Requires the training to be provided in a live, safe, and appropriate manner. Requires the Secretary to pay particular attention to the mental health training needs of populations and target audiences residing in rural areas.

Mandate Prevention Act of 2010 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require any bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report that would increase the direct costs of federal private sector mandates by an amount that causes specified thresholds to be exceeded, unless: (1) the bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report provides new budget authority or new entitlement authority in the House of Representatives or direct spending authority in the Senate for each fiscal year for such mandates included in the report in an amount equal to or exceeding the direct costs of such mandate; or (2) the bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report includes an authorization for appropriations in an amount equal to or exceeding the direct costs of such mandate and identifies a specific dollar amount of such costs for each year up to ten years during which such mandate shall be in effect.

Requires the responsible federal agency to: (1) determine whether there are insufficient appropriations for that fiscal year to provide for the direct costs of such mandate, and (2) notify the appropriate authorizing committees of Congress of the determination and submit either: (1) a statement that the agency has determined, based on a re-estimate of the direct costs of such mandate

Free File Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of the Treasury to continue to operate the IRS Free File Program as established by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and published in the Federal Register on November 4, 2002. The program shall continue to provide free commercial-type online individual income tax preparation and electronic filing services to the lowest 70% of taxpayers by income. The number of eligible taxpayers receiving such services shall be calculated based on prior year aggregate taxpayer adjusted gross income data.  The IRS Free File Program shall continue to make available to all taxpayers (without regard to income) a basic, online electronic fillable forms utility.  The IRS Free File Program shall continue to work cooperatively with the private sector to provide the free individual income tax preparation and the electronic filing services described in this bill.

Presidential Library Donation Reform Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the federal criminal code to require the Department of the Treasury to publish on the National Archives and Records Administration website information regarding every contributor who gave the organization a contribution or contributions (whether monetary or in-kind) totaling $200 or more for the quarterly period.  The requirement to submit such information shall continue until the later of: (1) the Archivist of the United States has accepted, taken title to, or entered into an agreement to use any land or facility for the Presidential archival depository for the President, or (2) the President whose archives are contained in the deposit no longer holds the Office of President.  The bill prohibits the Archivist from knowingly and willfully submitting false material information or omitting material information with respect to the contribution.  The penalties for violations of this requirement shall apply to a violation in the same manner as a violation of the federal criminal code.  The bill also prohibits a person from making a contribution in the name of another person, from permitting his or her name to be used to effect a contribution, or from accepting a contribution that is made by one person in the name of another person.

Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp Promotion Act of 1998 - Amends the Migratory Bird Conservation Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to use from receipts from the sale of migratory bird hunting and conservation stamps an amount not to exceed $1 million for each of FY 1999 through 2003 for the promotion of additional stamp sales. 
Directs the Secretary to include in each report under the Act a statement of all expenditures under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act and a copy to the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission, the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate, and the Committee on Resources of the House of Representatives. 
Directs the Act to provide a copy to the Commission, the Senate Committee on Agriculture and the Ways and Means Committee, and the House Committee on the Judiciary Committee. 
Amends the Sikes Act to authorize the Secretary to make a one-time payment of $100,000 to the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission to promote additional stamp sales.

Renewable Energy Investment Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2015: (1) the renewable electricity production credit, (2) the tax credit for investment in alternative fuel property, and (3) the tax credit for alcohol fuels.

Authorizes the extension of the renewable electricity production credit through 2015.

Extends through 2015: (1) the tax credit for investment in advanced energy facilities, and (2) the tax credit for investment in renewable fuel property.

Authorizes appropriations for advanced biofuels research, development, and demonstration.

National Reconstruction Study Area Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service (NPS), to complete a study of the study area to assess the suitability and feasibility of designating the study area as a unit of the National Park System.

Directs the Attorney General to provide for the granting of posthumous citizenship (as of September 10, 2001) to a person who: (1) died as a result of an injury incurred in one or more of specified events; (2) was not culpable for any of such events; and (3) on September 11, 2001, had pending an application for naturalization or a certificate of citizenship filed by the person.

Strengthening Background Checks Act of 2013 - Amends the NICS Improvement Amendments Act of 2007 to increase the mandatory penalties for a state that fails to make data available to the national instant criminal background check system (NICS).  Directs the Attorney General to withhold 10% of the amount that would otherwise be allocated to a state under the NICS Improvement Amendments Act of 2007 if the state: (1) fails to comply with the requirements of this Act, or (2) provides less than 90% of the records required to be provided under NICS.  Amends the NICS Improvement Amendments Act of 2007 to authorize the Attorney General to waive such requirement for a year if the state provides substantial evidence that it is making reasonable efforts to comply with the requirements of this Act.  Amends the NICS Improvement Amendments Act of 2007 to authorize the Attorney General to waive such requirement for additional one-year periods if the state provides substantial evidence that it is making reasonable efforts to comply with the requirements of this Act. Freedom to Fish Act - Amends the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act to eliminate the authority of the Secretary of Commerce to regulate recreational fishing in national marine sanctuaries unless: (1) there is a clear indication that recreational fishermen are the cause of a specific conservation problem and that less severe conservation measures will not adequately provide for conservation and management of the affected stocks of fish; (2) the closed area regulation includes specific measurable criteria to determine the conservation benefit of the closed area on the affected stocks of fish and provides a timetable for periodic review of the continued need for the closed area; (3) the closed area is no larger than that which is supported by the best available scientific information; or (4) provision is made to reopen the closed area to recreational fishing whenever the condition in the closed area that was the basis of the closure no longer exists.
Amends the National Marine Sanctuaries Act to revise the Magnuson-Stevens Act to require the Secretary to provide the appropriate Regional Fishery Management Council with the opportunity to propose, and revise from time to time, all regulations applicable to fishing within designated marine sanctuaries according to the standards and procedures of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act. Requires such regulations, upon approval by the Secretary, to apply

State Court Interpreter Grant Program Act - Directs the Administrator of the Office of Justice Programs of the Department of Justice to make grants to States to develop and implement court interpreter technical assistance programs to assist individuals with limited English proficiency in accessing and understanding State court proceedings in which they are a party.

Requires the Administrator to allocate specified amounts to each State for each fiscal year for which extraordinary needs must be addressed in order to develop, implement, or expand a State court interpreter program.

Social Security Caregiver Credit Act of 2018 This bill amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to deem wage payments under OASDI for caregivers of dependent relatives in the case of a death after such month (in addition to wages or self-employment income actually paid to or derived by such individual during such month) at an amount per month equal to: (1) 50% of the national average wage index for the second calendar year preceding the calendar year in which the month occurs; and (2) the excess of the amount determined over 1/2 of the wages or self-employment income actually paid to or derived by such individual during such month over 1/2 of the wages or self-employment income actually paid to or derived during the preceding calendar year.

Sexual Assault Prosecution Act of 2002 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit sexual offenses against women and girls, including murder, rape, and sexual or sexual assault, in violation of the provisions of this Act.Directs the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation to develop a plan to grant voluntary awards to States to facilitate DNA analysis of all casework evidence of unsolved crimes.Directs the Assistant Attorney General of the Office of Justice Programs to develop criteria for the granting of such awards, including the number of unsolved crimes awaiting DNA analysis in the State that is applying for an award, and the development of a comprehensive plan to collect and analyze DNA evidence by the State applying for an award.

Over-the-Counter Hearing Aid Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to promulgate regulations to establish a category of over-the-counter hearing aids as defined by this Act. The FDA must issue regulations to establish a category of hearing aids that are identical to, but not identical to, the regulations promulgated by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). HHS must update and finalize the draft guidance of the Department of Health and Human Services entitled, "Regulatory Requirements for Hearing Aid Devices and Personal Sound Amplification Products," issued on November 7, 2013.

Red Cliffs Desert Reserve Completion Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to pay James Doyle, out of money not otherwise appropriated, a sum of money, in an amount to be determined by the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, representing the amount to which Doyle may be entitled to make James Doyle whole for any damages and losses sustained by Doyle by reason of the Federal Government's taking of approximately 2,000 acres of his land located in the St. George area of Utah, now designated as the Red Cliffs Desert Reserve and set aside as habitat for the Mojave desert tortoise, a species listed under the Endangered Species Act of 1973.

Teaching Children to Save Lives Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Education to award grants to local educational agencies or targeted schools for implementing nationally recognized CPR and AED training courses.

Authorizes the Secretary to use such grants to: (1) train individuals in CPR and AED skills and instruction; (2) obtain printed informational or instructional materials; (3) obtain manikins; (4) obtain AED training devices; and (5) obtain other equipment as determined appropriate by the Secretary.

Requires the Secretary to award grants based on: (1) demonstrated need for initiating a CPR or AED training program in a targeted school or community served by targeted schools; (2) demonstrated need for continued support of an existing CPR or AED training programs in targeted schools or communities served by targeted schools; and (3) opportunities to encourage and foster partnerships with and among community organizations, including emergency medical service providers, fire and police departments, nonprofit organizations, public health organizations, and parent-teacher associations to aid in providing CPR or AED training.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on grant amounts and recipients, how the funds were used, and the impact of the funds on the development of CPR and AED training programs in schools implementing the grants.

Comprehensive Problem Gambling Act of 2011 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish and implement programs for the prevention, treatment, and research of pathological and other problem gambling.

Directs the Secretary, acting through the Administrator, to carry out a national campaign to increase knowledge and raise awareness within the general public with respect to problem gambling.

Requires the Secretary, in carrying out such campaign, to carry out activities that include augmenting and supporting existing national campaigns and producing and placing public service announcements.

Authorizes the Secretary, in carrying out such campaign, to: (1) coordinate the voluntary donation of, and administer, resources to assist in the implementation of, new programs and the augmentation and support of existing national campaigns to provide national strategies for dissemination of information to treat problem gambling; and (2) encourage media outlets to provide information aimed at preventing problem gambling.

Requires the Secretary, in carrying out such campaign, to target radio and television audiences of events including sporting and gambling events.

Requires the Secretary, in carrying out such campaign, to evaluate the effectiveness of activities under this Act.

Welfare Improvement Act of 1997 - Amends title IV part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of the Social Security Act to prohibit a State from using any part of the grant under TANF for cash benefits for a minor child who is born to a receiving family receiving assistance under the State TANF program or a person who received such assistance at any time during the ten-month period ending with the birth of the child.  Excludes from such prohibition a child who is born into a family that does not include any other children. 
Amends part A of title IV to prohibit a State from:  (1) recruiting activities; and (2) revoking authority to recruit under the State TANF program. 
Amends part V (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of the Social Security Act to require States to:  (1) establish a random testing program for use of controlled substances by an individual in a family receiving TANF assistance; and (2) terminate TANF assistance for any individual who tests positive for the use of controlled substances.

Researchers and Farmers Freedom From Terrorism Act of 2000 - Amends the Federal criminal code to provide for imprisonment for five years and a death sentence for animal enterprise terrorism. Directs the Director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms to establish and maintain a national clearinghouse for information on crime and terrorism committed against or directed at any animal enterprise.

Gun Victim Compensation Act - Amends the federal criminal code to provide that any person who sells, delivers, or otherwise transfers a firearm in violation of the prohibition against the sale or other transfer of a firearm by a person who is under 18 years of age shall be liable for damages caused by a discharge of the transferred firearm by the transferee.

Provides that no such liability shall apply to: (1) a temporary transfer of a handgun to a juvenile if the handgun is used in the course of employment, in the course of ranch or farming related to the operation of the farm or ranch, hunting, or a course of instruction in the safe and lawful use of a handgun; (2) a ranch or farming activity with the prior written approval of the juvenile's parent or legal guardian and at the direction of an adult who is not prohibited by federal, state, or local law; (3) ranch or farming activities with the prior written approval of the juvenile's parent or legal guardian and at the direction of an adult who is not prohibited by federal, state, or local law; (4) ranch or farming activities with the prior written approval of the juvenile's parent or legal guardian and at the direction of an adult who is not prohibited by federal, state,

Small Business Relief and Job Creation Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an unemployed individual who begins work for an eligible small business during 2018 or 2019 to elect to treat such individual as a member of a targeted group for purposes of the unemployment compensation tax credit.

Stop the Sale of Murderabilia Act of 2013 - Amends the federal criminal code to prohibit a prison inmate convicted of a crime of violence who knowingly deposits for mailing or delivery, or knowingly causes to be delivered by mail, any property, article, or object, with intent that it be placed in interstate or foreign commerce, from being imprisoned for more than six months and from receiving a prison sentence for more than ten years. Provides for criminal forfeiture of property used to commit, facilitate, or promote the commission of, a crime or derived from, or traceable to, the gross proceeds of such crime. Authorizes civil remedies, including injunctive relief, damages, and attorney fees, for violations of this Act.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior or the Secretary of Agriculture to develop and implement a process to expedite access to federal lands under the administrative jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior for eligible organizations and individuals to request access to such lands to conduct good Samaritan search-and-recovery missions.

Requires the Secretary to notify eligible organizations and individuals of the approval or denial of a request by an eligible organization and eligible individual to carry out a good Samaritan search-and-recovery mission within 48 hours after the request is made.

Requires the Secretary to develop search-and-recovery focused partnerships with search-and-recovery organizations to: (1) coordinate good Samaritan search-and-recovery missions on federal lands under the administrative jurisdiction of the Secretary; and (2) expedite and accelerate mission efforts for missing individuals on federal lands under the administrative jurisdiction of the Secretary.

MMA Territorial Equity for Low-Income Individuals Act of 2004 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for the equitable treatment of residents of territories under Medicare prescription drug (Prescription Drug) Transitional Assistance Program (PTA).

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to request the Institute of Medicine of the National Academy of Sciences to study the access of Medicare beneficiaries in the United States territories to prescription drugs during each of three periods: (1) before Medicare enactment, (2) during the implementation of the prescription drug benefit program, and (3) beginning on January 1, 2006.

Volunteer First Responders Housing Act - Allows a qualified volunteer first responder who submits to the Secretary of Agriculture a verification letter in accordance with this Act to be eligible for a verified adjustment in annual income in the amount of $18,000.

Requires a qualified volunteer first responder to submit to the Secretary a verification letter from the eligible employer for which the volunteer first responder volunteers, which shall: (1) include the date on which the volunteer first responder joined the eligible employer as a volunteer, (2) attest to the Secretary that the volunteer first responder continuously served as a volunteer for the eligible employer during the two-year period preceding the verification letter, and (3) include a copy of the certification of the volunteer first responder as a firefighter or other responder in the state, unit of general local government, or Indian tribe in which the individual served as a volunteer.

Requires the Secretary to amend the Good Neighbor Next Door Sales Program of the Department of Housing and Urban Development to provide that a qualified volunteer first responder who qualifies as a firefighter or emergency medical technician for purposes of the Department's Good Neighbor Next Door Sales Program shall qualify as a firefighter or emergency medical technician for the Department's Good Samaritan Next Door Sales Program.

This bill directs the Department of Transportation to provide the following assistance to the Rockland Harbor, Maine, area: (1) a supplemental major rehabilitation report; and (2) an evaluation of existing conditions at the Herbert Hoover Dike navigation system.

Forest Roads-Community Right-To-Know Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agriculture, and the Secretary of the Treasury to meet with appropriate State and local government officials to describe all agency plans or proposals that, within the next two fiscal years, will or may result in the permanent closure of Forest roads on Federal lands. Requires the Secretary concerned to provide information that: (1) shows Forest roads selected or proposed for permanent closure; (2) shows traffic patterns and volumes on the roads over the previous five years; and (3) explains how users of the roads will be adversely affected with longer travel times or adverse travel conditions by the permanent closure of the roads.

Prohibits the Secretary concerned from proceeding with the permanent closure of a Forest road until the end of the 90-day period beginning on the date that the announcement regarding the road's permanent closure was published in the local newspaper of record.

Prohibits the permanent closure of any Forest road implemented during the fiscal year in which this Act is enacted unless: (1) advance notice of the permanent closure is provided to the appropriate State and local government officials; and (2) the Secretary complies with the public notice and comment requirements.

Estate and Gift Tax Phase-Out Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to phase out the estate and gift tax through increases in unified estate and gift tax credit amounts. 
Repeals the Federal transfer tax.

Common Sense Campaign Reform Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a limited tax credit for contributions to a candidate for federal office.  Increases such credit ceiling to $2,500 for taxpayers in the same state as the candidate. 
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to increase the ceiling for the income tax credit for contributions to a candidate for federal office by persons other than multicandidate political committees. 
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require a multicandidate political committee to include in its name the name of the entity that establishes the fund. 
Requires a multi-candidate political committee to include in its name the name of the entity that establishes the fund. 
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require any separate segregated fund that is a multicandidate political committee to include in its name the name of the entity that establishes the fund.

Developing Resources Immediately and Long-Term through Leases on Our Nation's Offshore Waters Act of 2009 or the DRILL NOW Act of 2009 - Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to authorize the President to withdraw any lands of the outer Continental Shelf from disposition for exploration, development, or production of oil and gas, except as necessary for national security purposes.

Authorizes the governor of a state to petition the Secretary of the Treasury to issue leases authorizing the conduct of oil and natural gas exploration and extraction activities in any area within 50 miles of the coastline of the state and within the lateral seaward boundaries of the state extended.

Requires the Secretary to deposit 30% of qualified revenues from leases in the Clean and Alternative Energy Fund and 40% of such revenues in the general fund of the Treasury.

Requires the Secretary to deposit the remainder of qualified revenues from leases in the general fund of the Treasury.

Requires the Secretary to deposit 30% of qualified revenues from any federal oil and gas lease in a separate account in the Treasury, which shall be known as the Clean and Alternative Energy Fund, and 40% of such revenues in the general fund of the Treasury.

Federal Reserve Board Civil Rights Compliance Act of 1999 - Requires the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to post and keep posted in conspicuous places upon its premises where such notices to employees and applicants for employment are customarily posted, and at such other places as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission may determine, a notice to be prepared or approved by the Commission setting forth:  (1) excerpts from or summaries of the pertinent provisions of title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and of Federal law; and (2) information pertinent to the rights and procedures applicable under such Acts to employees of, and applicants for employment by, the Board. 
Directs the Board to report to specified congressional committees on the Board's compliance with such Act.

Neighborhood Security Act of 2003 - Authorizes the Attorney General, through the Office of Justice Programs, to award one or more grants to eligible nonprofit organizations and professional associations to develop and improve Neighborhood Watches throughout the nation.

Education Savings Account and School Excellence Act of 1999 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to permit corporations to contribute to education individual retirement accounts (ERAs) for the benefit of their employees.

Restoring the Partnership for County Health Care Costs Act of 2015 This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) and title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to allow beneficiaries who are released from custody after posting bond or who are released under house arrest to continue to receive Medicaid, Medicare, SSI, and CHIP benefits.
Telephone Call Privacy Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to modify requirements relating to the use and disclosure of customer proprietary network information.

Internet of Things Consumer Tips to Improve Personal Security Act of 2017 or the IOT Consumer TIPS Act of 2017 This bill requires the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to develop voluntary educational cybersecurity resources for consumers relating to the practices of consumers with respect to the protection and use of devices that are part of the Internet of Things (IoT). The resources must be technology-neutral and include guidance, best practices, and advice for consumers to protect against, mitigate, and recover from cybersecurity threats or security vulnerabilities, where technically feasible. The FTC must ensure that the resources are available to the public on the FTC's website.

Indian Tribal Development Corporation Feasibility Study Act of 2004 - Amends the Native American Business Development, Trade Promotion, and Tourism Act of 2000 to direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish the Tribal Development Corporation Feasibility Study Group to: (1) study the feasibility of establishing an Indian Tribal Development Corporation; and (2) report to specified congressional committees on the results of such study and any recommendations for further legislative action.

Authorizes appropriations.

Railroad Hours of Service Act of 2010 - Amends Federal transportation law to revise provisions regarding the nonapplication, exemption, and alternate hours of service (OASDI) for railroad employees.

Defines "yardmaster employee" as an employee who supervises and coordinates the activities of workers engaged in railroad traffic operations, including making up or breaking up trains and switching inbound or outbound traffic.

Defines "dispatcher employee" as an employee who supervises and coordinates the activities of workers engaged in railroad traffic operations, including making up or breaking up trains and switching inbound or outbound traffic.

Defines "duty hours of train employee" as the hours the train employee is required to work on duty while on duty, including any work where there is a potential to interact or otherwise come into contact with safety-critical devices or circuits.

Defines "nonapplication, exemption, and alternate hours of service" as any hours the train employee is required to work on duty, including any work where there is a potential to interact or otherwise come into contact with safety-critical devices or circuits.
