Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area Act of 2015 This bill establishes in Utah the Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area to provide for: (1) the enhancement of recreational uses; and (2) the use of off-highway vehicles.  The bill requires the Department of the Interior, acting through the Director of the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), to: (1) administer the Area and proposed exchange parcel in accordance with applicable federal laws and land use plans, and (2) only allow uses of the Area that are consistent with the purposes of the Sand Mountain Open OHV Area.  If the state of Utah offers to convey to the United States title to the non-federal land, Interior must accept the offer and convey to the state all interest in the federal land.  The bill establishes a process for the exchange of federal and non-federal land.  The bill sets forth the value of the federal and non-federal land to be exchanged and the equalization of the value of the federal and non-federal land.  Interior must add to, and administer as part of, the Area the recreation area as part of the Recreation Area.

Arsenic-Treated Wood Mandatory Labeling Act - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to require each piece of arsenic-treated wood offered for sale in the United States to have affixed to it a consumer warning label that displays specified statements, including: (1) this wood has been treated with arsenic; (2) arsenic exposure through the mishandling of this wood can cause cancer, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; (3) never burn this wood; (4) to avoid the health risks associated with mishandling arsenic-treated wood, you must wear gloves, goggles, coveralls, and face masks when working with it; and (5) wash exposed body areas thoroughly with soap and water after working with arsenic-treated wood.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to promulgate regulations to ensure compliance with and carry out this Act.

Broadband Conduit Deployment Act of 2015 This bill directs the Department of Transportation (DOT) to require states to evaluate the need for broadband conduit in accordance with this bill as part of any covered highway construction project. If the evaluation reveals an anticipated need in the next 15 years for broadband conduit beneath hard surfaces to be constructed by the project, the conduit shall be installed as part of the covered highway construction project.  DOT shall ensure that each broadband conduit installed is placed at a depth consistent with industry best practices and that, in determining the depth of placement, considers the location of existing utilities and the cable separation requirements of state and local electrical codes.  DOT shall ensure that any requesting broadband provider has access to each such conduit on a competitively neutral and nondiscriminatory basis, for a cost-based rate.  The bill authorizes DOT to waive the application of this bill if it is appropriate for a project based upon: (1) a showing of undue burden, (2) a determination that the installation of broadband conduit beneath hard surfaces to be constructed as part of a covered highway construction project is not necessary based on the availability of existing broadband infrastructure, or (3) the consideration of other relevant factors.

Requires the Secretary to reimburse partners for costs relating to the pilot program as specified.

Preserving Data in Government Act of 2017 This bill requires any open government data that is made available to the public for at least 90 consecutive days to remain machine-readable, available in an open format, and part of the worldwide public domain or, if necessary, published with an open license.  It prohibits the alteration of the digital location, format, or content of open government data for the purpose of routine asset maintenance or long-term archiving.  Any such alteration shall not constitute a renewal of the public access period for which the open government data has been made available to the public.  An agency may remove open government data from public availability if: (1) the agency determines that the open government data is too costly to maintain or does not provide sufficient value to the public, (2) not less than six months before the agency removes the data, and (3) the data is available for download on the worldwide public domain for at least six months before the agency removes it.

Genetic Fairness Act of 1996 - Prohibits an insurer offering a health plan from:  (1) terminating, restricting, limiting, or otherwise applying conditions to coverage of an individual or family member under the plan; (2) canceling or refusing to renew the coverage of an individual or family member under the plan; (3) denying coverage or excluding an individual or family member from coverage under the plan; (4) imposing a rider that excludes coverage for certain benefits and services under the plan; (5) establishing differentials in premium rates or cost-sharing for coverage under the plan; or (6) otherwise discriminating against an individual or family member in the provision of health care. 
Requires an insurer offering a health plan to provide an enrollee with a written statement disclosing the rights of the enrollee under this Act. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) enforcement; (2) employee welfare benefit plans; and (3) private cause of action. 
Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to enforce such requirements in the same manner as provided for under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA), except that in no case shall a State enforce such requirements as they relate to employee welfare benefit

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award grants to local educational agencies (LEAs) that have taken steps to improve teacher quality and raise student achievement. 
Requires the Secretary to award such grants to enable such agencies to carry out school construction. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Education Modernization Fund Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to make loans to States for the purpose of constructing and modernizing elementary and secondary schools.  Establishes in the Treasury the Education Modernization Fund.  Requires the Fund to be used for such purposes as specified.

Derivatives and Hedge Fund Regulatory Improvement Act of 2008 - Directs the appropriate federal banking agencies, in coordination with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), to initiate a coordinated rulemaking with respect to the entities under their respective jurisdictions that engage in transactions involving unregistered hedge funds or over-the-counter derivatives to: (1) extend the requirements of regulations relating to the safety and soundness of the financial system applicable to mutual funds under the Investment Company Act of 1940 to unregistered hedge funds; (2) require the fund to disclose its policies on borrowing money and a shareholder vote to change such policy; (3) provide for the regulation of over-the-counter derivatives; and (4) prohibit insured depository institutions from trading derivatives for their own accounts.

Authorizes each of such agencies and authorities to grant exceptions to the requirements of this Act.

Marriage Penalty Relief Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for: (1) elimination of the standard deduction for purposes of the marriage penalty; (2) elimination of the $5,000 dollar limitation on the first marriage penalty; (3) an inflation adjustment to the marriage penalty; and (4) increased phaseout amounts for inflation adjustments.

Repatriate Our Patriots Act - Prohibits a special veteran from being removed from the United States.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to: (1) take steps to ensure that the period in which an application for naturalization is pending does not exceed 90 days; and (2) furnish each special veteran naturalized or naturalized with a certificate of citizenship with a statement that the period in which such application is pending does not exceed 90 days.

Allows a special veteran residing abroad to be naturalized or to be eligible for U.S. military and veterans benefits if the special veteran is unable to understand, or to communicate an understanding of, the meaning of his or her language because of a physical or developmental disability or mental impairment.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to cancel the removal of a special veteran who is in removal proceedings on the date of enactment of this Act.

Directs the Attorney General to rescind any outstanding removal order and any finding that the special veteran is subject to removal or is inadmissible.

Provides for the naturalization of special veterans in removal proceedings or ordered removed.

Provides for the naturalization of special veterans in military and veterans benefits cases.

Mowa Band of Choctaw Indians Recognition Act - Extends Federal recognition to the Mowa Band of Choctaw Indians of Alabama.  Restores Federal rights and privileges of the Tribe.  Transfers all rights and interests in lands held by the Tribe to the United States in trust for the Tribe.  Directs the Secretary of the Interior to accept such lands on behalf of the United States.  Requires the Tribe to be eligible for all services and benefits that are provided by the Federal Government to Indians because of their status as federally recognized Indians.  Permits the Tribe to organize for its common welfare and to adopt a constitution and bylaws in accordance with prescribed Secretary of the Interior regulations.

Know Before You Fly Act This bill amends the Federal Aviation Administration's website to require an air carrier to include in its website a clear statement that it will: (1) provide for hotel accommodations, (2) arrange for ground transportation, (3) provide meal vouchers, (4) arrange for air transportation on another air carrier or foreign air carrier to the passenger's destination, and (5) provide for sleeping facilities, food, and water inside the airport terminal. The information provided by a covered air carrier shall identify each air carrier and foreign air carrier with which the covered air carrier will arrange air transportation. The bill defines "covered air carrier" as an air carrier that provides scheduled or public charter passenger air transportation by operating an aircraft that as originally designed has a passenger capacity of 35 or more seats. The bill directs the FAA to designate an office of the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to receive and analyze reports involving fumes in the air conditioning and pressurization systems of aircraft operated under provisions of the Code of Federal Regulations.

Sport Fish Restoration and Recreational Boating Safety Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Aid in Fish Restoration Act (FAIRA) to revise the annual appropriation for the Department of the Interior for the Coast Guard's annual boating safety program.

Directs the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating to transfer to the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating: (1) $6.5 million for FY2012-FY2017; (2) $200,000 to fund the National Boating Safety Advisory Council established under FAIRI; and (3) not less than $6 million for national boating safety activities of national nonprofit public service organizations and such sums made available for allocation and distribution shall remain available until expended.

Authorizes the Secretary to use not less than $1.2 million in FY2012 for the purposes of the boating safety program.

Extends the exception to the boating safety program from the limitation on transfers to fund.

Revises the recreational boating safety program to: (1) increase from two to five the maximum number of persons to be transferred to the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating; and (2

Disaster-Affected Homeowners Notification Act of 2013 - Requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae), or the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to provide to each mortgagor a direct notification of their inability to make a mortgage payment, including a community-wide notification, in connection with any major disaster declared pursuant to the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act. Requires the applicable agency heads to: (1) provide such direct notification to each mortgagor in accordance with such Act, and (2) issue guidelines regarding measures designed to provide notice and awareness of such notification.

Help Extend Auditory Relief (HEAR) Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of hearing aids as durable medical equipment. Defines "hearing aid" to mean a hearing aid that is: (1) any wearable instrument or device for, offered for, the purpose of, or represented as aiding individuals with, or compensating for, hearing loss that meets certain requirements of the Food and Drug Administration for marketing; and (2) that meets specified requirements regarding the use of hearing aids, including the services of a physician or qualified audiologist who is legally authorized to furnish such services under the state law in which the services are furnished. Defines "hearing aid" to include hearing aids, in the case of an individual who has a hearing loss, a comprehensive audiologic assessment to determine if a hearing aid is appropriate and to determine the need for other diagnostic medical or audiologic testing and a threshold test to determine audio acuity.

Forest Service Financial Accountability Restoration Act of 1999 - Authorizes the Forest Service to make conditional appropriations for FY 1998 through 2000 for discretionary programs and activities relating to the restoration of Forest Service financial accountability. 
Requires the Forest Service to maintain or increase outputs, relative to the levels achieved during FY 1999, from programs that directly reduce the natural resources restoration and maintenance backlog within the National Forest System.

Distributed Power Hybrid Energy Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy to develop and transmit to the Congress a distributed power hybrid systems strategy showing: (1) opportunities and priorities that might best be met with distributed power hybrid systems configurations; (2) what barriers exist to the use of distributed power hybrid systems; (3) what technology gaps need to be closed; and (4) what system integration tools are needed to plan, design, build, and operate distributed power hybrid systems for maximum benefits.

National Urban Watershed Model Restoration Act - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to develop and carry out a pilot program to serve as a national model for the restoration of urban watersheds and community environments.  Requires such program to be carried out in the Anacostia River watershed, District of Columbia and Maryland. 
Directs the Administrator to:  (1) integrate on a community or geographic basis the regulatory and nonregulatory programs of the Environmental Protection Agency with other Federal, State, and local government programs and provide effective coordination among such programs; (2) support baseline monitoring efforts of State and local governments to determine key trends in ambient environmental conditions for the purpose of filling gaps in critical data about the environmental condition of the watershed; (3) develop and maintain environmental indicators in conjunction with interested public entities and ensure regular public reporting of such indicators; (4) provide grants to local community groups and nonprofit organizations to foster community involvement in the decision making process, environmental educational goals, and restoration strategies; (5) assist in the establishment of measurable goals for such restoration; (6) maintain annual program plans which provide for public input; (7) provide opportunities for the education of school children and community groups on local environmental resources and on what individuals can do to reduce environmental and

Social Security Disability Amendments Act of 1994 - Amends title XVI (Supplemental Security Income) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to disregard deemed income and resources of ineligible spouse when determining continued eligibility under SSA title XVI (b) (Supplemental Security Income) for individuals with disabilities. 
Expands the rules for the exclusion of certain grant, scholarship, or fellowship income from the determination of continued eligibility. 
Amends SSA title XVI to provide for the treatment of certain grant, scholarship, or fellowship income as earned income for purposes of SSI eligibility.

Truth in Video Game Rating Act - Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to prescribe rules to prohibit any rating organization from assigning a content rating to any video or computer game that is to bear a label containing such content rating when sold or distributed in interstate commerce unless such rating organization has reviewed the playable content of the video or computer game in its entirety.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on the efficacy of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board (ESTB) in assigning appropriate content ratings to video and computer games, including ratings for online or Internet-based games.

Requires the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, to act as the lead federal agency for coordinating and disseminating information on existing federal programs and assistance that may be used to help initiate, develop, and finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy retrofitting projects for schools.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) review existing programs and financing mechanisms available in or from the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Energy, the Department of Education, the Department of the Treasury, the Internal Revenue Service, the Environmental Protection Agency, and other appropriate federal agencies with jurisdiction over energy financing and facilitation that are currently used to help initiate, develop, and finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy retrofitting projects for schools; (2) establish a federal cross-departmental collaborative coordination, education, and outreach effort to streamline communication and promote available federal opportunities and assistance for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy retrofitting projects that enables states, local educational agencies, and schools to use existing federal opportunities more effectively and to form partnerships with governors, state energy programs, local educational, financial, and energy officials, nonprofit organizations, and other appropriate entities to support the initiation of the projects; (3) provide technical assistance for states, local educational agencies, and schools

Nonprofit Energy Efficiency Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to establish a pilot program to award grants for the purpose of retrofitting nonprofit buildings owned by nonprofit organizations with energy-efficiency improvements.

Authorizes the Secretary to award such a grant if an applicant submits an application at the time specified in this Act and containing the information the Secretary may prescribe.

Subjects such grants to a minimum non-federal cost-sharing requirement of 50%.

Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to eliminate the requirement that the Secretary report to Congress on the cost-effectiveness of energy-efficiency improvements to nonprofit buildings.

Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to require the Secretary of Labor to notify pension plan administrators of an individual's account plan if the percentage of assets in the individual account that consists of employer securities and employer real property exceeds 50 percent of the total account. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from the gross income of an individual taxpayer a specified amount of employer securities and real property held through an investment option of the individual's plan which is not designed to invest primarily in employer securities or employer real property. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to prohibit the Secretary from assessing a civil penalty against a plan administrator of up to $100 a day from the date of the plan administrator's failure or refusal to provide notice to participants and beneficiaries. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for the tax treatment of certain tax-exempt retirement plans.

Medicare HMO Protection Act of 1998 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to delay the effectiveness of a Medicare+Choice organization's termination of a contract under this Act if the Secretary determines that:  (1) the termination would cause an imminent and serious health risk to the enrollees; (2) the termination would result in a significant reduction in the Medicare+Choice plans available in the area affected; or (3) the organization terminating coverage is offering Medicare+Choice plans in contract areas that are in close proximity to the affected area without suffering considerable financial losses. 
Authorizes the Secretary to renegotiate a contract for a new contract under which the organization shall continue coverage.  Permits the Secretary and the organization to negotiate during the period of delay for a new contract which shall enable the organization to continue coverage. 
Requires each contract to require the organization to provide (and pay for) written notice at least 120 days prior to the contract's termination, as well as a description of alternatives for obtaining benefits to each enrollee. 
Requires enrollees to be notified at least 120 days before the termination of the contract.

Focus on Children Act - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to direct the Director of the Budget Office to study and report to the Congress on spending on children and on the budget of the President for the prior fiscal year.

Requires the Director to submit to Congress a report that includes: (1) information and data regarding spending on children under appropriation Acts, including continuing resolutions, for the fiscal year; (2) information and data regarding spending on children under an entitlement authority for that fiscal year; (3) the share of federal spending that constitutes spending on children; and (4) the date on which federal spending on children will be less than outlays for interest on the public debt.

Requires the Director to: (1) develop and maintain an Internet website that provides raw quantitative data relating to spending on children contained in reports and studies required under this Act; (2) develop and maintain an Internet website that provides that data in a widely-accessible file format that allows the public to analyze the data; and (3) develop and maintain an Internet website that provides categories of data by budget account.

Intercity Passenger Rail Trust Fund Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish the Intercity Passenger Rail Trust Fund.  Transfers amounts in the Fund to amounts equivalent to certain taxes received in the Treasury at the rate of five cents for each gallon with respect to which tax is imposed.  Requires that amounts in the Fund be available without fiscal year limitation to finance qualified expenses of:  (1) the National Railroad Passenger Corporation; and (2) each non-Amtrak State.  Requires each non-Amtrak State to receive an amount equal to the lesser of:  (1) the State's qualified expenses for the fiscal year, or (2) the product of 1/12 of 1 percent of the lesser of 100 or 120 percent of the lesser of the aggregate amounts transferred and credited to the Fund for such fiscal year or the aggregate amounts appropriated from the Fund for such fiscal year.  Specifies that if the amount determined under this Act exceeds the amount for any fiscal year, the amount for the following fiscal year shall be increased by the amount of such excess. Guam War Claims Review Commission Act - Establishes the Guam War Claims Review Commission to:  (1) review the facts and circumstances surrounding the implementation and administration of the Guam Meritorious Claims Act and the effectiveness of such Act in addressing the war claims of American nationals residing on Guam between December 8, 1941, and July 21, 1944; (2) review all relevant Federal and Guam territorial laws, records of oral testimony previously taken, and documents in Guam and the Archives of the Federal Government regarding Federal payments of war claims in Guam; (3) advise on any additional compensation that may be necessary to compensate the people of Guam for death, personal injury, forced labor, forced march, and internment; and (4) report to the Secretary of the Interior, the Committee on Resources and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources and the Judiciary of the Senate. 
Directs the Chairman of the Commission to exercise the Commission's executive and administrative powers and to delegate such powers to the Commission's staff. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to carry out a program to provide low-income, minority, or disadvantaged law students with the information, preparation, and financial assistance to gain access to and complete law school study.  Authorizes the Secretary to contract with, or make a grant to, the Council on Legal Education Opportunity to provide law school information and resources to assist law students in their studies.

Federal Public Safety Officer Surviving Spouse Protection Act of 2005 - Amends federal law to provide for termination of a survivor annuity for remarried Federal public safety officers who were killed in the line of duty.

Drug Rebate Equalization Act of 2009 - Amends the Medicaid managed care organization contract with a state to provide that payment for covered outpatient drugs dispensed to eligible individuals who are enrolled with the entity shall be subject to the same rebate required under the state under 1927.

Limits the capitation rate for covered outpatient drugs to that provided for inpatient drugs.

Provides for a contract based on actual cost experience related to rebates and subject to the Federal regulations requiring actuarially sound rates.

Prohibits a state Medicaid managed care organization with a contract from excluding or otherwise restricting coverage of a covered outpatient drug on the basis of policies or practices of the organization, such as those affecting utilization management, formulary adherence, and cost sharing or dispute resolution, in lieu of any state policies or practices relating to the exclusion or restriction of coverage of such drugs.

States that any formulary established by a Medicaid managed care organization with a contract may be based on positive inclusion of drugs selected by a formulary committee consisting of physicians, pharmacists, and other individuals with appropriate clinical experience as long as drugs excluded from the formulary are available through prior authorization.

Prohibits a state Medicaid managed care organization with a contract from being required to maintain the same policies and practices
Grants a Federal charter to the 29th Division Association, Incorporated (a nonprofit corporation organized under the laws of New Jersey).

Improving Department of State Oversight Act of 2015 This bill requires the Department of State, with the concurrence of the Inspector General of the Department, to certify to the congressional intelligence and appropriations committees that the Department has made reasonable efforts to ensure the integrity and independence of the Office of the Inspector General Information Technology (OIG) systems.  The bill amends the Foreign Service Act of 1980 to require the OIG to report to the Inspector General at least every five years on the advisability and feasibility of implementing a multi-tier system for inspecting foreign service posts based on risk.

Partnering to Detect and Defeat Tunnels Act This bill directs the Department of Defense (DOD) to seek to enter into an agreement with Israel to partner and coordinate in developing and deploying technologies to detect and counter tunnels, including by: (1) carrying out research, development, testing, and evaluation activities with respect to tunnel detection technologies; and (2) carrying out operational testing of such technologies in both the United States and Israel.  DOD shall designate a military department or other element of DOD as the lead agency of the federal government for developing technology to counter tunnels.  The Department of the Army shall designate a senior intelligence officer to manage the collection and analysis of intelligence regarding the tactical use of tunnels by state and non-state actors.  The bill authorizes the Department of Defense to carry out this Act for FY2016.

Public Pension Parity Act of 1995 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income any amount received by an individual as a governmental pension (other than a qualified governmental pension received by the taxpayer unless the taxpayer performed the service giving rise to the pension).  Limits such exclusion to the maximum social security benefits of the taxpayer for the taxable year which would be excluded from gross income if such benefit amount were treated as social security benefits received during the taxable year.

Directs the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture to jointly establish a broad-based advisory group to review recommendations on acceptable criteria for determining fair market values and next best alternative use for radio and television communications site uses. 
Directs the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture to jointly establish a broad-based advisory group to review the methodology used in any previous studies and to reach concurrence on such methodology. 
Requires the advisory group to assess the validity of the results of such studies, taking into account all reasonable options for the establishment of fair market values and next best alternative use.

Directs the President to take specified steps, by imposing quotas, tariff surcharges, negotiated enforceable voluntary export restraint agreements, or otherwise, to ensure that the volume of steel products imported into the United States does not exceed the average volume of steel products that was imported monthly into the United States during the preceding 36-month period. 
Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, through the U.S. Customs Service, and the Secretary of Commerce, by implementing a program for administering and enforcing the restraints, to establish and implement a steel import notification and monitoring program. 
Requires the Customs Service to obtain an import notification certificate for steel products imported into the United States.  Requires the Secretary to issue such certificate to any person who files an application that meets the requirements of this Act. 
Requires the Secretary to compile and publish weekly information regarding steel imported into the United States.  Requires the information to include the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States classification, the country of origin, the port of entry, quantity, value of imported, and whether the imports are entered for consumption or are entered into a bonded warehouse or foreign trade zone. 
Directs the Secretary to make such information available to the public.

Protecting Employees and Retirees in Municipal Bankruptcies Act of 2014 - Amends federal bankruptcy law to require a municipal bankruptcy court, in determining a municipality's eligibility to be a debtor under the bankruptcy code, to establish by clear and convincing evidence that it satisfies the requirements of this Act.  Repeals the current limitation on the authority to issue a stay pending appeal of a determination by a bankruptcy court that an entity is eligible to be a debtor and requires the appropriate court of appeals to consider and determine such appeal on an expedited basis.  Directs the appropriate court of appeals to have jurisdiction of an appeal of a determination made by a bankruptcy court that an entity is eligible to be a debtor and to consider and determine such appeal on an expedited basis.  Requires the bankruptcy court to: (1) consider and determine the appeal on an expedited basis, and (2) treat an appeal of a determination made by a bankruptcy court as an action for relief from the obligation to pay the retiree benefits of a municipal bankruptcy debtor.  Requires the authorized representative of the employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement (or retiree benefits) to be the labor organization that is signatory to such agreement unless the organization no longer represents active employees in the bargaining unit the retirees belonged to when

Health Care Fraud and Abuse Advisory Opinion Act of 1994 - Amends title XI of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue advisory opinions as provided in this Act on matters relating to remuneration, inducement to reduce or limit services to individuals entitled to benefits, and fair market value or value received for goods or services.
Alternative Minimum Tax Repeal Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to eliminate the alternative minimum tax on individual taxpayers beginning after 2010.

Great Lakes Ecology Protection Act of 2000 - Amends the Nonindigenous Aquatic Nuisance Prevention and Control Act of 1990 to direct the Secretary of Transportation to issue regulations to prevent the introduction and spread of aquatic nuisance species within the Great Lakes.

Ethanol Stimulus Act of 2006 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow small ethanol producers in two-two states to claim tax credits for producing ethanol from two-two sources. Defines "eligible ethanol production facility" as any ethanol production facility the original use of which commences with the taxpayer after August 8, 2005, and before August 9, 2010, or in the case of a taxpayer constructing property for the taxpayer's own use, the construction of which begins after August 8, 2005, and before August 9, 2010, in a two-two state which is a two-two state on the date of such purchase under this Act.

Directs the Attorney General to make such reports available by electronic means by December 15, 1997.

Amends the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 to prohibit the Export-Import Bank from guaranteeing, insuring, extending credit, or participating in the extension of credit to an entity with respect to the export of any good or service destined for the People's Republic of China unless the Board of Directors of the Bank has determined that the entity has established and is adhering to the code of conduct.

Directs the Bank to withdraw any guarantee, insurance, or credit it has provided to an entity with respect to the export of any good or service destined for China if the Board determines that the entity is not adhering to the code of conduct.

Requires an entity to: (1) provide a safe and healthy workplace; (2) ensure fair employment, including by avoiding child and forced labor, respecting freedom of association and the right to organize and bargain collectively, paying minimum wages required by law or the prevailing industry wage, whichever is higher; and (3) comply with U.S. and local laws promoting good business practices, including laws prohibiting illicit payments and ensuring fair competition.

Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to convey, without consideration, to the State of Colorado all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to a parcel of real property other than Kit Carson Chapel, including improvements, other than Kit Carson Chapel, of the Ft. Lyon Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in southern Colorado.  Prohibits the Secretary from making such conveyance of real property authorized until the Secretary opens at least three health care facilities, and a nursing home care facility, in the Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 19, which shall serve as replacement facilities for the Ft. Lyon Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center.  Authorizes the Secretary to pay the Colorado State or private nursing home care costs incurred in providing nursing home care to any veteran who is relocated from the Ft. Lyon Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, Colorado, to the State of Colorado or such facility, as the case may be, as a result of the closure of the Center.  Requires the Under Secretary for Health of the Department of Veterans Affairs, acting through the Director of VISN 19, to report to the Senate Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs on the status of the health care system for veterans under the Network in the

Genetic Privacy and Nondiscrimination Act of 2003 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit health plans from: (1) adjusting premium or contribution amounts for a group on the basis of predictive genetic information concerning any individual or family member of the individual; or (2) requiring health plans to adjust premium or contribution rates for such individuals or family members on the basis of predictive genetic information concerning such individuals or family members.

Requires health plans to prohibit health insurance issuers from using predictive genetic information in setting premium rates for individuals on the basis of predictive genetic information concerning such individuals or family members.

Victims of Abuse Access to Health Insurance Act - Prohibits an insurer from engaging in a practice that has the effect of denying, canceling, or limiting health insurance coverage or health benefits, or establishing, increasing, or varying the premium charged for coverage or benefits to: (1) an individual on the basis that the individual is, has been, or may be the victim of domestic violence; or (2) to or for a group or employer on the basis that the group includes or the employer employs, or provides or subsidizes insurance for, an individual described in clause (1).

Prohibits a health benefit plan from considering a condition or injury that occurred as a result of domestic violence as a pre-existing condition.

Prohibits a health benefit plan from considering a condition or injury that occurred prior to the first date of coverage (without regard to any waiting period).

Authorizes an aggrieved individual to commence a civil action for specified relief.

Authorizes the court to award appropriate relief, including temporary, preliminary, or permanent injunctive relief and compensatory and punitive damages, as well as the costs of suit and reasonable fees for plaintiffs attorneys and expert witnesses.

Army Arsenal Strategic Workload Enhancement Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Defense (DOD) to develop and promulgate measurable and enforceable guidelines for DOD, defense agencies, and the military services to have supplies, components, end items, parts, assemblies, and sub-assemblies made in factories or arsenals owned by the United States to the extent those factories or arsenals can make those supplies, components, end items, parts, assemblies, and sub-assemblies on an economical basis while preserving the ability to provide an effective and timely response to mobilization, national defense contingency situations, and other emergency requirements.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to assign government-owned and government-operated Department of the Army factories and arsenals sufficient workload to ensure cost efficiency and technical competence in peacetime, while preserving the ability to provide an effective and timely response to mobilizations, national defense contingency situations, and other emergency requirements.

Directs the Comptroller General to review each report required for completeness and compliance and provide findings and recommendations to the congressional defense committees not later than 60 days after the report is submitted to Congress.

Janey Ensminger Act of 2016 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry to periodically review the scientific literature relevant to the relationship between the employment or residence of individuals at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, for not fewer than 30 days after August 1, 1953, and December 21, 1987, and specific illnesses or conditions incurred by those individuals. The agency must determine, for each illness or condition, that there is evidence that exposure to a toxic substance at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, during the period specified in the review may be a cause of the illness or condition. The agency must categorize the evidence of the connection of the illness or condition to: (1) sufficient or modest to conclude that the exposure is a cause of the illness or condition; (2) moderate to conclude that the exposure is a cause; or (3) no more than limited supporting causation. The agency must publish a list of each illness or condition, including the categorization of the evidence of causal connection. The bill amends the Federal criminal code to provide that the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) shall transfer $2 million to the Chief Business Office and Financial

Veterans Equal Treatment Act - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to develop a new formula for the allocation of Department of Veterans Affairs medical care funds to the national service regions, known as Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISNs), of the Department. Requires the Secretary to take specified requirements into account in developing such formula.Authorizes appropriations for FY 2004, and for medical care for the Department of Veterans Affairs.

Safe and Affordable Drugs from Canada Act of 2015 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to promulgate regulations permitting individuals to safely import into the United States a prescription drug purchased from an approved Canadian pharmacy that is dispensed by a pharmacist licensed in Canada.  The FDA must publish on the FDA's website a list of approved Canadian pharmacies from which individuals may purchase prescription drugs.

Off-Reservation Land Acquisition Guidance Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to evaluate: (1) the benefits to the Indian tribe associated with taking a parcel of off-reservation land into trust for the benefit of an Indian tribe; and (2) any concerns raised by applicable state and local governments relating to the acquisition of the off-reservation land.

Requires the Secretary to prepare a report that includes an assessment of: (1) the impacts of taking such land into trust on the on-reservation unemployment rate, reservation life and tribal membership if the members, dependents, and descendants of the Indian tribe relocate to the land or adjacent communities, (2) the specific benefits of taking such land into trust, including an assessment of whether on-reservation jobs will be created and, if so, the quantity of jobs expected to be created; and (3) whether the tribal government can efficiently exercise its governmental and regulatory responsibilities of the tribal government if a gaming facility is constructed on the land.

Prohibits the Secretary from approving any application for taking off-reservation land into trust that is pending on the date of enactment of this Act until the Secretary promulgates regulations to carry out this Act.

Save Our Seas Act of 2017 or the SOS Act of 2017 This bill amends the Marine Debris Act to require the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to work with other federal agencies to develop outreach and education strategies to address both land- and sea-based sources of marine debris.  The bill also requires the Administrator of NOAA, acting at the discretion of the governor of a state, to determine whether there is a severe marine debris event. If NOAA makes such a determination that there is a severe marine debris event, it is authorized to make sums available to be used by the state or NOAA in cooperation with the state: (1) to assist in the cleanup and response required by the severe marine debris event; or (2) other activity as the Administrator determines is appropriate in response to the severe marine debris event.  The bill expresses the sense of Congress that the President should: (1) support federal funding for research and development of alternatives to materials that reduce municipal solid waste and its consequences in the ocean, (2) work with foreign countries that contribute the most to the global marine debris problem, and (3) encourage the United States Trade Representative to consider the impact of marine debris in relevant trade agreements. Great Lakes Federal Effectiveness Act - Establishes the Great Lakes Research Council to: (1) advise and promote coordination of federal research activities to avoid unnecessary duplication and ensure greater effectiveness in achieving ecosystem protection of the Great Lakes through the goals of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement; (2) prepare a document which includes an assessment of the research activities needed to fulfill the Agreement goals; (3) identify topics for and participate in meetings, workshops, symposia, and conferences on such issues; (4) make recommendations for the uniform collection of data for enhancing research and management protocols relating to the Great Lakes ecosystem; (5) advise and cooperate in the establishment of a multi-media data base for the ecosystem; and (6) ensure that the results, findings, and information regarding such research programs are disseminated in a timely manner and in useful forms to interested persons, using as much as possible existing mechanisms.

Requires the Council to: (1) be comprised of one research manager with extensive knowledge, scientific expertise, and experience in the Great Lakes ecosystem for each of the following agencies: (1) the Environmental Protection Agency; (2) the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; (3) the U.S. Coast Guard; (4) the U.S. Fish and

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax deduction for contributions to candidates for public office.  Limits such deduction to $100 for a joint return.  Allows such deduction, with respect to any political contribution, only if the contribution is verified in the manner prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury.

Cuba Sanctions Reform Act of 2004 - Terminates immediately one year of the restrictions on trade and other relations with Cuba, including the embargo on certain sugar imports, and authorizes joint resolutions of the two Houses of Congress approving such renewal.

Authorizes the President to impose export controls with respect to Cuba, and exercise the President's authority under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act with respect to Cuba pursuant to a declaration of national emergency, if made on account of an unusual and extraordinary threat to U.S. national security, foreign policy, or economy.

Subjects to expiration and renewal the travel restrictions related to Cuba by U.S. citizens or residents and transactions incident to travel.
Magistrate Judge Improvement Act of 2000 - Amends the Federal judicial code to grant the U.S. magistrate judge the power to exercise contempt authority.

Community Investment and Empowerment Act - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to direct the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to make competitive grants to communities for: (1) the creation of a grant and/or revolving loan fund program that helps develop financing packages for Class 1 commercial investment; (2) lowering real estate property tax rates; (3) conducting community-wide market analysis to help recruit and/or retain Class 1 commercial investment; (4) creating employment training programs for Class 1 business customer service, sales, and managerial positions; (5) program allowances for activities such as the publication of marketing materials, development of economic development web pages, and educational outreach activities with retail trade associations; and (6) hiring business recruitment specialists.

Prohibits the Administrator from making a grant unless the community agrees that, with respect to the costs to be incurred by the community in carrying out the activities for which the grant is awarded, the community will make available non-Federal contributions equal to at least ten percent of the federal funds provided under the grant. Limits the non-federal contribution to at least 10% of the grant funds.

Allocates grant funds based on a formula that takes into account specified factors

This bill requires the Department of Commerce to assess the U.S. economy to determine what goods the United States currently produces, where such goods are produced, in which manufacturing sector the United States is most competitive, and what policies are necessary to maintain or increase the competitiveness of U.S. manufacturing in the global economy.  The bill requires the Department to develop a comprehensive national manufacturing strategy.  The strategy must: (1) increase the aggregate number of manufacturing jobs in the United States; (2) identify emerging technologies to strengthen the competitiveness of the U.S. global marketplace; (3) strengthen manufacturing sectors in which the United States is most competitive; and (4) strengthen manufacturing sectors in which the United States is most competitive.  The bill requires the Department to: (1) conduct a survey of all Federal agencies that provide support to U.S. manufacturers, including the Department of Commerce, the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, the Department of Labor, the Department of the Treasury, the Small Business Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of the United States Trade Representative, and other Federal agencies; and (2) hold at least two public hearings on the survey recommendations. Local Farm Vehicle Flexibility Act - Amends Federal transportation law to prohibit the Secretary of Transportation from terminating, reducing, limiting, or otherwise interfering with the amount or timing of certain State grants under the National Highway System (NHS) for a covered farm vehicle or the driver of such vehicle that is less stringent than the requirements for commercial motor vehicles and drivers established under the title 49, Code of Federal Regulations pertaining to controlled substances and alcohol use and testing, commercial driver's licensing, driver qualifications, medical certifications, driving and operating commercial vehicles, parts and accessories for the safe operation of commercial vehicles, the maximum hours of service of drivers, vehicle inspection repair and maintenance, employee safety and health standards, and recordkeeping related to compliance with such standards.

True Understanding of the Economy and Safety Act or the TRUE Safety Act - Directs the Comptroller General to assess the methodology followed in carrying out the efficacy of the restart rule published on December 27, 2011, by the Department of Transportation (DOT) to determine whether the data collected is representative of the drivers subject to the restart rule and the methodology is statistically valid. Directs the Comptroller General to assess the Regulatory Impact Analysis (GAO) accompanying the final rule published on December 27, 2011, regarding the validity and representativeness of the driver data used to evaluate the operational and economic impacts of the new 34-hour restart rule applicable to operators of commercial motor vehicles. Directs the Comptroller General to: (1) conduct an assessment of the methodology and data used in developing the proposed safety and health benefits of the new 34-hour restart rule applicable to operators of commercial motor vehicles; (2) review the safety, health, cost, and operational implications of the restart rule and the potential impact of a greater number of commercial motor vehicles on major roads during the morning commutes as a result of the restart rule; and (3) review the research used in developing and justifying the new restart rule, particularly as it relates

Women's Autoimmune Diseases Research and Prevention Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the Office on Women's Health in the Department of Health and Human Services to expand, intensify, and coordinate research and related activities regarding autoimmune diseases in women.

Requires the Director of the Office on Women's Health to coordinate activities with other similar activities conducted by other national research institutes and agencies of the National Institutes of Health to the extent that such Institutes and agencies have responsibilities that are related to autoimmune diseases in women.

Requires the Director of the Office of Women's Health to conduct or support research to expand the understanding of the causes of, and methods for preventing, autoimmune diseases in women.

Requires the Director of the Office on Women's Health to: (1) determine the prevalence of autoimmune diseases in women, including African American women and other women who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups; (2) develop methods for preventing autoimmune diseases in women; and (3) evaluate diagnostic approaches to evaluating women with suspected autoimmune diseases.

Authorizes appropriations.

Redundant Remapping Reform Act of 2011 - Prohibits the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) from updating or publishing a National Flood Insurance Program rate map during a covered period with respect to an area protected by a levee: (1) for which a community or other party has sought recognition under the National Flood Insurance Act of 1964 or has not issued a Letter of Final Determination (a final determination that the area protected by the levee will be insured), and (2) with respect to which the Administrator has not issued a Letter of Final Determination.

Prohibits the Administrator from updating or publishing a National Flood Insurance Program rate map during a covered period with respect to an area protected by a qualified levee that is being planned, constructed, or rehabilitated, if the scheduled completion date for the planning, construction, or rehabilitation occurs during the covered period.

Requires the Administrator to publish a notice to be used by owners of qualified levees to disclose to persons affected by the qualified levees: (1) information relating to the possible dangers of living in an area affected by the qualified levees without flood insurance coverage; (2) information relating to the availability of flood insurance coverage; and (3) any other

Amends the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 to increase the numbers admitted to the United States and the number of aliens eligible for special immigrant status.

Excludes from numerical limitation as to the number of special immigrant aliens: (1) counting against any numerical limitation, (2) excluding counting against any numerical limitation, and (3) excluding counting against any numerical limitation.

Authorizes the Secretary of Homeland Security to adjust the status of an alien to that of a lawful permanent resident if the alien: (1) was paroled or admitted as a nonimmigrant into the United States; and (2) is otherwise eligible for special immigrant status under the Immigration and Nationality Act.

Provides refugee and humanitarian assistance eligibility for special immigrant aliens.

Extends refugee and humanitarian assistance eligibility for special immigrant aliens to individuals who are: (1) at least age 16; (2) eligible for special immigrant status under the Immigration and Nationality Act; and (3) in the United States for at least 12 months.

Transparency in Energy Production Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of the Interior to make information that describes for all covered operations: (1) the aggregate amount of each fossil fuel, by type and by state, produced under federal leases; and (2) the portion and source of such amount that was released by each of venting, flaring, and fugitive release.  Interior shall: (1) initiate a process to correct any errors in the information provided, and (2) report to Congress on efforts to decrease greenhouse gas emissions from covered operations and on plans for reducing such emissions.

Authorizes the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate to award a single gold medal to honor the soldiers from the U.S. prisoners of war who were captured and imprisoned in Bataan, Philippines, during World War II.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the Smithsonian Institution should make the gold medal received available for display at other locations, particularly locations associated with those who fought in defense of Bataan/Corregidor/Luzon and the prisoners of war who were held in the open, exposed to the elements with little or no water.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to strike bronze duplicates of the gold medal.

Authorizes appropriations.

Government Shutdown Accountability and Economic Report Act of 2017 This bill requires the payroll administrator of each House of Congress to exclude from the payments otherwise required to be made for compensation of each Member of Congress serving in that chamber an amount equal to the product of one day's worth of pay under the annual rate of pay applicable to the Member under the Legislative Reorganization Act of 1946 and the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown is in effect.  If a government shutdown occurs, the payroll administrator shall release any remaining amounts in escrow for Members of Congress to deposit in an escrow account.  The bill defines a "government shutdown" as one in which the government is unable to meet its obligations under the fiscal year appropriations law.

Small Business Banking Regulatory Relief Act of 1999 - Amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act to authorize depository institutions to permit the owner of any deposit or account to make up to 24 transfers per month to another account of the owner in the same institution. 
Amends the Federal Reserve Act to authorize the Federal Reserve Board to waive the requirement that a depository institution maintain a reserve ratio of at least 100 percent for securities held by a depository institution in its possession. 
Amends the Federal Reserve Act to permit the payment of interest on any reserve at a Federal reserve bank.

Border Security and Elimination of Sanctuary for Illegal Aliens Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to increase incentives to recruit individuals to become such agents by offering them repayment of higher education loans, not to exceed $6,000 per year, and a maximum of $40,000.

Authorizes the Secretary to deploy newly-developed and cutting-edge technologies to secure the international land and maritime borders of the United States.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) make a priority the construction of the border fencing required under the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996; and (2) report to Congress on the progress and expected completion date of such construction.

Requires the head of an alien who is unlawfully present in the United States to be immediately detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and presented before an immigration judge, with the alien's name and fingerprints added to an appropriate watch list, to be ordered removed without further hearing or review in the same manner as an alien subject to immediate removal is subject to removal under the Immigration and Nationality Act.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make permanent the criminal penalties for unlawful presence in the United States for an alien who

Drug-Induced Rape Prevention and Punishment Act of 1996 - Amends the Controlled Substances Act to impose penalties for distribution of a controlled substance with intent to commit a crime of violence of up to 20 years' imprisonment, a fine, or both. 
Amends the Controlled Substances Act to impose penalties for unlawful possession of flunitrazepam (defined as exceeding 1 gram).  Imposes a fine and/or prison term of up to three years. 
Directs the Administrator of the Drug Enforcement Administration to study and report to specified congressional committees on the appropriateness and desirability of rescheduling flunitrazepam as a Schedule I controlled substance under the Controlled Substances Act. 
Authorizes the Attorney General to:  (1) create educational materials regarding the use of controlled substances in the furtherance of rape and sexual assaults; and (2) disseminate those materials to police departments through the United States.

Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Amendments of 1993 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to increase the enforcement powers of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). 
Authorizes the Commission to request the head of an agency, department, or unit to appear before it to explain the reasons for the agency's failure to submit a plan to the Commission.  Directs the Commission to order the agency head or any officer or employee of such agency to submit the plan before the end of such period as determined to be reasonable. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) enforcement of compliance orders; (2) civil actions relating to subpoena and witness production; and (3) congressional intent with respect to content of affirmative action plans.

Chacoan Outliers Protection Act of 1993 - Amends the Chacoan Outliers Protection Act to designate certain outlying areas of the Chacoan Indian Reservation in New Mexico as Chaco Culture Archeological Protection Sites. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to assist the Navajo Nation in the protection and management of such Sites through a grant, contract, or cooperative agreement.
