(Sec. 1) This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to convey to the Tanana Tribal Council in Tanana, Alaska, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to certain property in the village of Tanana, including the village's entire land, improvements, and appurtenances, including certain land and improvements in the Bristol Bay Recording District in the village of Seward Meridian, in connection with health and social services programs.  The bill declares that the Council shall not be liable for soil, surface water, groundwater, or other contamination resulting from the disposal, release, or presence of environmental contamination on any portion of the property on or before the date on which the property is conveyed to the Council.  The bill also directs HHS to convey to the Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation in Dillingham, Alaska, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to certain property in the corporation's dental annex in the corporation's Seward Meridian office building.

Dental and Optometric Care Access Act or the DOC Access Act This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require a group health plan or individual or health insurance coverage to provide certain optometric and dental services to a person enrolled in the plan or coverage. The plan or coverage must also provide that the doctor may charge the enrollee for the services.

Earmark Transparency Act of 2010 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to direct the Clerk of the House of Representatives and the Secretary of the Senate to jointly establish a searchable website, available to the public at no cost, listing all Senate and House requests for congressionally directed spending items.

Requires the website to be comprised of a database including: (1) the fiscal year in which the item would be funded; (2) the number of the bill or joint resolution for which the request is made, if available; (3) the amount of the initial request made by the Congress; (4) the amount approved by the House and Senate committees as passed by the President, as well as any amendments or changes in the final dollar amount; and (5) the name and address of the intended recipient.

Requires the website to allow the public to: (1) search, sort, and download all information in the database in a machine-readable format; (2) ascertain through a single search, by individual Member of Congress, the total number and dollar value of congressionally directed spending items requested by that Member and the total number and dollar value of such items contained in bills or joint resolutions as passed by either

Less Imprecision in Species Treatment Act of 2018 or the LIST Act of 2018 This bill amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to require the Department of the Interior, within 90 days after receiving or producing certain information regarding a species included in a list published under the Act, to find whether the inclusion of the species in the list was less likely to have occurred if the information was: (1) accurate beyond scientifically reasonable margins of error; (2) fraudulent; or (3) misrepresentative.  Interior must, within 90 days after receiving or producing such information, find whether the inclusion of the species in the list was less likely if the information was: (1) determined on the basis of scientific or commercial information available to, or received or produced by, Interior; or (2) inaccurate beyond scientifically reasonable margins of error, fraudulent, or misrepresentative.  Interior must, within 90 days after finding that a person submitted a petition that is the subject of a positive finding, remove any species for which a positive finding is made.  Interior must publish in the Federal Register notice of any finding that includes the information received or produced by the Department.  Any positive finding by Interior shall not be

Authorizes advanced training in the United States National's or citizen of the United States, if he is a citizen but not a U.S. national, to become a U.S. citizen before beginning advanced training and to file an application for naturalization within 60 days after the later of: (1) the date that he meets the requirements for naturalization in the Immigration and Nationality Act; or (2) the date that he is accepted into advanced training. 
Authorizes the use of the Army Reserve and Army National Guard for financial assistance as members of the Senior Reserve Officers' Training Corps.

Veterans' Housing Benefits Enhancement Act of 2007 - Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to furnish veterans' housing assistance, including hospital rooms and other appropriate accommodations, for permanent disability in the line of duty in the active military, naval, or air service.

Directs the Secretary to report to the congressional veterans committees on the advisability of providing such assistance to veterans and members of the Armed Forces who reside with family members on a permanent basis.

Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals Reorganization Act of 2000 - Divides the current U.S. Court of Appeals for the ninth circuit into the following two circuits: (1) the ninth circuit composed of Arizona, California, Nevada, consisting of the 20-seat ninth circuit judges, and holding regular sessions in San Francisco and Los Angeles; and (2) the twelfth circuit composed of Alaska, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Northern Mariana Islands, Oregon, and Washington, consisting of the 8-seat circuit judges, and holding regular sessions in Portland and Seattle.

Main Street Revolving Loan Fund Program - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to establish the Main Street Revolving Loan Fund Program to provide temporary loans to businesses that meet the size requirement of $1 million or less. Establishes in the Treasury a revolving loan fund for such program.

Requires the Secretary to deposit amounts received as payment on such loans into the fund.

Makes such loans available for use to finance the cost of operations, including: (1) purchasing and operating equipment; (2) paying salaries, wages, and building expenses; and (3) purchasing inventory or making improvements to enhance productivity.

Prohibits such loans from being used to significantly expand operations.

Requires the Secretary to make such loans available for a period not to exceed nine months.

Authorizes the use of such loans for administrative costs in any fiscal year to carry out the program.

Dairy Promotion Equity Act - Amends the Dairy Production Stabilization Act of 1983 to require that the first through ninth sentences of the Act's program on dairy product promotion be: (1) dairy products that are imported into the United States; and (2) imported dairy products that are imported into the United States.

Requires the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to consider whether the Board should consider a referendum to determine whether producers favor suspension of the application of the amendments made by the Act.

Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to conduct a referendum to determine whether producers favor suspension of the application of the amendments.

Balanced Trade Act of 2006 - Amends the Trade Act of 1974 to require the President, whenever there is a U.S. current account deficit that exceeds two percent of the gross domestic product (GDP), to determine that fundamental international payments problems exist that require special import measures to restrict imports.

Requires the President to declare, for such period, a temporary import surcharge in the form of duties (in addition to those already imposed, if any) on imported articles.

Provides for an additional ten-percent surcharge in the case of a U.S. current account deficit that does not exceed one percent of the gross domestic product.

Iran Intelligence Oversight Act - Directs the Director of National Intelligence (DNI) to submit to Congress an updated National Intelligence Estimate on Iran. Requires such estimate to address: (1) Iran's foreign policy and regime objectives; (2) Iran's nuclear programs and capabilities; (3) Iran's military and defense capabilities; (4) Iran's relationship with terrorist organizations and the use of terrorist organizations in furtherance of Iranian foreign policy objectives; (5) Iran's support for international community's potential course of action with respect to Iran; and (6) Iran's anticipated reaction to such actions.

Directs the President to report to Congress on: (1) the objectives of U.S. policy on Iran; (2) the strategy for achieving such objectives; (3) the strategy for achieving Iran's objectives; (4) the level of popular and elite support within Iran for the Iran regime and for its civil nuclear program, nuclear weapons ambitions, and other policies; and (5) the prospects for reform and political change within Iran.

Directs the DNI to report to Congress on the process for vetting and clearing statements of Administration officials drawn from or rely upon intelligence.

Financial Accounting for Intangibles Reexamination (FAIR) Act - Expresses the sense of the Congress that, prior to changing existing rules of accounting for business combinations and intangible assets, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FSBA) should undertake a comprehensive reexamination of the appropriate methods of accounting for purchased and internally generated intangibles including goodwill, and should await the results of related studies of these issues.

Establishes the Commission on Financial Accounting for Intangibles (Commission).

Directs the Commission to: (1) consider the general usefulness of financial statements prepared under generally accepted accounting principles in light of recent trends in the securities markets; (2) consider the impact that shortcomings in generally accepted accounting principles have on securities market volatility, capital allocation, and the investment of retirement fund assets, both individual and institutional; (3) consider the economic impact that would result if the method of accounting for business combinations were eliminated; and (4) consider the economic impact that would result if the method of accounting for business combinations were eliminated.

Terminates the Commission not more than 30 days after submission of such report.

Immigration Backlog Reduction Act of 2011 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to order the removal of an alien arriving in the United States, or who has not been admitted or paroled into the United States, without further hearing or review, unless: (1) the alien has been charged with a crime; (2) the Secretary determines that the alien presents a significant risk to national security; or (3) the alien indicates an intention to apply for asylum.

Directs the Secretary, if an alien (other than an alien described in such Act) who is arriving in the United States, or who has not been admitted or paroled into the United States for the four-year period immediately before the date of the determination of inadmissibility, is inadmissible under the Immigration and Nationality Act, and the alien indicates either an intention to apply for asylum or a credible fear of persecution, to refer the alien for an interview if the officer determines that the alien has been physically present in the United States for less than one year.

Directs the Secretary, if an alien (other than an alien described in such Act) who is arriving in the United States, or who has not been admitted or

Mortgage E-Verify Act of 2010 - Amends the Federal National Mortgage Association Charter Act to prohibit the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) from refinancing, restructuring, or modifying any single-family housing mortgage held by or backed by security issued by the corporation, or from purchasing, or issuing any security backed by, any single-family housing mortgage made for the refinancing, restructuring, or modification of the mortgagor's previous single-family housing mortgage on the same property, unless the identity and work eligibility of the mortgagor under such mortgage has been confirmed by an inquiry under this Act.

Prohibits lenders for single-family housing mortgages and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) from refinancing, restructuring, or modifying any single-family housing mortgage insured by the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or made for the refinancing, restructuring, or modification of the mortgagor's previous single-family housing mortgage on the same property, unless the identity and work eligibility of the mortgagor under such mortgage has been confirmed by an inquiry under this Act.

Prohibits the Secretary from: (1) authorizing or entering into any agreement for the refinancing, restructuring, or modification of any single-family housing mortgage held by

Cure for AIDS Act of 2012 - Requires the Secretary of Defense, acting through the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Program, to establish and support an accelerated research program dedicated to the discovery of a cure for HIV/AIDS.

Directs the Secretary to ensure that research conducted under this Act is highly targeted to address: (1) how HIV persists despite antiretroviral therapy; (2) where HIV persists beyond the reach of antiretroviral therapy; (3) whether ongoing attempts of the immune system to clear the infection actually hinder the ability of the medical community to cure infected individuals; (4) why the immune system reduces but does not eliminate levels of the virus; (5) how to measure ultra-low levels of the virus in the body of an infected individual; (6) identifying and testing interventions, such as drugs, that may eliminate the virus from infected individuals; and (7) identifying and testing interventions, such as vaccines, that may help an infected individual permanently control the virus without antiretroviral therapy.

Requires the Secretary to coordinate with at least one eligible nonprofit entity whose primary mission is ending the AIDS epidemic through innovative research and that has experience carrying out programs dedicated to AIDS cure research to establish research priorities for peer-reviewed funded research

Acid Deposition and Ozone Control Act of 1997 - Amends the Clean Air Act to require the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to add any State to the single ozone transport region that contributed four parts per billion or more to ozone via aerial transport to the ozone level of any noncompliant area in the region for any one of the second through tenth worst ozone days that occurred during the previous 10 years. 
Requires any control measure adopted before enactment of this Act to apply to any State added to such region after enactment of this Act. 
Requires the Administrator to promulgate regulations requiring reductions in the emissions of nitrogen oxide and sulfur dioxide in any State added to such region to one-third of the 1990 levels by the year 2003.  Authorizes the Administrator to establish an allowance trading program to carry out this Act.

This bill amends the STOCK Act to make changes to the effective date of the online access to certain financial disclosure forms for officers and employees of the executive branch and the federal government.  The President, Vice President, Members of Congress, and any officer occupying a position listed in the following sections 3312 or 5313 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) may make public disclosures of their financial disclosure reports and notices of extensions, amendments, and blind trusts with respect to such reports.  Congressional staff must be given the same online access to such reports as executive branch officials.  The bill also amends the Freedom of Information Act to make it out of scope for the public disclosure of certain financial disclosure reports and notices of extensions, amendments, and blind trusts with respect to certain executive branch officers and employees.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a 20-year recovery period for the depreciation of certain systems installed in nonresidential and residential rental buildings.

Financial Institution Customer Protection Act of 2014 - Prohibits a federal banking agency from suggesting, requesting, or ordering a depository institution to terminate a specific customer account unless: (1) the agency has a material reason to do so, and (2) such reason is not based solely on reputation risk. Requires the agency, if a customer poses a threat to national security, to: (1) provide the institution in writing, and (2) accompany such request, order, or termination with a justification.  Prohibits the agency from informing a customer of the justification for the customer's account termination.  Requires each federal banking agency to: (1) report to Congress on the aggregate number of specific customer accounts that it suggested, requested, or ordered a depository institution to terminate during the previous year, and (2) state the legal authority under which it made such suggestions, requests, and orders.  Amends the Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery, and Enforcement Act of 1989 to revise the definition of "depository institution" to include a depository institution and an insured credit union.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make it inadmissible in any immigration-imminent danger proceedings for an alien convicted of an aggravated felony who is present in the United States after the expiration of the period of stay authorized by the Attorney General or who is present in the United States without being admitted or paroled if either the alien has been convicted of committing a felony in the United States or the alien has not resided continuously in the United States for at least seven years immediately preceding the date of initiation of proceedings to remove the alien from the United States.  Makes such an alien inadmissible to the United States if either the alien subsequently has been granted a full and unconditional pardon by the President or by the Governor of any of several States.  Authorizes the waiver of such inadmissibility in certain criminal aliens who have been convicted of committing a felony in the United States or who have not resided continuously in the United States for at least seven years immediately preceding the date of initiation of proceedings to remove the alien from the United States.  Provides for the annulling of the inadmissibility of an alien conviction for criminal aliens who have been found by the Attorney General to be to their for themselves, or to be in the United States for purposes of removal, if either the Attorney General alleges that the

Amends the Federal Reserve Act to revise the Federal Reserve Act by: (1) removing the requirement that a member bank be one-sixth of its subscription to be paid on call; (2) requiring the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to direct a member bank to pay one-twelfth of its subscription in lieu of one-half; and (3) allowing a member bank to elect to pay one-twelfth of its subscription in lieu of one-half.

Requires a member bank with total consolidated assets of $10 billion or less to make such election before the end of the one-year period beginning on the enactment of this Act.

Directs the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to adjust the dollar amounts of total consolidated assets specified under this Act and to reflect the change in the Gross Domestic Product Price Index.

Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve Boundary Adjustment Act of 2004 - Amends the National Parks and Recreation Act of 1978 to revise the boundaries of the Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve in Louisiana.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire any land, water, and interests within the boundary of the Preserve by donation, purchase with funds, transfer from any other federal agency, or exchange.

Requires the Secretary to preserve and protect: (1) fresh water drainage patterns; (2) vegetative cover; (3) the integrity of ecological and biological systems; and (4) water and air quality.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) preserve and protect the preservation of the ecological and biological systems and water and air quality of the Preserve; and (2) protect the integrity of the ecological and biological systems and water and air quality of the Preserve and the preservation of the ecological and biological systems and water and air quality of the park.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) consider any federal land acquired in the areas of the Preserve and the land of the park; and (2) preserve and protect the integrity of the ecological and biological systems and water and air quality of the park and the preservation of the ecological

Authorized Rural Water Projects Completion Act - Establishes the Reclamation Rural Water Construction Fund in the Treasury to be used for the construction of authorized rural water projects. Limits the amount of interest that may be deposited in the Fund and the amount of such interest that may be expended.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to expend from the Fund up to a specified amount for any fiscal year in which the Secretary has completed a feasibility report that recommends the construction of a rural water project.

Terminates the Fund and transfers to the reclamation fund the amounts required to be transferred to it.

Iran Nuclear Nonproliferation Act - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) full diplomatic, political, and economic relations between the United States and Iran cannot be normalized unless and until such safeguards are put in place to prevent weaponization of Iran's nuclear program and the government of Iran ends its support for international terrorist groups, but the attainment of these policy objectives should not constitute preconditions for any diplomatic dialogue; and (2) no congressional authorization for the use of military force in any Act of Congress enacted before the date of the enactment of this Act constitutes, either implicitly or explicitly, an authorization for the use of military force against Iran or its nuclear program.

States that it is U.S. policy not to enter into a preemptive war against Iran in the absence of an imminent threat, and then only in accordance with international law and constitutional and statutory requirements for congressional authorization.

Prohibits the use of appropriated funds to carry out covert actions for the purpose of causing regime change in Iran or to carry out any military action against Iran in the absence of an imminent threat, in accordance with international law and constitutional and statutory requirements for congressional authorization.

Amends the Small Business Act to authorize the Small Business Administration (SBA) to award competitive grants to one or more eligible associations (national or regional entities that represent small businesses participating in SBIR or STTR programs under the Small Business Administration Act) for use in accordance with the SBA technical assistance program to small businesses located in low participation areas in order to: (1) advise and guide such businesses through the SBIR and STTR processes from application to award and successful completion of each phase of the program; and (2) reimburse qualified mentoring organizations participating in the program for necessary expenses and travel expenses for employees providing services away from their homes or regular places of business for individuals serving without pay.

The bill also amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to provide that, if a state's initial designation is not extended, the initial designation shall terminate when the state's initial designation is extended.

Military Call-Up Relief Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to waive early withdrawal penalty for distributions from qualified retirement plans to individuals called to active duty during the national emergency declared by the President on September 14, 2001.

State Veterans Home Nurse Recruitment Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make payments to States for assisting States in the hiring and retention of nurses and the reduction of nursing shortages at such States' homes.

Defines "computer hardware" to include disk drives, integrated circuits, display screens, cables, modems, speakers, and printers.

Residential and Commuter Toll Fairness Act of 2009 - Authorizes states, counties, municipalities, and multi-jurisdictional transportation authorities that operate or manage transportation systems to establish programs that offer discounted transportation tolls, user fees, or other fares for residents of specific geographic areas in order to reduce or alleviate toll burdens imposed upon such residents.

Authorizes states, counties, municipalities, and multi-jurisdictional transportation authorities to enact such rules or regulations necessary to establish such programs.

Taxpayer's Right to View Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit cable operators from assessing or collecting separate charges for any video programming of a sporting, theatrical, or other entertainment event if it is performed at a facility constructed, renovated, or maintained with tax revenues or by an organization that receives public financial support. 
Authorizes the Federal Communications Commission and local franchising authorities to make determinations concerning the applicability of this prohibition.

Consumer Learning through Electronically-Accessible and Reasonable Cost Information Act of 2013 or the CLEAR Cost Information Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a Medicare beneficiary's annual report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) on the percentage of total hospital care furnished by hospitals to be included on the beneficiary's Medicare home Internet website. Requires the Secretary to post such data on a publicly accessible and searchable website that: (1) allows for meaningful comparisons of the data by zip code, and (2) is readily understandable by a typical consumer. Requires the inclusion of a link on the beneficiary's home Internet website to the data posted on the website. Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require the Secretary to post the data contained in the Medicare payment advisory commission's annual report on the percentage that charity care makes up of the total care furnished by hospitals and critical access hospitals.

Communities Committed to College Tax Credit Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 50% of contributions made to a qualified scholarship funding trust (i.e., a trust established and maintained by an organization that is part of a local education agency [LEA] and that is organized to provide scholarships to children of LEA agencies). Limits the amount of such credit to $200 million.

Clinical Trials Modernization Act of 2015 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to establish and implement a framework through which: (1) sponsors of drugs, biological products, or devices may submit to the FDA a proposal for the incorporation of adaptive trial designs, Bayesian methods, or other alternative statistical methods into proposed clinical protocols and marketing applications; and (2) the FDA will commit to review and provide feedback on such proposals. The FDA must update and finalize the draft guidance on the use of adaptive trial design and Bayesian methods for drugs and biological products. The FDA must also establish a process for the review and revision of the guidance. The bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the FDA to establish a process for the evaluation of required postapproval studies and clinical trials.

Medicare Home Health Equity Act of 1998 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise the formula for payment to home health agencies for cost and related services. 
Directs the Director of the Congressional Budget Office to certify annual excess amounts to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for the interim payment system for home health services.

Ensuring the Taxpayer a Fair Return for Federal Offshore Oil and Gas Resources Act of 2015  This bill amends the Mineral Leasing Act to increase the minimum bid per acre for oil and gas and tar sands leases to reflect inflation.  The bill also increases the annual rentals for oil and gas and tar sands leases by an additional 18.75%.  The bill also amends the Royalty Rates Act to revise royalty rates for oil and gas and tar sands leases.  The bill also amends the Mineral Leasing Act to extend the royalty sharing authority for oil and gas leases in Alaska.

Kake Tribal Corporation Land Exchange Act - Amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior to convey specified Federal land to the corporation, Kake Tribal Corporation, for the development of a municipal watershed area.

Caring Family Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an exemption from the tax on personal income for each family member of the taxpayer who has attained age 60 and is unable to perform at least two activities of daily living due to a loss of functional capacity.

Serving Everyone with Reliable, Vital Internet, Communications, and Education Act of 2007 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to revise the purposes of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to require the FCC to: (1) continue the Lifeline Assistance Program and the Link Up Program, respectively, to provide universal service; and (2) expand such programs by allowing low-income consumers participating in such programs to choose to use such assistance for any one of the following: (1) wire or wireless telephone service; (2) Internet access service; (3) wire or wireless broadband service; or (4) any evolving technology the FCC deems consistent with such purposes.

Requires the FCC to study and report to Congress on: (1) the benefit level for a household participating in the Lifeline Assistance Program which will encourage low-income consumers to seek broadband service; and (2) projections on the potential of new broadband service consumers who would seek such service if economically accessible.

Business Relief and Incentives for Small Entrepreneurs Act of 2007 or the Business RAISE Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a 15-year straight-line depreciation allowance for certain restaurant improvements. Defines "qualified retail improvement property" as any nonresidential real property that is: (1) open to the general public and used in the trade or business of selling tangible personal property or services to the general public; and (2) placed in service more than three years after the date the building was first placed in service.

Requires the Secretary of Labor to publicize the expanded work opportunity tax credit for disabled veterans.

Allows such credit for employees who are employed on average at least 40 hours per week.

National Parks Capital Improvements Act of 1996 - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into a memorandum of agreement with an entity to act as an authorized fund raising organization for the benefit of the Grand Canyon National Park and any other national park designated by the Secretary that has an approved general management plan with capital needs in excess of $5 million. 
Authorizes the Secretary to authorize the Superintendent of the Park to charge and collect a surcharge of not to exceed two dollars per person for entrance fees to the Park.  Requires such surcharge to be used by the organization to amortize the bond issue, provide for the reasonable costs of administration, and maintain a sufficient reserve consistent with industry standards. 
Authorizes the Secretary to use bond proceeds for a park facility project.  Prohibits the use of any part of such proceeds (other than interest as provided in this Act) to defray administrative expenses.  Requires such project to be consistent with the laws governing the National Park System, the Park, and the general management plan for the Park.

Secure Online Communication Enforcement Act of 2000 - Amends the Federal criminal code to authorize a governmental entity to require a provider of remote computing service to disclose the contents of any electronic communication to which such service is made applicable by this Act. Strengthening Homeland Security, Intelligence, and Essential Law Enforcement Departments Act of 2011 or SHIELD Act of 2011 - Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to make payments on obligations incurred by the U.S. government to the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard for active-duty personnel who perform active service during the period of lapsed appropriations.

District of Columbia Land Use Notification Act of 1993 - Amends the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 to prohibit the Administrator of the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office from carrying out any activity that affects real property located in the District of Columbia unless:  (1) the Administrator provides a notice describing such activity and the property affected to the Mayor of the District of Columbia, the Chair of the Council of the District of Columbia, and the Chair of the Advisory Neighborhood Commission in whose neighborhood such property is located; and (2) the Administrator provides the individuals described in clause 1 with the opportunity to present oral or written comments on the activity before the Administrator carries it out.  Authorizes the Administrator to waive such requirements if the Administrator finds that compliance with such requirements would jeopardize the public safety or the national security interests of the United States, but only if the Administrator:  (1) certifies such finding and the reasons for such finding to the individuals and to Congress; and (2) provides such individuals with notice of such requirements and the opportunity to present comments.

Security Enhancement and Jobs Act of 2011 - Amends the Transportation Security Act of 1996 to direct the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to approve or deny an application for the screening of passengers and property at an airport if the Secretary determines that the airport operator: (1) has not been granted security screening services approval for a certain time period, and (2) has not been granted security screening approval for a certain period.

Alaska Natural Gas Pipeline Improvement Act of 2011 - Amends the Alaska Natural Gas Pipeline Act of 2004 to revise the definition of "Alaska natural gas transportation project" to include any pipeline system that is authorized under the Alaska Natural Gas Transportation Act of 1976 or the Natural Gas Act.

Defines "Alaska natural gas transportation project" as any pipeline segment that the Commission finds could feasibly be incorporated into and serve as an integrated segment of the natural gas transportation system.

Preventing Illegal Radio Abuse Through Enforcement Act or the PIRAATE Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Communications Act of 1934 to impose a fine and/or prison term of up to $2 million for willfully and knowingly causing or causing or suffering to be done any pirate radio broadcasting. The FCC must annually report to Congress on the implementation of this bill and associated enforcement activities.  The bill prohibits the FCC from preempting state or local law prohibiting pirate radio broadcasting. Skills Connection Act - Directs the Secretary of Labor to create a publicly available, easily navigable, and searchable database containing: (1) a registry of credentials for purposes of enabling programs that lead to such a credential to receive priority; (2) a skills database, for purposes of enabling such a credential to receive priority; (3) a jobs bank; and (4) information relating to skills and credentials required for employment in the manufacturing sector, as determined by the Secretary by using Manufacturing Institute-Endorsed Manufacturing Skills Certification System or similar resource or by consulting with an organization similar to the Manufacturing Institute.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) list the credential in the registry if the credential is required by federal or state law for an occupation; (2) list the credential and an updated credential, if the credential involved is an industry-recognized, nationally portable credential that is consistent with the Secretary's established industry competency models and is consistently updated through third party validation to reflect changing industry competencies; and (3) provide an assessment of which skills listed in the skills database aligned with or are related to the requirements of the credential.

Supporting America's Protective Security Advisor Act of 2007 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to include within the Protective Security Coordination Division of the Office of Infrastructure Protection in the Department of Homeland Security a Protective Security Advisor Program Office within the Office.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to develop a plan for the assignment and distribution of protective security advisors that takes into account baseline requirements and anticipated growth after the enactment of this Act.

Requires the plan to: (1) ensure that protective security advisors are located across the United States to ensure appropriate coverage and coordinated support, with an emphasis on high-risk regions; and (2) assign advisors and support staff based on risk, including consideration of assigning additional advisors in areas of greater population density and concentration of critical infrastructure and key resources.

Requires the Secretary to submit to Congress a report outlining and justifying the plan.

Civil Rights Commission Act of 1998 - Amends the Civil Rights Commission Act of 1983 to extend and authorize appropriations for FY 2001 for the Civil Rights Commission (Commission).

Workers' Political Rights Act - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to exclude labor organizations from the political committee and campaign committee rules governing contributions and expenditures.

Telecommunications Trust Act of 1998 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to establish in the Treasury the Telecommunications Trust Fund to provide for Federal universal service support.  Authorizes appropriations. 
Establishes the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) in the Telecommunications Trust Fund.  Requires amounts in the Fund to be available only to provide for Federal universal service support mechanisms pursuant to the Communications Act of 1934.

This bill requires the Department of Education to pay Fort Lewis College in Colorado a tuition charge for Indian students who are not residents of Colorado. The amount of such payment may not exceed the amount equal to the charges for tuition for all Indian students who were not residents of Colorado and who were enrolled in Fort Lewis College for the academic year ending before the beginning of such fiscal year.

Rebuilding Equity Act of 2013 - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to establish a voluntary program for refinancing into fully amortizing 20-year term loans to borrowers who qualify for the Home Affordable Refinance Program carried out by the enterprises. Rural Broadband Access Enhancement Act - Amends the Rural Electrification Act of 1936 to revise the eligibility requirements for certain rural broadband access grants.

Prohibits the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) from approving an application for a loan or loan guarantee for a new broadband service to an eligible rural community in which at least 40 percent of the population does not have access to broadband service, unless the value of the assets of the applicant not pledged or hypothecated for any other purpose equals at least 10 percent of the principal amount of the loan which is the subject of the application.

Requires the Secretary to reduce the paperwork required of applicants.

Prohibits the Secretary from approving an application for a loan or loan guarantee for a new broadband service in a community with at least three service providers.

Eliminates the limitation on the amount of funds that may be used to provide loans or loan guarantees to entities with various shares of installed telephone subscriber lines.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on the status of the program.

Security Clearance Family Review Act This bill prohibits the granting of security clearance to a relative of the President if such relative has a commercial relationship with a state-owned or privately owned foreign financial institution.

This bill designates the Gateway Arch and the Old St. Louis Courthouse as National Historic Landmarks and the grounds surrounding the Gateway Arch and the Old St. Louis Courthouse as for inclusion on the National Register of Historic Places.

Department of Defense Office of the Victim Advocate Act of 2004 - Establishes in the Office of the Secretary of Defense a Director with responsibility for coordination of programs and activities relating to victims of interpersonal violence among members of the armed forces or between members and their families and partners.

Requires the Director to: (1) coordinate programs and activities of the military departments relative to care, services, and treatment for victims; (2) serve as headquarters program manager for the victim advocates and the victim service specialists in the Department's authorized by law military and civilian communities; (3) coordinate services for victims among military and civilian communities and provide guidance to victims in obtaining those services; (4) evaluate the prevalence of interpersonal violence associated with members of the armed forces; (5) evaluate the programs established by the military departments providing services to victims of interpersonal violence; (6) evaluate the delivery of services by the military departments to victims; (7) review the facilities of the military departments providing services to victims; (8) review the hotline programs for victims of violence, including command and installation hotlines, the National Domestic Violence Hotline, and the National Sexual Assault Hotline; (9) review disciplinary actions taken against members of the armed forces who commit acts of interpersonal violence;

Amends the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act to repeal the ownership-based criteria for the repatriation of certain cultural items.

Amends the Act to authorize the Federal Government and museums to conduct research on human remains and associated funerary objects for which no lineal descendants have been identified and in cases of all other cultural items.  Requires the Federal agency or museum with custody of the items to make such items available for such study unless the Federal agency or museum has reasonably established that the potential scientific benefit of the study is outweighed by curatorial, cultural, or other reasonable considerations.

Transparency and Accountability of Failed Exchanges Act - Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require a state that is awarded a grant to establish an Exchange and terminates the operation of such Exchange or otherwise transfers the operation of such Exchange to an entity other than the state: (1) within 30 days after the termination or transfer, to report to Congress and the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) on how amounts awarded to such state pursuant to such grant were used; and (2) within 30 days after the termination or transfer, to provide to the HHS Secretary any property acquired by such state with amounts awarded pursuant to such grant and to submit to Congress and the Secretary a record of the provision of such property to the HHS Secretary.

Prescribes requirements for the retention of funds for deficit reduction and for treatment of property.

Authorizes the Administrator of General Services to dispose of property obtained pursuant to such grant through a public auction for cash and for not less than fair market value.

Exempts any disposal of property conducted under such provisions from certain requirements for the conveyance of property under the False Claims Act.

Requires the Attorney General to bring an action before the appropriate U.S. district court to enforce such provisions.

Transnational Criminal Organization Illicit Spotter Prevention and Elimination Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make it a federal crime to knowingly transmit, by any means, to another person the location, movement, or activities of any federal, state, local, or tribal law enforcement agency with intent to further a federal crime relating to immigration, customs, controlled substances, or agriculture, monetary instruments, or other border controls.

Prescribes criminal penalties for: (1) the unlawful destruction, alteration, or damage of federal, state, local, or tribal border fences, sensors, or other physical or electronic devices deployed to control such border or port of entry; and (2) the unlawful construction, excavation, or making of any structure intended to defeat, circumvent, or evade such border or port of entry.

Provides for the bankruptcy of the U.S. immigration, customs, and controlled substance enforcement and administration agencies.

Amends the Interstate Transportation of Dangerous Criminals Act of 2000 to extend the statute of limitations for the criminal prosecution of persons who violate provisions of such Act.

Nye County Higher Education Campus Conveyance Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the Nye County Nevada Higher Education Campus in Pahrump Valley, Nevada, without consideration, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the Federal land for use as a campus for the College.

Conditions the conveyance on the Chancellor agreeing to: (1) pay any administrative costs associated with the conveyance, including the cost of any environmental, wildlife, cultural, or historical resources studies; (2) use the conveyed Federal land for educational and recreational purposes; (3) release and indemnify the United States from claims or liabilities which may arise from uses carried out on the conveyed Federal land by the United States or any person; (4) erect at the College an appropriate and centrally located monument that acknowledges the conveyance of the Federal land by the United States for the purpose of furthering the higher education of citizens in the State; and (5) assist the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) in providing information to the students of the College and the citizens of the State on: (1) public land in the State; and (2) the role of BLM in managing, preserving, and protecting the public land.

Subjects the conveyance to all valid existing rights

Protect Marriage from the Courts Act of 2015 This bill amends the federal judicial code to prohibit the Supreme Court and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 4th and 7th Circuits from having jurisdiction to adjudicate or enforce claims pertaining to the validity of a state law, or state administrative or judicial decisions, that: (1) define marriage as limited to the union of one man and one woman; or (2) refuse state recognition of or allow the state to refuse recognition of same-sex marriages performed and licensed in other states.

Fairness for Working Americans Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the refundable tax credit for earnings and earned income for taxpayers in the United States or their U.S. tax-exempt retirement plans. Includes as earned income any amount excluded from gross income by reason of the section 112 of the Internal Revenue Code. Defines "domestic" as a U.S. corporation or partnership unless the Secretary of the Treasury provides otherwise by regulations. Treats a "corporate expatriation transaction" as a transaction if: (1) a controlling shareholder of the acquiring corporation is a U.S. citizen or lawfully present in the United States; and (2) the acquiring corporation meets certain requirements related to ownership and stock.

Higher Education Savings Plan Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for the tax deduction for the education expenses of a qualified higher education expense distribution (defined as any distribution from a designated higher education expense annuity to the taxpayer if such distribution is used within 90 days of the distribution to pay qualified tuition and related expenses required for the taxpayer's enrollment or attendance at an eligible institution of higher education).

Grants a Federal charter to the National Academy of Inventors, a nonprofit organization that was organized under the laws of Florida and meets the requirements of the charter, if the organization does not comply with such requirements.

Accelerating Kids' Access to Care Act This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require a state Medicaid program to include an eligible out-of-state provider or supplier of medical or other items or services furnished to a child for which payment is available under the state Medicaid program that is located in another state and with respect to which the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) has determined there is a limited risk of fraud, waste, or abuse for purposes of determining the level of Medicaid screening. The requirements of this bill are the following:   an eligible out-of-state provider or supplier that elects to be and is enrolled in the state Medicaid program, and   enrollment in the state Medicaid program for a period of five years before being required to obtain revalidation.   The HHS Secretary shall establish a process for permitting a provider or supplier, as the case may be, to enroll in the Medicaid program under Medicare program title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act, at the same time, at the same time in the state Medicaid program, and for a period of five years before being required to obtain revalidation.

Public Library Innovation Space Act This bill amends the Museum and Library Services Act to authorize the Director of the National Public Library of the National Governors Association to make competitive grants to public libraries to carry out programs that include the development of makerspaces (spaces for the creation of physical goods and the provision of educational opportunities for the use of such goods) at public libraries.

Rural Equity Payment Index Reform Act of 2003 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise the physician work adjustment factors for purposes of the Medicare physician fee schedule.

Campaign Sunlight Act of 2012 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to establish and operate a website, to be known as the Campaign Accountability Site, through which members of the public may view the contents of political advertisements.

Requires the website to: (1) make the contents of a political advertisement available for viewing in the same format through which the advertisement was disseminated, and (2) make the sources of the contents available on the website directly or through hyperlinks to the sources submitted by the sponsor of the advertisement.

Requires the sponsor of a political advertisement to submit the contents of the advertisement to the Commission within 24 hours after it is disseminated, or 72 hours after it is disseminated, in the case of an advertisement that is disseminated during the seven-day period that ends on the date of the election for the office sought by the candidate.

Requires the Commission to pay the sponsor of a political advertisement the amount of any such fee if the Commission determines that it is appropriate to impose fees on the sponsors of political advertisements.

Veterans Justice Outreach Act of 2015 Directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to carry out a program to support veterans in contact with the criminal justice system by discouraging unnecessary criminalization of mental illness and other nonviolent crimes.  Directs the VA to carry out the program in partnership with local law enforcement, judicial, and community-based treatment and legal assistance organizations. Authorizes the VA to conduct specified outreach and assistance for the provision of such support.

Higher Education Family Opportunity Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax deduction for the qualified tuition and related expenses paid or incurred by an individual.  Limits such deduction to the amount equal to the individual's educational expenses.
Grants a Federal charter to the Black Veterans of America (a nonprofit corporation organized under the laws of Minnesota).

Anti-Pyramid Promotional Scheme Act of 2016 This bill prohibits any person from establishing, operating, promoting, or causing a pyramid promotional scheme. A violation of this bill is treated as an unfair or deceptive act or practice in or affecting commerce under the Federal Trade Commission Act. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) shall enforce such prohibition in the same manner, by the same means, and with the same jurisdiction, powers, and duties as though all applicable terms and provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act (FTCA) were incorporated into and made a part of this bill.  As used in this bill, "appropriate inventory purchase agreement" means a program by which a plan or operation repurchases, upon request at the termination of a participant's business relationship with the plan or operation and based upon commercially reasonable terms, current and marketable inventory purchased and maintained by the participant for resale, use, or consumption, and such plan or operation in its recruiting literature, sales manual, and contracts with participants, including the manner in which the repurchase is exercised, and disclosure of any inventory that is not eligible for repurchase. Medical Savings Account Availability Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) repeal the limitations on the availability of tax-exempt medical savings accounts; (2) increase the amount of such accounts available to employees and to the tax deduction for contributions to such accounts; (3) allow employers and employees to contribute to such accounts; (4) allow tax-free medical savings accounts for employer contributions; and (5) allow tax-free medical savings accounts for both employers and employees.

International Peacekeeping Reform Act of 1997 - Prohibits the use of funds made available to the Department of State under the account "Contributions for International Peacekeeping Activities" or any other funds made available to the Department under any law to pay for assessed or voluntary contributions to the United Nations (U.N.) to establish, expand, or modify a U.N. peacekeeping operations unless:  (1) the President certifies to the appropriate congressional committees that the operation involves an international conflict in which hostilities have ceased and all significant parties to the conflict agree to the imposition of U.N. peacekeeping forces for the purpose of seeking an enduring solution to the conflict; and (2) the President determines that the U.N. peacekeeping operation meets the requirements of this Act.  Requires the President to certify and determine and certify to the Congress that the U.N. peacekeeping operation meets specified requirements.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for the cost of qualified child disability expenses. Limits the amount of such credit to $3,000, with an annual reduction of $500 for each $1,000 (or fraction thereof) by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000.

Amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to recognize Alexander Creek, Incorporated, as a Native village under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior to negotiate with Alexander Creek to fairly and equitably settle any claims that Alexander Creek has against the United States.

Requires the Secretary to enter into an agreement with Alexander Creek regarding the claims.

Requires Alexander Creek to notify its members of the termination of their benefits from the Region.

Rural Broadband Enhancement Act - Amends the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act to make loans and other extensions of credit to provide funds for the costs of the construction, improvement, and acquisition of facilities and equipment for the provision of broadband service in eligible rural communities.

Requires the Rural Utilities Service of the Department of Agriculture to make such loans or other extensions of credit to eligible entities to provide funds for the construction, improvement, or acquisition of facilities and equipment (including consumer equipment) for the provision of broadband service in eligible rural communities.

Defines "eligible rural community" as any incorporated or unincorporated place that: (1) has not more than 20,000 inhabitants, based on the most recent available population statistics of the Bureau of the Census; and (2) is not located in an area designated as a Metropolitan Area by the Office of Management and Budget.

Prohibits the loan or extension of credit from being made after September 30, 2006.

Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the federal criminal code to include among the military retired pay of members of the Armed Forces with extensive hazardous duty experience: (1) the amount of special pay for hazardous duty received if the member received special pay under the Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS) or the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) for not less than 60 months; and (2) the amount of basic pay if the member received special pay under CSRS or FERS for not less than 60 months.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on: (1) whether members of the National Guard and reserve constitute a disproportionately large portion of the employees of any size or type of business; (2) the amount of federal tax benefit that would be appropriate to compensate such a business for costs associated with employing members of National Guard and reserve units and having such members called to active duty; and (3) whether changes can be made to the small business loan program to assist small businesses to deal with the costs associated with employing members of National Guard and reserve units and having such members called to active duty.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress on the feasibility and desirability of expanding the Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps (JROTC)

Rebuild American Manufacturing Act of 2013 - Directs the President to develop a comprehensive national manufacturing strategy that includes: (1) a survey of all persons with headquarters in the United States that maintain manufacturing facilities outside of the United States to identify categories of products manufactured and the number of jobs in such facilities; (2) a survey of all Federal agencies that provide assistance to U.S. manufacturers, including the Department of Commerce, the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, the Department of Labor, the Department of the Treasury, the Small Business Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of the United States Trade Representative, the National Science Foundation, and such other Federal agencies as the President considers appropriate; (3) a survey of manufacturing goods produced in the United States and where such goods are produced; (4) a survey of U.S. and foreign-based manufacturing and production workers; (5) a survey of the global competitiveness of U.S. manufacturing; and (6) recommendations for achieving the goals of the strategy.

Higher Education Fairness Act of 1997 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to provide that family contribution for dependent students shall be the amount of any tax credit taken by the parents under the Internal Revenue Code. 
Provides for the family contribution from available income for independent students without dependents other than a spouse. 
Provides for the family contribution from available income for independent students with dependents other than a spouse. 
Provides for regulations for the family contribution from available income for independent students. 
Provides for updated tables and amounts for income protection allowances for independent students.
Grants a Federal charter to the American Military Retirees Association (a veterans service organization).

National Park Centennial Challenge Fund Act - Establishes in the Treasury the National Park Centennial Challenge Fund to be used to finance signature projects and programs to enhance the National Park System as it approaches its Centennial in 2016 and to prepare the parks for another century of conservation, preservation, and enjoyment.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service (NPS), to develop a list of signature projects and programs eligible for funding from the Challenge Fund.

Authorizes the Secretary, beginning on October 1, 2007, and ending on September 30, 2017, to transfer to the Fund qualified cash donations received by the NPS.

Appropriates in each fiscal year an amount equal to the qualified donations received and the pledge of donations through letters of credit in the same fiscal year, not to exceed $100 million in any one year.

Prohibits the Secretary from obligating any amounts based on a letter of credit, or amounts to match a letter of credit, until amounts from that letter of credit are deposited in the Fund.

Prohibits the Secretary from: (1) obligating any amounts to match a letter of credit, or amounts to match a credit,

Air Traffic Supervisor Retirement Reform Act of 1995 - Amends Federal law to provide for civil service retirement and retirement system benefits for Federal employees who perform a specified number of service years in the Air Transportation Service.

Public Servant Priority Placement Act of 1995 - Amends Federal law to direct the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to establish a Government-wide program and each agency to establish an agency program to facilitate employment placement for Federal employees who:  (1) are scheduled to be separated from service under a reduction in force under regulations prescribed under this Act or procedures established under this Act; or (2) are separated under such a reduction in force. 
Requires each agency program to provide a system to require the offer of a vacant position in an agency to an agency employee of such employee's affected agency to an agency employee of another agency affected by a reduction in force action, if the position cannot be filled within the agency, the employee to whom the offer is made is qualified for the offered position, and the geographic location of the offered position is within the commuting area of the employee's residence or the employee's present or last held position. 
Requires the Government-wide placement program to:  (1) coordinate with other Federal agencies for the placement of agency employees affected by a reduction in force action within such agency; and (2) provide a system to require the offer of a vacant position in an agency to an agency employee of another

Sportsmanship in Hunting Act of 2008 - Amends the federal criminal code to prohibit knowingly transporting, transporting, or possessing a confined exotic animal for the purpose of allowing the killing or injuring of that animal for entertainment or for the collection of a trophy.

Imposes a fine and/or imprisonment of up to one year for such prohibited acts.

Excludes from the definition of "confined exotic animal" any animal that has been held in captivity for the shorter of the majority of the animal's life or a period of one year.

Helping College Students Cross the Finish Line Act This bill amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Department of Education (ED) to award grants to institutions of higher education to establish financial assistance programs for students to complete their degrees and certificates within a reasonable time frame. ED must create and annually report to Congress on the number of students who received financial assistance under the program.
